1.1.m: The Ahirbudhnyasaṃhitā in the holy Pāñcarātra.
The first chapter, named “The Descent of the Teaching”.

1.1.s:
śuklāmbaradharaṃ viṣṇuṃ śaśivarṇaṃ caturbhujam |
prasannavadanaṃ dhyāyet sarvavighnopaśāntaye ||
1.1.d:
शुक्लाम्बरधरं विष्णुं शशिवर्णं चतुर्भुजम् |
प्रसन्नवदनं ध्यायेत् सर्वविघ्नोपशान्तये ||
1.1.m: One should meditate upon Viṣṇu, clad in white garments, possessing the color of the moon, having four arms, / with a serene countenance, for the pacification of all obstacles.

To him who has the form of the triad of syllables, the unmanifest, the transformations, the senses, and the rest, / who is the reality of the transcendent emanation and so forth—homage to the discus, to the bearer of the discus. || 1-1

1.1.s:
somasūryānalākalpāmakalpāminduśekharām |
pañcabinduṃ hareḥ śaktiṃ pañcakṛtyakarīṃ numaḥ || 1-2 ||
1.1.d:
सोमसूर्यानलाकल्पामकल्पामिन्दुशेखराम् |
पञ्चबिन्दुं हरेः शक्तिं पञ्चकृत्यकरीं नुमः || 1-2 ||
1.1.m: We praise Hari's Śakti, adorned with Soma, Sūrya, and Agni, unadorned, having the moon on her crest, / possessing five points, performing the five cosmic functions. || 1-2
Bharadvāja's question to Durvāsas regarding the cause of the greatness of the Sudarśana.

1.1.s:
āplutaṃ divyagaṅgāyāmupāsīnaṃ paraṃ padam |
bharadvājo'tha papraccha durvāsasamakalmaṣam || 1-3 ||
1.1.d:
आप्लुतं दिव्यगङ्गायामुपासीनं परं पदम् |
भरद्वाजोऽथ पप्रच्छ दुर्वाससमकल्मषम् || 1-3 ||
1.1.m: Bathed in the divine Gaṅgā, seated in worship of the highest abode, / Bharadvāja then questioned the sinless Durvāsas: || 1-3

1.1.s:
anasūyāhṛdānanda bhagavaṃstapasāṃ nidhe |
asti me saṃśayaḥ kaścit taṃ me vyākhyā tu marhasi || 1-4 ||
1.1.d:
अनसूयाहृदानन्द भगवंस्तपसां निधे |
अस्ति मे संशयः कश्चित् तं मे व्याख्या तु मर्हसि || 1-4 ||
1.1.m: “O delight of the heart of Anasūyā, O blessed one, treasury of austerities, / I have a certain doubt; please explain it to me. || 1-4
In the Atharvanic determination involving the rites of Agni and Soma, / and in the host of missile weapons of great power, both projecting and withdrawing; || 1-5

1.1.s:
lokapālāstrasaṃghe ca tattatsāmarthyasaṃbhṛte |
mahodayāsu śaktīṣu vahnisūryenduvartmanām || 1-6 ||
1.1.d:
लोकपालास्त्रसंघे च तत्तत्सामर्थ्यसंभृते |
महोदयासु शक्तीषु वह्निसूर्येन्दुवर्त्मनाम् || 1-6 ||
1.1.m: and in the host of missile weapons of the world-guardians, endowed with their respective powers; / in the greatly exalted powers of the paths of fire, sun, and moon; || 1-6
and in the multitude of weapons based on missile weapons, fashioned by Brahmā, Rudra, and others, / skillful in the acts of protection, destruction, and creation of the three worlds; || 1-7

1.1.s:
maharṣigaṇasaṃdṛṣṭe mantragrāme mahodaye |
vaiṣṇave ca gadāśārṅgaśaṅkhakhaḍgādipūrvake || 1-8 ||
1.1.d:
महर्षिगणसंदृष्टे मन्त्रग्रामे महोदये |
वैष्णवे च गदाशार्ङ्गशङ्खखड्गादिपूर्वके || 1-8 ||
1.1.m: in the greatly exalted multitude of mantras seen by the host of great sages; / and in the Vaiṣṇava [weapons], beginning with the mace, the Śārṅga bow, the conch, and the sword; || 1-8

1.1.s:
lākṣme ca dalagaṇḍābjapūrve'straughe mahodaye |
anyatroccāvace'pyevaṃ kīrtyamāne prabhāvataḥ || 1-9 ||
1.1.d:
लाक्ष्मे च दलगण्डाब्जपूर्वेऽस्त्रौघे महोदये |
अन्यत्रोच्चावचेऽप्येवं कीर्त्यमाने प्रभावतः || 1-9 ||
1.1.m: and in the greatly exalted host of missile weapons belonging to Lakṣmī, beginning with the petal, the cheek, and the lotus; / and likewise elsewhere in diverse things, when proclaimed according to their power— || 1-9

1.1.s:
sudarśanāśrayatvaṃ tu tatra tatra nirūpitam |
kiṃkṛtaṃ tasya māhātmyaṃ svataḥ saṃsargato'pi vā || 1-10 ||
1.1.d:
सुदर्शनाश्रयत्वं तु तत्र तत्र निरूपितम् |
किंकृतं तस्य माहात्म्यं स्वतः संसर्गतोऽपि वा || 1-10 ||
1.1.m: their reliance upon Sudarśana is established here and there. / By what is its greatness produced—by itself or through association? || 1-10

1.1.s:
kiṃ tat sudarśanaṃ nāma kaśca śabdārtha iṣyate |
tena kiṃ kriyate karma jagad vyāpnoti tat katham || 1-11 ||
1.1.d:
किं तत् सुदर्शनं नाम कश्च शब्दार्थ इष्यते |
तेन किं क्रियते कर्म जगद् व्याप्नोति तत् कथम् || 1-11 ||
1.1.m: What is that named Sudarśana, and what is accepted as the meaning of the word? / What action is performed by it, and how does it pervade the world? || 1-11

1.1.s:
kiyantaḥ kīdṛśāḥ ke ca vyūhāstasyoditā mune |
prayojanaṃ ca kiṃ teṣāṃ vyūhī teṣāṃ ca kīdṛśī || 1-12 ||
1.1.d:
कियन्तः कीदृशाः के च व्यूहास्तस्योदिता मुने |
प्रयोजनं च किं तेषां व्यूही तेषां च कीदृशी || 1-12 ||
1.1.m: How many, of what kind, and which are the emanations declared of it, O sage? / And what is their purpose, and what is their emanating source like? || 1-12

1.1.s:
viṣṇunā tasya saṃbandhaḥ kaśca kīdṛk ca saṃmataḥ |
kiṃ tena niyataṃ nityamutānyatrāpi dṛśyate || 1-13 ||
1.1.d:
विष्णुना तस्य संबन्धः कश्च कीदृक् च संमतः |
किं तेन नियतं नित्यमुतान्यत्रापि दृश्यते || 1-13 ||
1.1.m: What is its connection with Viṣṇu, and of what kind is it considered to be? / Is it restricted to him eternally, or is it seen elsewhere as well? || 1-13

1.1.s:
p. 3) eṣa me saṃśayo jāto nānāśāstranirīkṣaṇāt |
chindhyenaṃ bhagavan samyagupasanno'smyadhīhi bhoḥ || 1-14 ||
1.1.d:
प्. 3) एष मे संशयो जातो नानाशास्त्रनिरीक्षणात् |
छिन्ध्येनं भगवन् सम्यगुपसन्नोऽस्म्यधीहि भोः || 1-14 ||
1.1.m: This doubt has arisen in me from examining various scriptures. / Sever this completely, O blessed one; I have approached you, teach [me], sir!” || 1-14
Durvāsas's reply preceded by praise of the question.

1.1.s:
upapannamidaṃ vatsa yat tvayaivaṃ vimṛśyate |
tāni tāni tapāṃsyadya vyuchanti tava suvrata || 1-15 ||
1.1.d:
उपपन्नमिदं वत्स यत् त्वयैवं विमृश्यते |
तानि तानि तपांस्यद्य व्युछन्ति तव सुव्रत || 1-15 ||
1.1.m: “This is fitting, my child, that you deliberate thus. / Those various austerities of yours are bearing fruit today, O you of noble vows! || 1-15
The arising of the desire to know the highest reality only for one whose taints are ripened.

1.1.s:
āntaḥkaraṇike taistaiḥ kṣayaṃ nīte kaṣāyake |
manīṣā jāyate puṃsāṃ paratattvavimarśinī || 1-16 ||
1.1.d:
आन्तःकरणिके तैस्तैः क्षयं नीते कषायके |
मनीषा जायते पुंसां परतत्त्वविमर्शिनी || 1-16 ||
1.1.m: When the taints belonging to the inner organ have been brought to destruction by various means, / there arises in men the intellect that investigates the highest reality. || 1-16
Doubt in this matter even for Brahmā and the others.

1.1.s:
na saṃśayī bhavāneva pūrvopanyastavastuni |
brahmādyāśca yatante'tra saṃśayānā manīṣiṇaḥ || 1-17 ||
1.1.d:
न संशयी भवानेव पूर्वोपन्यस्तवस्तुनि |
ब्रह्माद्याश्च यतन्तेऽत्र संशयाना मनीषिणः || 1-17 ||
1.1.m: You are not the only one in doubt regarding the subject set forth before; / even wise beings such as Brahmā and others strive in this matter, having doubts. || 1-17
His own attainment of the determination of the truth from Ahirbudhnya.

1.1.s:
nirṇayo'tra mayā prāpto nāradāya surarṣaye |
sākṣāt kathayataḥ pṛṣṭācchaṃkarāllokaśaṃkarāt || 1-18 ||
1.1.d:
निर्णयोऽत्र मया प्राप्तो नारदाय सुरर्षये |
साक्षात् कथयतः पृष्टाच्छंकराल्लोकशंकरात् || 1-18 ||
1.1.m: The conclusive determination in this matter was obtained by me from the divine sage Nārada, / to whom it was spoken directly when asked of Śaṃkara, who brings auspiciousness to the world. || 1-18
Having obtained the supreme fruit of asceticism, Nārada, revered by the gods,
severing all doubts among Brahmā, the gods, and the great sages, || 1-19
His approaching Ahirbudhnya due to doubt regarding the reality even for himself.

1.1.s:
svayaṃ tu saṃśayaṃ prāpya gahanaṃ durvidaṃ suraiḥ |
arāgarogakaluṣastapasvī saṃyatendriyaḥ || 1-20 ||
1.1.d:
स्वयं तु संशयं प्राप्य गहनं दुर्विदं सुरैः |
अरागरोगकलुषस्तपस्वी संयतेन्द्रियः || 1-20 ||
1.1.m: himself arrived at a doubt that was deep and hard for the gods to comprehend; / free from the taint of passion and disease, an ascetic whose senses were controlled, || 1-20
knowing the correct application of words, sentences, and means of valid cognition, / a celibate student, an abode of self-restraint, knowing the division between the higher and the lower, || 1-21
desirous of hearing, free from egotism, devoted to true knowledge, / Nārada, the tiger among sages, wandering through the three worlds, || 1-22

1.1.s:
chettāraṃ saṃśayasyāsya durvidasya surarṣibhiḥ |
devādanabhigamyānyaṃ sarvajñāccandraśekharāt || 1-23 ||
1.1.d:
छेत्तारं संशयस्यास्य दुर्विदस्य सुरर्षिभिः |
देवादनभिगम्यान्यं सर्वज्ञाच्चन्द्रशेखरात् || 1-23 ||
1.1.m: finding no other dispeller of this doubt—difficult for the divine sages to know— / than the all-knowing god who bears the crescent moon, || 1-23

1.1.s:
prabhābhiḥ svābhirakhilān prahasantamivācalān |
unmeṣamiva sattvasya prakṛṣṭajñānakāriṇaḥ || 1-24 ||
1.1.d:
प्रभाभिः स्वाभिरखिलान् प्रहसन्तमिवाचलान् |
उन्मेषमिव सत्त्वस्य प्रकृष्टज्ञानकारिणः || 1-24 ||
1.1.m: which seemed to mock all mountains with its own splendors, / as if the awakening of sattva that produces superior knowledge, || 1-24

1.1.s:
siddhavidyādharākīrṇaṃ devagandharvasevitam |
kailāsaṃ śaṃkarāvāsaṃ śaṃkaraṃ draṣṭumāyayau || 1-25 ||
1.1.d:
सिद्धविद्याधराकीर्णं देवगन्धर्वसेवितम् |
कैलासं शंकरावासं शंकरं द्रष्टुमाययौ || 1-25 ||
1.1.m: thronged with siddhas and vidyādharas, attended by gods and gandharvas— / he came to Kailāsa, the abode of Śaṃkara, to see Śaṃkara. || 1-25
By Rudras, Vasus, Ādityas, siddhas, Sādhyas, hosts of Maruts, / by sages, yogins, divine beings, and also manifold spirits, || 1-26

1.1.s:
p. 5) dadarśa sevitaṃ tatra samāsīnaṃ sahomayā |
tryakṣaṃ varadamīśānaṃ śūlinaṃ candraśekharaṃ || 1-27 ||
1.1.d:
प्. 5) ददर्श सेवितं तत्र समासीनं सहोमया |
त्र्यक्षं वरदमीशानं शूलिनं चन्द्रशेखरं || 1-27 ||
1.1.m: he saw him attended there, seated together with Umā, / the three-eyed, boon-granting Īśāna, bearer of the trident, crescent-crested, || 1-27

1.1.s:
patiṃ paśūnāmaniśaṃ bhavapāśāvibhedinam |
sthitaṃ mūrtibhiraṣṭābhiravaṣṭabhya jagattrayam || 1-28 ||
1.1.d:
पतिं पशूनामनिशं भवपाशाविभेदिनम् |
स्थितं मूर्तिभिरष्टाभिरवष्टभ्य जगत्त्रयम् || 1-28 ||
1.1.m: the lord of bound souls who perpetually severs the bonds of worldly existence, / standing having supported the triad of worlds by means of eight forms. || 1-28

1.1.s:
taṃ dṛṣṭvā devamīśānaṃ nārado devadarśanaḥ |
praṇipatyātha tuṣṭāva gīrbhiragryābhirādarāt || 1-29 ||
1.1.d:
तं दृष्ट्वा देवमीशानं नारदो देवदर्शनः |
प्रणिपत्याथ तुष्टाव गीर्भिरग्र्याभिरादरात् || 1-29 ||
1.1.m: Seeing that god Īśāna, Nārada, whose vision is divine, / having bowed down, then praised him respectfully with sublime words: || 1-29
Praise of Ahirbudhnya by Nārada.

1.1.s:
namaste devadeveśa namaste vṛṣaketana |
vṛṣapravaravāhāya vṛṣṇe kāmapravarṣiṇe || 1-30 ||
1.1.d:
नमस्ते देवदेवेश नमस्ते वृषकेतन |
वृषप्रवरवाहाय वृष्णे कामप्रवर्षिणे || 1-30 ||
1.1.m: “Homage to you, O lord of the gods of gods! Homage to you whose emblem is the bull, / whose mount is the excellent bull, the showerer who rains down desires! || 1-30

1.1.s:
ojīyase parasmai te mīḍhuṣṭama namo'stu te |
sarvajñāya svatantrāya nityatṛptāya te namaḥ || 1-31 ||
1.1.d:
ओजीयसे परस्मै ते मीढुष्टम नमोऽस्तु ते |
सर्वज्ञाय स्वतन्त्राय नित्यतृप्ताय ते नमः || 1-31 ||
1.1.m: To you, the most vigorous, the supreme, most generous giver, let homage be! / Homage to you, the omniscient, the independent, the eternally satisfied! || 1-31

1.1.s:
anādibodharūpāya namaste nityaśaktaye |
kartre hartre ca jagatāṃ ṣaḍaṅgāya namo'stu te || 1-32 ||
1.1.d:
अनादिबोधरूपाय नमस्ते नित्यशक्तये |
कर्त्रे हर्त्रे च जगतां षडङ्गाय नमोऽस्तु ते || 1-32 ||
1.1.m: Homage to you whose nature is beginningless awareness, whose power is eternal! / To the creator and destroyer of the worlds, having six limbs, let homage be! || 1-32

1.1.s:
daśāvyaya namastubhyaṃ namaste kṛttivāsase |
aghorāyātha ghorāya ghoraghoratarāya ca || 1-33 ||
1.1.d:
दशाव्यय नमस्तुभ्यं नमस्ते कृत्तिवाससे |
अघोरायाथ घोराय घोरघोरतराय च || 1-33 ||
1.1.m: Homage to you whose state is imperishable, homage to you clad in animal skins! / To the placid, and to the fierce, and to the exceedingly fierce! || 1-33
Homage to the god Sadyojāta, to Vāmadeva!

1.1.s: p. 6) namo jyeṣṭhāya rudrāya bhavodbhava namo'stu te || 1-34 ||
1.1.d: प्. 6) नमो ज्येष्ठाय रुद्राय भवोद्भव नमोऽस्तु ते || 1-34 ||
1.1.m: Homage to the eldest, to Rudra; O origin of existence, let homage be to you! || 1-34

1.1.s:
namo balavikārāya balapramathanāya te |
namaḥ  -  -  -  -  -  -  -  -  -  -  -  -  -  -  -  -  -  -  -  -  -  - ya te namaḥ] || 1-35 ||
1.1.m: Homage to the transformer of strength, to the crusher of strength! / Homage […] to you, homage! || 1-35

1.1.s:
namaḥ kalavikārāya kālāya kalanātmane |
namaste sarvabhūtānāṃ damanāya manonmana || 1-36 ||
1.1.d:
नमः कलविकाराय कालाय कलनात्मने |
नमस्ते सर्वभूतानां दमनाय मनोन्मन || 1-36 ||
1.1.m: Homage to the transformer of parts, to time, to the soul of impulsion! / Homage to you, the subduer of all beings, O Manonmana! || 1-36

1.1.s:
namaḥ śarvāya śāntāya śaṃbhave śaṃbhave namaḥ |
vidyeśvara namastubhyaṃ bhūteśvara namo'stu te || 1-37 ||
1.1.d:
नमः शर्वाय शान्ताय शंभवे शंभवे नमः |
विद्येश्वर नमस्तुभ्यं भूतेश्वर नमोऽस्तु ते || 1-37 ||
1.1.m: Homage to Śarva, to the tranquil, to Śaṃbhu, to Śaṃbhu homage! / O lord of knowledge, homage to you; O lord of beings, let homage be to you! || 1-37

1.1.s:
mahādeva namaste'stu namastatpuruṣāya te |
jñānarūpa namastubhyaṃ namo vairāgyavāridhe || 1-38 ||
1.1.d:
महादेव नमस्तेऽस्तु नमस्तत्पुरुषाय ते |
ज्ञानरूप नमस्तुभ्यं नमो वैराग्यवारिधे || 1-38 ||
1.1.m: O Mahādeva, let homage be to you! Homage to you, Tatpuruṣa! / O you whose form is knowledge, homage to you! Homage, O ocean of dispassion! || 1-38

1.1.s:
aiśvaryaguṇapūrṇāya namaste tapasāṃ nidhe |
nityasatya namaste'stu kṣamāsāra namo'stu te || 1-39 ||
1.1.d:
ऐश्वर्यगुणपूर्णाय नमस्ते तपसां निधे |
नित्यसत्य नमस्तेऽस्तु क्षमासार नमोऽस्तु ते || 1-39 ||
1.1.m: To you who are full of the attribute of sovereignty, homage, O treasury of austerities! / O you of eternal truth, let homage be to you; O essence of forbearance, let homage be to you! || 1-39

1.1.s:
dhṛtisāra namastubhyaṃ sraṣṭre te jagatāṃ namaḥ |
ātmasaṃbodhapūrṇāya trīn lokānadhitiṣṭhate || 1-40 ||
1.1.d:
धृतिसार नमस्तुभ्यं स्रष्ट्रे ते जगतां नमः |
आत्मसंबोधपूर्णाय त्रीन् लोकानधितिष्ठते || 1-40 ||
1.1.m: O essence of fortitude, homage to you; homage to you, creator of the worlds, / who are filled with self-awakening, who preside over the three worlds! || 1-40

1.1.s:
daśāvyayāya te nityamavyayāya namo namaḥ |
kṣoṇyambvanalavāyvabhracandrādityātmane namaḥ || 1-41 ||
1.1.d:
दशाव्ययाय ते नित्यमव्ययाय नमो नमः |
क्षोण्यम्ब्वनलवाय्वभ्रचन्द्रादित्यात्मने नमः || 1-41 ||
1.1.m: Homage, homage to you of unchanging state, who are eternally immutable! / Homage to you who are the self of earth, water, fire, wind, ether, moon, and sun! || 1-41
Homage to the benefactor of all, who stand pervading the three worlds!
To the best of divine seers thus praising him with the highest words, || 1-42
he whose emblem is the bull spoke these words sweet with grace:
I am pleased with this hymn and with your devotion, O bull among sages! || 1-43

1.1.s: brūhi kiṃ karavāṇyadya yadyapi syāt sudurlabham |
1.1.d: ब्रूहि किं करवाण्यद्य यद्यपि स्यात् सुदुर्लभम् |
1.1.m: Speak: what may I do today, even if it be very difficult to attain?
What else is to be said here, if the lord of the world is pleased? || 1-44
For this alone the striving wise desire.
I am gracious to you today; let my vision bear fruit! || 1-45

1.1.s: brūhi nārada tattvena yat te manasi vartate |
1.1.d: ब्रूहि नारद तत्त्वेन यत् ते मनसि वर्तते |
1.1.m: Tell, O Nārada, truly what is in your mind.
Nārada's vision of the majesty of Sudarśana in the battle with Kālanemi
In the battle of Kālanemi, resembling the war over Tārakā, || 1-46
when the sustainer of the world, the god of gods who wields the bow Śārṅga, had engaged, / striking terror into gods, Dānavas, Gandharvas, Yakṣas, and Rakṣases; || 1-47
which was crowded with hosts of weapons and missile weapons blazing like a thousand midday suns; / when the armies of the lords of gods and Asuras were cut down by the great missile; || 1-48
which was thronged with swarms of Piśācas, Pretas, Vetālas, and Bhūtas / crowding, gathering, leaping, born of fright and wonder; || 1-49

1.1.s:
p. 8) udyantīṣvatighorāsu hrādinīṣvaśanīṣu ca |
devadānavadehebhyaḥ kṣaradbhiḥ kṣatajaistathā || 1-50 ||
1.1.d:
प्. 8) उद्यन्तीष्वतिघोरासु ह्रादिनीष्वशनीषु च |
देवदानवदेहेभ्यः क्षरद्भिः क्षतजैस्तथा || 1-50 ||
1.1.m: when very terrifying thunders and thunderbolts were rising; / and by blood streaming from the bodies of gods and Dānavas || 1-50

1.1.s:
syandamānāsu vegena syandinīṣu samantataḥ |
vidrutaiḥ sarvato bhītairhataśeṣaiḥ surāsuraiḥ || 1-51 ||
1.1.d:
स्यन्दमानासु वेगेन स्यन्दिनीषु समन्ततः |
विद्रुतैः सर्वतो भीतैर्हतशेषैः सुरासुरैः || 1-51 ||
1.1.m: rivers were flowing with swift currents on every side; / while the gods and Asuras who survived, terrified, were fleeing in all directions; || 1-51
as the lord of the world mounted Garuḍa, with Sudarśana in his lotus hand, / Kālanemi manifested the entire array of missile weapons: || 1-52

1.1.s:
bhṛśāśvatanayā ye te ye te tvanmukhaniḥsṛtāḥ |
ye te brahmamukhodbhūtā ye te saṃvartakālajāḥ || 1-53 ||
1.1.d:
भृशाश्वतनया ये ते ये ते त्वन्मुखनिःसृताः |
ये ते ब्रह्ममुखोद्भूता ये ते संवर्तकालजाः || 1-53 ||
1.1.m: those that are the sons of Bhṛśāśva; those that issued from your mouth; / those born of the mouth of Brahmā; those produced at the time of the universal dissolution; || 1-53

1.1.s:
lokapālodbhavā ye te ye te pātālavāsinaḥ |
mahābhūtamayā ye te ye te vaikārikodbhavāḥ || 1-54 ||
1.1.d:
लोकपालोद्भवा ये ते ये ते पातालवासिनः |
महाभूतमया ये ते ये ते वैकारिकोद्भवाः || 1-54 ||
1.1.m: those originating from the world-guardians; those inhabiting the nether world; / those consisting of the great elements; those born of the ego-principle; || 1-54

1.1.s:
guṇatrayamayā ye te ye te gandharvayonayaḥ |
rakṣoyakṣodbhavā ye te ye te vidyādharāhvayā || 1-55 ||
1.1.d:
गुणत्रयमया ये ते ये ते गन्धर्वयोनयः |
रक्षोयक्षोद्भवा ये ते ये ते विद्याधराह्वया || 1-55 ||
1.1.m: those consisting of the three guṇas; those born of Gandharvas; / those originating from Rakṣases and Yakṣas; those named after Vidyādharas; || 1-55

1.1.s:
ye te dvandvaguṇodbhūtā ye te śaktisamudbhavāḥ |
atharvāṅgirasā ye te ye te mantrāntarodbhavāḥ || 1-56 ||
1.1.d:
ये ते द्वन्द्वगुणोद्भूता ये ते शक्तिसमुद्भवाः |
अथर्वाङ्गिरसा ये ते ये ते मन्त्रान्तरोद्भवाः || 1-56 ||
1.1.m: those born of pairs of opposites; those originating from Śakti; / those belonging to Atharvan and Aṅgiras; those originating from other mantras; || 1-56

1.1.s:
sarvakāryakarā ye te  pravartakanivartakāḥ |
yaṣṭayaḥ śaktayo yāstā ye te daṇḍādirūpakāḥ || 1-57  ||
1.1.d:
सर्वकार्यकरा ये ते  प्रवर्तकनिवर्तकाः |
यष्टयः शक्तयो यास्ता ये ते दण्डादिरूपकाः || 1-57  ||
1.1.m: those that perform all functions, both projecting and withdrawing; / staffs, Śaktis, and those having the forms of rods and the like; || 1-57
possessed of great strength and great power, intent on destroying the three worlds, / some resembling kingly mountains, some resembling lordly serpents, || 1-58

1.1.s:
p. 9) pārāvāranibhāḥ kecit kecid gaganasaṃnibhāḥ |
jvalajjvālāśatālīḍhā rodasīmadhyavartinaḥ || 1-59 ||
1.1.d:
प्. 9) पारावारनिभाः केचित् केचिद् गगनसंनिभाः |
ज्वलज्ज्वालाशतालीढा रोदसीमध्यवर्तिनः || 1-59 ||
1.1.m: some resembling oceans, some resembling the sky, / enveloped in hundreds of blazing flames, standing between heaven and earth, || 1-59

1.1.s:
nṛtyantaśca hasantaśca kṣvelantaḥ patayālavaḥ |
anirdeśyā anaupamyā gaurāḥ śvetāruṇāsitāḥ || 1-60 ||
1.1.d:
नृत्यन्तश्च हसन्तश्च क्ष्वेलन्तः पतयालवः |
अनिर्देश्या अनौपम्या गौराः श्वेतारुणासिताः || 1-60 ||
1.1.m: dancing, laughing, leaping, swooping down, / indescribable, incomparable, fair, white, crimson, and black, || 1-60

1.1.s:
nānāsaṃsthānavarṇāśca nānāvibhramarociṣaḥ |
sarve saṃbhūya saṃyattāḥ kālanemipracoditāḥ || 1-61 ||
1.1.d:
नानासंस्थानवर्णाश्च नानाविभ्रमरोचिषः |
सर्वे संभूय संयत्ताः कालनेमिप्रचोदिताः || 1-61 ||
1.1.m: having diverse forms and colours, gleaming with diverse movements, / all assembling, prepared, impelled by Kālanemi. || 1-61
The vanquishing of all missile weapons by Sudarśana
With their deployments and retractions, along with their secret teachings, all meeting together, / by all those complete collections of missile weapons, in the great fire of Sudarśana || 1-62

1.1.s:
sudarśanamahāvahnau saṃbhūya śalabhāyitam |
pūrṇāhutirabhūt tasmin kālanemirmahāsuraḥ || 1-63 ||
1.1.d:
सुदर्शनमहावह्नौ संभूय शलभायितम् |
पूर्णाहुतिरभूत् तस्मिन् कालनेमिर्महासुरः || 1-63 ||
1.1.m: raised in Nārāyaṇa's hand, they became like moths together; / and the great Asura Kālanemi became the final oblation into it. || 1-63
The arising of doubt from seeing this most wondrous majesty

1.1.s:
taṃ dṛṣṭvā vismayāviṣṭaḥ saṃgrāmaṃ mahadadbhutam |
antarhitaṃ kṣaṇāt kṛṣṇaṃ praṇipatya jagadgurum || 1-64 ||
1.1.d:
तं दृष्ट्वा विस्मयाविष्टः संग्रामं महदद्भुतम् |
अन्तर्हितं क्षणात् कृष्णं प्रणिपत्य जगद्गुरुम् || 1-64 ||
1.1.m: Having seen that battle, a great wonder, filled with astonishment, / bowing down to Kṛṣṇa, the teacher of the world, who vanished in an instant, || 1-64

1.1.s:
imaṃ saṃdehasaṃdohaṃ hṛdayena vahan gurum |
tavāntikamiha prāptaḥ saṃśayacchedanāya vai || 1-65 ||
1.1.d:
इमं संदेहसंदोहं हृदयेन वहन् गुरुम् |
तवान्तिकमिह प्राप्तः संशयच्छेदनाय वै || 1-65 ||
1.1.m: carrying this heavy burden of doubt in my heart, / I have come here to your presence indeed, in order to sever my doubt. || 1-65

1.1.s: na hi sarvajñamīśānaṃ vinā chettāsya vidyate |
1.1.d: न हि सर्वज्ञमीशानं विना छेत्तास्य विद्यते |
1.1.m: For indeed none exists to cut it away except Īśāna, the all-knowing.

1.1.s: devarṣe saṃśayān brūhi ye vartante tavāntare || 1-66 ||
1.1.d: देवर्षे संशयान् ब्रूहि ये वर्तन्ते तवान्तरे || 1-66 ||
1.1.m: O divine seer, speak the doubts that reside within you; || 1-66
even if they are indescribable, I shall cut them all away now.
Then, to the questions spoken in order by Nārada, the divine seer, || 1-67
the blessed Śarva, pleased in mind in every way, explained.
This is that saṃhitā proclaimed, dealing with the objects of various mantras, || 1-68

1.1.s:
pañcarātramayī divyā nāmnāhirbudhnyapūrvikā |
arthaiḥ parakṛtiprāyaiḥ purākalpaiśca saṃyutā || 1-69 ||
1.1.d:
पञ्चरात्रमयी दिव्या नाम्नाहिर्बुध्न्यपूर्विका |
अर्थैः परकृतिप्रायैः पुराकल्पैश्च संयुता || 1-69 ||
1.1.m: consisting of Pāñcarātra, divine, bearing Ahirbudhnya's name as its prefix, / endowed with meanings mostly of deeds of others and ancient traditions, || 1-69
having divisions of various doctrines, adorned with various branches of knowledge. / Here two hundred and forty chapters were displayed. || 1-70

1.1.s:
tato dvāparavelāyāṃ manuṣyāṇāṃ hitāya vai |
adhyāyānāṃ śatenātha viṃśatyā ca samanvitā || 1-71 ||
1.1.d:
ततो द्वापरवेलायां मनुष्याणां हिताय वै |
अध्यायानां शतेनाथ विंशत्या च समन्विता || 1-71 ||
1.1.m: Then, in the Dvāpara age, for the welfare of human beings, / endowed then with one hundred and twenty chapters, || 1-71

1.1.s:
ativistaramutsṛjya guhyena pratisaṃskṛtā |
tato'pi buddhisaṃkocānmanuṣyāṇāṃ hitāya vai || 1-72 ||
1.1.d:
अतिविस्तरमुत्सृज्य गुह्येन प्रतिसंस्कृता |
ततोऽपि बुद्धिसंकोचान्मनुष्याणां हिताय वै || 1-72 ||
1.1.m: leaving aside excessive length, it was redacted with secret [teachings]. / Then again, owing to the diminution of intellect, for the welfare of human beings, || 1-72

1.1.s:
p. 11) yāti dvāparasandhyaṃśe vyāsasyānumatermayā |
ṣaṣṭyadhyāyairiyaṃ bhūyaḥ saṃhitā pratisaṃskṛtā || 1-73 ||
1.1.d:
प्. 11) याति द्वापरसन्ध्यंशे व्यासस्यानुमतेर्मया |
षष्ट्यध्यायैरियं भूयः संहिता प्रतिसंस्कृता || 1-73 ||
1.1.m: as the twilight portion of the Dvāpara age was passing, by the permission of Vyāsa, / this saṃhitā was redacted once more by me in sixty chapters. || 1-73

1.1.s:
upanyāsthadyathāpraśnaṃ nārado bhagavānṛṣiḥ |
niruvāca yathā śarvastān sarvāṃstvaṃ nibodha me || 1-74 ||
1.1.d:
उपन्यास्थद्यथाप्रश्नं नारदो भगवानृषिः |
निरुवाच यथा शर्वस्तान् सर्वांस्त्वं निबोध मे || 1-74 ||
1.1.m: As the venerable seer Nārada propounded question by question, / and as Śarva expounded them, learn all that from me. || 1-74

1.1.s:
iti śrīpāñcarātre tantrarahasye ahirbudhnyasaṃhitāyāṃ
śāstrāvatāro nāma prathamo'dhyāyaḥ || 1 ||
1.1.d:
इति श्रीपाञ्चरात्रे तन्त्ररहस्ये अहिर्बुध्न्यसंहितायां
शास्त्रावतारो नाम प्रथमोऽध्यायः || 1 ||
1.1.m: Thus ends the first chapter, named 'The Descent of the Teaching', in the Ahirbudhnyasaṃhitā in the esoteric Tantra of the glorious Pāñcarātra. || 1
The second chapter, named 'Discrimination of Brahman Possessed of the Six Attributes'
Nārada's question to Ahirbudhnya

1.1.s:
mantragrāmānaśeṣāṃstān sūryavaiśvānaropamān |
anāyāsena jagrāha hareścakraṃ sudarśanam || 2-1 ||
1.1.d:
मन्त्रग्रामानशेषांस्तान् सूर्यवैश्वानरोपमान् |
अनायासेन जग्राह हरेश्चक्रं सुदर्शनम् || 2-1 ||
1.1.m: All those collections of mantras, resembling the sun and fire, / Hari's discus Sudarśana seized without effort. || 2-1

1.1.s:
sāṃsiddhikaprabhāvo'yamasya sāṃsargiko'pi vā |
kiṃ tat sudarśanaṃ nāma kaśca śabdārtha ucyate || 2-2 ||
1.1.d:
सांसिद्धिकप्रभावोऽयमस्य सांसर्गिकोऽपि वा |
किं तत् सुदर्शनं नाम कश्च शब्दार्थ उच्यते || 2-2 ||
1.1.m: Is this power of its innate, or rather acquired through association? / What is that called Sudarśana, and what is explained as the meaning of the word? || 2-2
Ahirbudhnya's account of obtaining his own knowledge from Saṃkarṣaṇa

1.1.s:
śṛṇu nārada tattvena yat tajjñānamanuttamam |
varṣāyutagaṇān ghoraṃ tapastaptvā mayā purā || 2-3 ||
1.1.d:
शृणु नारद तत्त्वेन यत् तज्ज्ञानमनुत्तमम् |
वर्षायुतगणान् घोरं तपस्तप्त्वा मया पुरा || 2-3 ||
1.1.m: Hear in truth, Nārada, that unsurpassed knowledge / which, having performed terrible asceticism for multitudes of myriad years in former times, || 2-3

1.1.s:
prāptaṃ saṃkarṣaṇāt sākṣād vijñānabalavāridheḥ |
brahmādiṣu yadanyeṣu na maharṣiṣu vidyate || 2-4 ||
1.1.d:
प्राप्तं संकर्षणात् साक्षाद् विज्ञानबलवारिधेः |
ब्रह्मादिषु यदन्येषु न महर्षिषु विद्यते || 2-4 ||
1.1.m: was directly obtained by me from Saṃkarṣaṇa, the ocean of wisdom and power— / which is not found in Brahmā and others, nor among the great sages. || 2-4

1.1.s:
sudarśanasvarūpaṃ tat procyamānaṃ mayā śṛṇu |
śrute yatrākhilādhāre saṃśayāste na santi vai || 2-5 ||
1.1.d:
सुदर्शनस्वरूपं तत् प्रोच्यमानं मया शृणु |
श्रुते यत्राखिलाधारे संशयास्ते न सन्ति वै || 2-5 ||
1.1.m: Hear that essential nature of Sudarśana being spoken by me, / which being heard as the support of everything, your doubts indeed will cease to be. || 2-5
Summary of the essential nature of the highest Brahman

1.1.s:
anādyantaṃ paraṃ brahma yat tadakṣaramavyayam |
anāmarūpasaṃbhedyamavāṅmanasagocaram || 2-6 ||
1.1.d:
अनाद्यन्तं परं ब्रह्म यत् तदक्षरमव्ययम् |
अनामरूपसंभेद्यमवाङ्मनसगोचरम् || 2-6 ||
1.1.m: Without beginning or end, the highest Brahman, which is that imperishable and undecaying [reality], / indistinguishable by name and form, beyond the reach of speech and mind, || 2-6
having all powers, denominated as the whole, possessed of the six attributes, unaging, constant—
Elucidation of the meaning of the word Sudarśana
its creative resolve, “May I be,” whether with respect to being or non-being, || 2-7

1.1.s:
svātantryānanuyojyena rūpeṇa parivartate |
yat tat prekṣaṇamityuktaṃ darśanaṃ tat pragīyate || 2-8 ||
1.1.d:
स्वातन्त्र्याननुयोज्येन रूपेण परिवर्तते |
यत् तत् प्रेक्षणमित्युक्तं दर्शनं तत् प्रगीयते || 2-8 ||
1.1.m: revolves with a form that cannot be questioned by virtue of its sovereignty; / that which is called regard (prekṣaṇa) is celebrated as vision (darśana). || 2-8

1.1.s:
vastutaḥ kālato deśāt tasya tvavyāhatirhi yā |
pūjā sātra suśabdārthastat sudarśanamīryate || 2-9 ||
1.1.d:
वस्तुतः कालतो देशात् तस्य त्वव्याहतिर्हि या |
पूजा सात्र सुशब्दार्थस्तत् सुदर्शनमीर्यते || 2-9 ||
1.1.m: Its unhinderedness in terms of entity, time, and space— / that excellence is here the meaning of the word “su”; that is declared to be “Sudarśana”. || 2-9
The dependence of all upon Sudarśana

1.1.s:
kāraṇaṃ jagato yat tadādhāro jagataśca yaḥ |
pramāṇaṃ jagato yat tat pramāṇārtho'khilaśca yaḥ || 2-10 ||
1.1.d:
कारणं जगतो यत् तदाधारो जगतश्च यः |
प्रमाणं जगतो यत् तत् प्रमाणार्थोऽखिलश्च यः || 2-10 ||
1.1.m: What is the cause of the universe and what is the support of the universe, / what is the means of knowledge for the universe and what is the entire object of knowledge, || 2-10

1.1.s:
tatrādhikāriṇo ye ca vibhāgā ye ca tadgatāḥ |
rakṣāvidhiśca yastasya sa ca yasya prakīrtitaḥ || 2-11 ||
1.1.d:
तत्राधिकारिणो ये च विभागा ये च तद्गताः |
रक्षाविधिश्च यस्तस्य स च यस्य प्रकीर्तितः || 2-11 ||
1.1.m: and the qualified persons therein, and the distinctions present in it, / and the rule of protection for it, and the one on whose behalf it is proclaimed: || 2-11

1.1.s:
sarvaṃ sudarśanāyattaṃ sudarśanamayaṃ ca yat |
iti sāṃsiddhikaṃ rūpaṃ tasya sarvātiśāyi ca || 2-12 ||
1.1.d:
सर्वं सुदर्शनायत्तं सुदर्शनमयं च यत् |
इति सांसिद्धिकं रूपं तस्य सर्वातिशायि च || 2-12 ||
1.1.m: everything is dependent on Sudarśana and consists of Sudarśana. / Thus its innate nature surpasses everything. || 2-12

1.1.s:
p. 14) astragrāmeṣvaśeṣeṣu yat tat sāmarthyamaiśvaram |
etadīyamaśeṣaṃ tadityāptaṃ svena tat svakam || 2-13 ||
1.1.d:
प्. 14) अस्त्रग्रामेष्वशेषेषु यत् तत् सामर्थ्यमैश्वरम् |
एतदीयमशेषं तदित्याप्तं स्वेन तत् स्वकम् || 2-13 ||
1.1.m: Whatever sovereign efficacy exists among all the collections of missile weapons, / all that belongs to this [discus]; thus it has gathered its own by itself. || 2-13
Questions posed again by Nārada

1.1.s:
devadeva jagannātha lokatritayaśaṃkara |
vimuhyatīva cittaṃ me saṃśayo bahulīkṛtaḥ || 2-14 ||
1.1.d:
देवदेव जगन्नाथ लोकत्रितयशंकर |
विमुह्यतीव चित्तं मे संशयो बहुलीकृतः || 2-14 ||
1.1.m: O god of gods, Lord of the Universe, benefactor of the three worlds, / my mind seems bewildered; my doubt has multiplied. || 2-14

1.1.s:
ṣāḍguṇyaṃ kiṃ paraṃ brahma kiṃprakāraṃ ca tadbhavet |
saṃkalpaḥ kīdṛśastasya kathaṃ darśanatāsya ca || 2-15 ||
1.1.d:
षाड्गुण्यं किं परं ब्रह्म किंप्रकारं च तद्भवेत् |
संकल्पः कीदृशस्तस्य कथं दर्शनतास्य च || 2-15 ||
1.1.m: What is that highest Brahman possessed of the six attributes, and of what nature might it be? / What is its creative resolve, and how is it vision? || 2-15

1.1.s:
kathaṃ cāvihatistasya sarvadeśātigocarā |
kiṃ kāraṇaṃ ca jagataḥ kīdṛśaṃ kiṃvidhaṃ ca tat || 2-16 ||
1.1.d:
कथं चाविहतिस्तस्य सर्वदेशातिगोचरा |
किं कारणं च जगतः कीदृशं किंविधं च तत् || 2-16 ||
1.1.m: And how is its unhinderedness having scope beyond all space? / And what is the cause of the universe, of what kind is it, and of what nature? || 2-16

1.1.s:
ko vā jagata ādhāraḥ kīdṛk katividhaśca saḥ |
kiṃ tat pramāṇamityuktaṃ kīdṛk katividhaṃ ca tat || 2-17 ||
1.1.d:
को वा जगत आधारः कीदृक् कतिविधश्च सः |
किं तत् प्रमाणमित्युक्तं कीदृक् कतिविधं च तत् || 2-17 ||
1.1.m: Or who is the support of the universe, what is it like, and of how many kinds? / What is that called the means of knowledge, what is it like, and of how many kinds? || 2-17

1.1.s:
pramāṇārthaśca ko nāma kīdṛk katividhaśca saḥ |
ke te'dhikāriṇo nāma kīdṛśāḥ kiṃvidhāśca te || 2-18 ||
1.1.d:
प्रमाणार्थश्च को नाम कीदृक् कतिविधश्च सः |
के तेऽधिकारिणो नाम कीदृशाः किंविधाश्च ते || 2-18 ||
1.1.m: And what indeed is the object of knowledge, what is it like, and of how many kinds? / Who indeed are those qualified persons, what are they like, and of what nature? || 2-18

1.1.s:
sarvasyāsya ca kā rakṣā tadvidhiḥ kaśca kiṃvidhaḥ |
kaśca tatrādhikāryarthaḥ sa ca kiṃguṇa iṣyate || 2-19 ||
1.1.d:
सर्वस्यास्य च का रक्षा तद्विधिः कश्च किंविधः |
कश्च तत्राधिकार्यर्थः स च किंगुण इष्यते || 2-19 ||
1.1.m: And what is the protection of all this, and what is its rule, and of what nature? / And what is the purpose of the qualified person therein, and endowed with what qualities is it held to be? || 2-19

1.1.s:
etanme bhagavan brūhi praśnajātamaśeṣataḥ |
upasaṃgṛhya caraṇāvupasanno'smyadhīhi bhoḥ || 2-20 ||
1.1.d:
एतन्मे भगवन् ब्रूहि प्रश्नजातमशेषतः |
उपसंगृह्य चरणावुपसन्नोऽस्म्यधीहि भोः || 2-20 ||
1.1.m: Tell me completely this whole collection of questions, O venerable one; / clasping your feet, I have approached you as a pupil; teach me, sir! || 2-20

1.1.s:
tato darśanapūtāya praṇipatyābhiyācate |
upasannāya munaye sarvaṃ vyācaṣṭa śaṃkaraḥ || 2-21 ||
1.1.d:
ततो दर्शनपूताय प्रणिपत्याभियाचते |
उपसन्नाय मुनये सर्वं व्याचष्ट शंकरः || 2-21 ||
1.1.m: Then Śaṃkara explained everything to the sage who was purified by seeing [him], / who had bowed down and beseeched him, having approached as a pupil. || 2-21
Detailed exposition of the essential nature of the highest Brahman

1.1.s:
ekaṃ nirduḥkhaniḥsīmasukhānubhavalakṣaṇam |
anādyantaṃ paraṃ brahma nārāyaṇamanāmayam || 2-22 ||
1.1.d:
एकं निर्दुःखनिःसीमसुखानुभवलक्षणम् |
अनाद्यन्तं परं ब्रह्म नारायणमनामयम् || 2-22 ||
1.1.m: One, characterized by the experience of sorrowless, limitless bliss, / without beginning or end, the highest Brahman, Nārāyaṇa, free from affliction, || 2-22
having made his dwelling in all beings, standing pervading all, / flawless, undisturbed, resembling a waveless ocean, || 2-23
The highest Brahman's opposition to what is to be shunned and its embodiment of auspicious qualities

1.1.s:
aprākṛtaguṇasparśamaprākṛtaguṇāspadam |
bhavodadheḥ paraṃ pāraṃ niṣkalaṅkaṃ nirañjanam || 2-24 ||
1.1.d:
अप्राकृतगुणस्पर्शमप्राकृतगुणास्पदम् |
भवोदधेः परं पारं निष्कलङ्कं निरञ्जनम् || 2-24 ||
1.1.m: having contact only with non-material qualities, the abode of non-material qualities, / the farther shore of the ocean of worldly existence, stainless, undefiled, || 2-24

1.1.s:
ākārād deśataḥ kālādanavacchedayogataḥ |
pūrṇaṃ nityoditaṃ vyāpi heyopādeyatojjhitam || 2-25 ||
1.1.d:
आकाराद् देशतः कालादनवच्छेदयोगतः |
पूर्णं नित्योदितं व्यापि हेयोपादेयतोज्झितम् || 2-25 ||
1.1.m: by virtue of non-limitation through form, space, or time, / full, ever-risen, all-pervading, free from what is to be rejected or accepted, || 2-25
truly indeterminable by definitions of “this,” “of such a kind,” or “of this measure.”
The highest Brahman being denoted by all words such as Paramātman
Above and beyond the principles that constitute the self of each preceding one, || 2-26
it is proclaimed as Paramātman because of its supreme selfhood; / through the union attained with the syllable “oṃ,” by entering into all principles, || 2-27

1.1.s:
p. 16) ṣāḍguṇyaguṇayogena bhagavān parikīrtitaḥ |
samastabhūtavāsitvād vāsudevaḥ prakīrtitaḥ || 2-28 ||
1.1.d:
प्. 16) षाड्गुण्यगुणयोगेन भगवान् परिकीर्तितः |
समस्तभूतवासित्वाद् वासुदेवः प्रकीर्तितः || 2-28 ||
1.1.m: and through union with the group of six attributes, it is proclaimed as Bhagavān; / because of dwelling in all beings, it is proclaimed as Vāsudeva; || 2-28

1.1.s:
āpnoti jagadityevamātmatvena nirūpitaḥ |
rūpāt prakārato'vyakteravyaktaḥ parigīyate || 2-29 ||
1.1.d:
आप्नोति जगदित्येवमात्मत्वेन निरूपितः |
रूपात् प्रकारतोऽव्यक्तेरव्यक्तः परिगीयते || 2-29 ||
1.1.m: because it pervades the universe, it is defined as the Self (ātman); / from its unmanifest form and manner, it is sung of as the Unmanifest (avyakta); || 2-29
because it is the primal power of all, it is called Sarvaprakṛti; / because effects are laid upon it, it is sung of as Pradhāna; || 2-30

1.1.s:
netṛtvādanitṛtvācca nitya ityapi paṭhyate |
ananādadanāccāpi hyanantaḥ paripaṭhyate || 2-31 ||
1.1.d:
नेतृत्वादनितृत्वाच्च नित्य इत्यपि पठ्यते |
अननाददनाच्चापि ह्यनन्तः परिपठ्यते || 2-31 ||
1.1.m: from leading and from moving, it is read as Nitya; / and from not breathing and from consuming, it is recited as Ananta; || 2-31

1.1.s:
parito mityabhāvācca prokto'parimito vudhaiḥ |
akṣayādakṣaraḥ prokto hyariṣṭo riṣṭavarjanāt || 2-32 ||
1.1.d:
परितो मित्यभावाच्च प्रोक्तोऽपरिमितो वुधैः |
अक्षयादक्षरः प्रोक्तो ह्यरिष्टो रिष्टवर्जनात् || 2-32 ||
1.1.m: from the absence of all-round measurement, it is declared Aparimita by the wise; / from undecaying, it is called Akṣara; and Ariṣṭa from being free of misfortune; || 2-32
from its immutable nature and unpervadedness, it is Acyuta; / from release from faults such as passion, and from being an object of equanimity, || 2-33
and from its equal material causality of all, it is celebrated as Sama; / because it is outside the path of meditation, and its nature cannot be questioned, || 2-34

1.1.s:
iyattayāpyacintyatvādacintyaḥ parikīrtitaḥ |
jaganti prabhavantyasmāt sarvatra prabhavatyapi || 2-35 ||
1.1.d:
इयत्तयाप्यचिन्त्यत्वादचिन्त्यः परिकीर्तितः |
जगन्ति प्रभवन्त्यस्मात् सर्वत्र प्रभवत्यपि || 2-35 ||
1.1.m: and because it cannot be conceived by any measure, it is proclaimed as Acintya; / because worlds originate from it and it holds sway everywhere, || 2-35

1.1.s:
prakṛṣṭaśca bhavo yasmāt prabhavaḥ parikīrtitaḥ |
sarvapralayabhūmitvādavyayo vyayanāśanāt || 2-36 ||
1.1.d:
प्रकृष्टश्च भवो यस्मात् प्रभवः परिकीर्तितः |
सर्वप्रलयभूमित्वादव्ययो व्ययनाशनात् || 2-36 ||
1.1.m: and because it is the supreme source of being, it is proclaimed as Prabhava; / because it is the ground of dissolution of all, it is Avyaya from destroying decay; || 2-36

1.1.s:
bṛhattvād bṛṃhaṇatvācca brahmeti śrutigahvare |
kapilaḥ śreṣṭhavidyatvāt tejiṣṭhatvācca kāpilaḥ || 2-37 ||
1.1.d:
बृहत्त्वाद् बृंहणत्वाच्च ब्रह्मेति श्रुतिगह्वरे |
कपिलः श्रेष्ठविद्यत्वात् तेजिष्ठत्वाच्च कापिलः || 2-37 ||
1.1.m: from being vast and from causing growth, it is [called] Brahman in the depths of scripture; / Kapila from having the foremost wisdom, and Kāpila from being the most radiant; || 2-37

1.1.s:
p. 17) hitaśca ramaṇīyaśca garbho hṛdayanāmavān |
hiraṇyagarbha ityevaṃ yogibhiḥ samudāhṛtaḥ || 2-38 ||
1.1.d:
प्. 17) हितश्च रमणीयश्च गर्भो हृदयनामवान् |
हिरण्यगर्भ इत्येवं योगिभिः समुदाहृतः || 2-38 ||
1.1.m: beneficial and delightful, the womb bearing the name of the heart, / thus it is spoken of as Hiraṇyagarbha by yogins; || 2-38

1.1.s:
apanāśatapoyogādapāntaratapāḥ śrutaḥ |
śivaṃkaratayā proktaḥ śivaḥ pāśupate sthitaiḥ || 2-39 ||
1.1.d:
अपनाशतपोयोगादपान्तरतपाः श्रुतः |
शिवंकरतया प्रोक्तः शिवः पाशुपते स्थितैः || 2-39 ||
1.1.m: it is heard as Apāntaratapas through the union of asceticism that destroys [sins]; / it is declared as Śiva by those established in the Pāśupata [doctrine] because of bringing auspiciousness; || 2-39
by those standing at a moderate distance who do not truly penetrate it— / by such words that reality is indicated. || 2-40
The possibility of experiencing Brahman upon the removal of obstacles
When merit and demerit accumulated over many births are destroyed, / when the web of latent impressions is cut away by the weapon of complete knowledge, || 2-41

1.1.s:
traiguṇyoparame tattu svenānubhavituṃ kṣamam |
sākṣādidamiti vyaktaṃ vācā vaktuṃ na śaknumaḥ || 2-42 ||
1.1.d:
त्रैगुण्योपरमे तत्तु स्वेनानुभवितुं क्षमम् |
साक्षादिदमिति व्यक्तं वाचा वक्तुं न शक्नुमः || 2-42 ||
1.1.m: and when the three guṇas subside, that [reality] can be experienced by oneself; / we are not able to state it clearly in words as “it is directly this.” || 2-42
Brahman cannot be attained by mere effort

1.1.s:
saṃvatsarasahasrāṇi pakṣirāḍiva saṃpatan |
naivāntaṃ kāraṇasyaiti yadyapi syānmanojavaḥ || 2-43 ||
1.1.d:
संवत्सरसहस्राणि पक्षिराडिव संपतन् |
नैवान्तं कारणस्यैति यद्यपि स्यान्मनोजवः || 2-43 ||
1.1.m: Even if flying like the king of birds for thousands of years, / one never reaches the end of the cause, even if one were swift as thought. || 2-43

1.1.s:
uparyupari gacchanto viśikṣantastathā tathā |
jñānodyamadaśāyāste na vyaktimadhikāṃ gatāḥ || 2-44 ||
1.1.d:
उपर्युपरि गच्छन्तो विशिक्षन्तस्तथा तथा |
ज्ञानोद्यमदशायास्ते न व्यक्तिमधिकां गताः || 2-44 ||
1.1.m: Soaring higher and higher, training themselves in every way, / in their stage of striving for knowledge they attain no greater manifestation. || 2-44
All principles settle down in that supreme Self;
both being and non-being are declared to consist of the thread of knowledge. || 2-45
Brahman is devoid of the three kinds of limitation

1.1.s:
sarvapratyakṣadarśitvāt sarvātmā tat paraṃ padam |
atītānāgate kāle madhyataḥ pratisaṃhṛte || 2-46 ||
1.1.d:
सर्वप्रत्यक्षदर्शित्वात् सर्वात्मा तत् परं पदम् |
अतीतानागते काले मध्यतः प्रतिसंहृते || 2-46 ||
1.1.m: Because it perceives everything directly, that highest abode is the self of all. / When past and future time are withdrawn from the middle, || 2-46

1.1.s:
vartamānaṃ na tad brahma nātītaṃ naiva bhāvi tat |
agrataḥ pṛṣṭhato naiva nordhvataḥ pārśvayordvayoḥ || 2-47 ||
1.1.d:
वर्तमानं न तद् ब्रह्म नातीतं नैव भावि तत् |
अग्रतः पृष्ठतो नैव नोर्ध्वतः पार्श्वयोर्द्वयोः || 2-47 ||
1.1.m: that Brahman is not present, nor is it past, nor yet to come; / it is not in front, nor behind, nor above, nor on either side; || 2-47

1.1.s:
na kalmāṣaṃ na vikalaṃ na kṛṣṇaṃ na ca piṅgalam |
na sāraṅgaṃ piśaṅgaṃ na kapilaṃ nāruṇaṃ na ca || 2-48 ||
1.1.d:
न कल्माषं न विकलं न कृष्णं न च पिङ्गलम् |
न सारङ्गं पिशङ्गं न कपिलं नारुणं न च || 2-48 ||
1.1.m: not spotted, not defective, neither black nor tawny, / neither dappled nor yellowish, not brown and not reddish-brown; || 2-48

1.1.s:
na babhru nakulaṃ naiva na śyāmaṃ na ca rohitam |
na dīrghaṃ naiva ca hrasvaṃ na sthūlaṃ naiva cāpyaṇu || 2-49 ||
1.1.d:
न बभ्रु नकुलं नैव न श्यामं न च रोहितम् |
न दीर्घं नैव च ह्रस्वं न स्थूलं नैव चाप्यणु || 2-49 ||
1.1.m: neither dark brown nor golden, neither dark blue nor red; / neither long nor short, neither gross nor subtle; || 2-49

1.1.s:
na vṛttaṃ nāpyapāvṛttaṃ nāśritaṃ tadanāśritam |
naiva bhāvo na cābhāvastadbhāvārcitaye na ca || 2-50 ||
1.1.d:
न वृत्तं नाप्यपावृत्तं नाश्रितं तदनाश्रितम् |
नैव भावो न चाभावस्तद्भावार्चितये न च || 2-50 ||
1.1.m: neither rounded nor uncurved; neither dependent nor independent; / neither being nor non-being, nor [existing] for the sake of revering being; || 2-50

1.1.s:
na śītaṃ nāpi caivoṣṇaṃ nānuṣṇāśītamapyuta |
na duḥkhaṃ na sukhaṃ naiva nirduḥkhaṃ sukhamavraṇam || 2-51 ||
1.1.d:
न शीतं नापि चैवोष्णं नानुष्णाशीतमप्युत |
न दुःखं न सुखं नैव निर्दुःखं सुखमव्रणम् || 2-51 ||
1.1.m: neither cold nor hot, nor even lukewarm; / neither suffering nor joy, [yet] free from suffering, flawless bliss; || 2-51

1.1.s:
na mūlaṃ nāpi tanmadhyaṃ naivāntaṃ kasyācinmune |
na śete tanna caivāste na tiṣṭhati na gacchati || 2-52 ||
1.1.d:
न मूलं नापि तन्मध्यं नैवान्तं कस्याचिन्मुने |
न शेते तन्न चैवास्ते न तिष्ठति न गच्छति || 2-52 ||
1.1.m: not the root, nor the middle, nor the end of anything, O sage; / it neither lies down, nor sits, nor stands, nor moves. || 2-52

1.1.s:
sarvadvandvavinirmuktaṃ sarvopādhivivarjitam |
ṣāḍguṇyaṃ tat paraṃ brahma sarvakāraṇakāraṇam || 2-53 ||
1.1.d:
सर्वद्वन्द्वविनिर्मुक्तं सर्वोपाधिविवर्जितम् |
षाड्गुण्यं तत् परं ब्रह्म सर्वकारणकारणम् || 2-53 ||
1.1.m: Free from all dualities, devoid of all limiting adjuncts, / that supreme Brahman possesses the six attributes, the cause of all causes. || 2-53

1.1.s:
kiṃ tat ṣāḍguṇyamityuktaṃ devadeva jagatpate |
kathaṃ ca guṇahīnaṃ tat ṣāḍguṇyaṃ parigīyate || 2-54 ||
1.1.d:
किं तत् षाड्गुण्यमित्युक्तं देवदेव जगत्पते |
कथं च गुणहीनं तत् षाड्गुण्यं परिगीयते || 2-54 ||
1.1.m: What is this sixfold attribute that has been spoken of, O god of gods, O lord of the world? / And how is that which is devoid of qualities proclaimed to possess the six attributes? || 2-54
Detailed explanation of the six attributes of Brahman

1.1.s:
aprākṛtaguṇasparśaṃ nirguṇaṃ parigīyate |
śṛṇu nārada ṣāḍguṇyaṃ kathyamānaṃ mayānagha || 2-55 ||
1.1.d:
अप्राकृतगुणस्पर्शं निर्गुणं परिगीयते |
शृणु नारद षाड्गुण्यं कथ्यमानं मयानघ || 2-55 ||
1.1.m: Because it has no contact with material qualities, it is proclaimed to be qualityless. / Hear, O sinless Nārada, the six attributes as they are described by me: || 2-55
Definition of the nature of knowledge

1.1.s:
ajaḍaṃ svātmasaṃbodhi nityaṃ sarvāvagāhanam |
jñānaṃ nāma guṇaṃ prāhuḥ prathamaṃ guṇacintakāḥ || 2-56 ||
1.1.d:
अजडं स्वात्मसंबोधि नित्यं सर्वावगाहनम् |
ज्ञानं नाम गुणं प्राहुः प्रथमं गुणचिन्तकाः || 2-56 ||
1.1.m: Inertless, self-conscious, eternal, penetrating everything— / such knowledge the contemplators of the attributes declare to be the first attribute. || 2-56
Brahman is both of the nature of knowledge and possesses the attribute of knowledge
It is proclaimed to be the very nature of Brahman, and also its attribute.
Definition of the nature of power
That which is the state of being the material source of the universe is celebrated as power. || 2-57
Definition of the nature of sovereignty

1.1.s:
kartṛtvaṃ nāma yat tasya svātantryaparibṛṃhitam |
aiśvaryaṃ nāma tat proktaṃ guṇatattvārthacintakaiḥ || 2-58 ||
1.1.d:
कर्तृत्वं नाम यत् तस्य स्वातन्त्र्यपरिबृंहितम् |
ऐश्वर्यं नाम तत् प्रोक्तं गुणतत्त्वार्थचिन्तकैः || 2-58 ||
1.1.m: Its agency, which is enriched by independence, / is proclaimed as sovereignty by the contemplators of the truth of the attributes. || 2-58
Definition of the nature of strength

1.1.s: śramahānistu yā tasya satataṃ kurvato jagat |
1.1.d: श्रमहानिस्तु या तस्य सततं कुर्वतो जगत् |
1.1.m: Its absence of fatigue, on the other hand, as it continually creates the universe,

1.1.s: p. 20) balaṃ nāma guṇastasya kathito guṇacintakaiḥ || 2-59 ||
1.1.d: प्. 20) बलं नाम गुणस्तस्य कथितो गुणचिन्तकैः || 2-59 ||
1.1.m: is declared by the contemplators of the attributes to be its attribute of strength. || 2-59
Definition of the nature of virility

1.1.s:
tasyopādānabhāve'pi vikāraviraho hi yaḥ |
vīryaṃ nāma guṇaḥ so'yamacyutatvāparāhvayam || 2-60 ||
1.1.d:
तस्योपादानभावेऽपि विकारविरहो हि यः |
वीर्यं नाम गुणः सोऽयमच्युतत्वापराह्वयम् || 2-60 ||
1.1.m: Its freedom from modification even while being the material cause / is the attribute called virility, whose other name is unswervingness. || 2-60
Definition of the nature of splendour
Its non-dependence on auxiliary causes is declared to be splendour.
The five attributes beginning with power are modes of the attribute of knowledge

1.1.s: ete śaktyādayaḥ pañca guṇā jñānasya kīrtitāḥ || 2-61 ||
1.1.d: एते शक्त्यादयः पञ्च गुणा ज्ञानस्य कीर्तिताः || 2-61 ||
1.1.m: These five attributes beginning with power are declared to belong to knowledge. || 2-61

1.1.s:
jñānameva paraṃ rūpaṃ brahmaṇaḥ paramātmanaḥ |
ṣāḍguṇyaṃ tat paraṃ brahma svaśaktiparibṛṃhitam |
bahu syāmiti saṃkalpaṃ bhajate tat sudarśanam || 2-62 ||
1.1.d:
ज्ञानमेव परं रूपं ब्रह्मणः परमात्मनः |
षाड्गुण्यं तत् परं ब्रह्म स्वशक्तिपरिबृंहितम् |
बहु स्यामिति संकल्पं भजते तत् सुदर्शनम् || 2-62 ||
1.1.m: Knowledge alone is the supreme form of Brahman, the Paramātman; / that supreme Brahman possessing the six attributes, augmented by its own Śakti, / adopts the creative resolve “May I become many,” which is Sudarśana. || 2-62

1.1.s:
iti śrīpāñcarātre tantrarahasye ahirbudhnyasaṃhitāyāṃ
ṣāḍguṇyabrahmaviveko nāma dvitīyo'dhyāyaḥ || 2 ||
1.1.d:
इति श्रीपाञ्चरात्रे तन्त्ररहस्ये अहिर्बुध्न्यसंहितायां
षाड्गुण्यब्रह्मविवेको नाम द्वितीयोऽध्यायः || 2 ||
1.1.m: Thus ends the second chapter, titled “Discrimination of the Brahman Possessing the Six Attributes,” in the Ahirbudhnyasaṃhitā of the esoteric Tantra in the venerable Pāñcarātra. || 2
Chapter Three, titled “Summary of the Universal Form”

1.1.s:
ṣāḍguṇyaṃ tat kathaṃ brahma svaśaktiparibṛṃhitam |
tasya śaktiśca kā nāma yayā bṛṃhitamucyate || 3-1 ||
1.1.d:
षाड्गुण्यं तत् कथं ब्रह्म स्वशक्तिपरिबृंहितम् |
तस्य शक्तिश्च का नाम यया बृंहितमुच्यते || 3-1 ||
1.1.m: How is that Brahman possessed of six attributes augmented by its own Śakti? / And what is its Śakti by which it is said to be augmented? || 3-1
The power of all entities is an inseparably related attribute

1.1.s:
śaktayaḥ sarvabhāvānāmacintyā apṛthaksthitāḥ |
svarūpe naiva dṛśyante dṛśyante kāryatastu tāḥ || 3-2 ||
1.1.d:
शक्तयः सर्वभावानामचिन्त्या अपृथक्स्थिताः |
स्वरूपे नैव दृश्यन्ते दृश्यन्ते कार्यतस्तु ताः || 3-2 ||
1.1.m: The powers of all entities are inconceivable and exist inseparably; / they are not seen in their essential nature, but they are seen from their effects. || 3-2

1.1.s:
sūkṣmāvasthā hi sā teṣāṃ sarvabhāvānugāminī |
idaṃtayā vidhātuṃ sā na niṣeddhuṃ ca śakyate || 3-3 ||
1.1.d:
सूक्ष्मावस्था हि सा तेषां सर्वभावानुगामिनी |
इदंतया विधातुं सा न निषेद्धुं च शक्यते || 3-3 ||
1.1.m: For it is their subtle state, accompanying all entities; / it can neither be affirmed nor denied as “this.” || 3-3
Powers are beyond questioning
For the powers pertaining to entities are beyond questioning by anyone.
The power of the supreme Brahman is also an inseparably related attribute
In this same way, O sage, of that Bhagavān, the supreme Brahman, || 3-4
Śakti accompanies all entities, like moonlight [belongs to] the cool-rayed moon;
it accompanies being and non-being, effecting all the works of the all-pervading Lord. || 3-5

1.1.s:
svātantryarūpā sā viṣṇoḥ prasphurattā jaganmayī |
uditānuditākārā nimeṣonmeṣarūpiṇī || 3-6 ||
1.1.d:
स्वातन्त्र्यरूपा सा विष्णोः प्रस्फुरत्ता जगन्मयी |
उदितानुदिताकारा निमेषोन्मेषरूपिणी || 3-6 ||
1.1.m: It is the independent flashing forth of Viṣṇu, consisting of the universe; / having arisen and unarisen forms, having the nature of closing and opening. || 3-6
The Śakti of the Bhagavān is designated by words such as bliss
Because of its non-dependence it is Bliss; it is independent because of eternal fullness; / the existence of the higher and lower universe unfolds on the canvas of its own self. || 3-7

1.1.s:
nityā kālāparicchedāt pūrṇākārāviyogataḥ |
vyāpinī deśavibhraṃśādriktā pūrṇā ca sarvadā || 3-8 ||
1.1.d:
नित्या कालापरिच्छेदात् पूर्णाकारावियोगतः |
व्यापिनी देशविभ्रंशाद्रिक्ता पूर्णा च सर्वदा || 3-8 ||
1.1.m: It is eternal because it is unbounded by time, never parting from its full form; / it is all-pervading, void of spatial lapse, and always full. || 3-8

1.1.s:
jagattayā lakṣyamāṇā sā lakṣmīriti gīyate |
śrayantī vaiṣṇavaṃ bhāvaṃ sā śrīriti nigadyate || 3-9 ||
1.1.d:
जगत्तया लक्ष्यमाणा सा लक्ष्मीरिति गीयते |
श्रयन्ती वैष्णवं भावं सा श्रीरिति निगद्यते || 3-9 ||
1.1.m: Because it is perceived as the universe, it is called Lakṣmī; / resorting to the condition of Viṣṇu, it is named Śrī. || 3-9

1.1.s:
avyaktakālapuṃbhāvāt sā padmā padmamālinī |
kāmadānācca kamalā paryāptasukhayogataḥ || 3-10 ||
1.1.d:
अव्यक्तकालपुंभावात् सा पद्मा पद्ममालिनी |
कामदानाच्च कमला पर्याप्तसुखयोगतः || 3-10 ||
1.1.m: Because of the unmanifest nature of time and the male soul, it is Padmā garlanded with lotuses; / and because it grants desires through the possession of ample joy, it is Kamalā. || 3-10

1.1.s:
viṣṇoḥ sāmarthyarūpatvād viṣṇuśaktiḥ pragīyate |
pālayantī harerbhāvaṃ viṣṇupatnī prakīrtitā || 3-11 ||
1.1.d:
विष्णोः सामर्थ्यरूपत्वाद् विष्णुशक्तिः प्रगीयते |
पालयन्ती हरेर्भावं विष्णुपत्नी प्रकीर्तिता || 3-11 ||
1.1.m: Because it has the nature of Viṣṇu's capacity, it is celebrated as the Śakti of Viṣṇu; / protecting the essential nature of Hari, it is proclaimed to be the consort of Viṣṇu. || 3-11

1.1.s:
jagadākārasaṃkocāt smṛtā kuṇḍalinī budhaiḥ |
anāhatā budhaiḥ proktā manovāgādyanāhateḥ || 3-12 ||
1.1.d:
जगदाकारसंकोचात् स्मृता कुण्डलिनी बुधैः |
अनाहता बुधैः प्रोक्ता मनोवागाद्यनाहतेः || 3-12 ||
1.1.m: Because of the contraction of the form of the universe, it is called Kuṇḍalinī by the wise; / it is called Anāhatā by the wise because it is unstruck by mind, speech, and the like. || 3-12
Through consciousness of supreme bliss, and because of the subtlety of mantras,
[and] from resting upon pure sattva, [she is] Gaurī; and indeed [she is] Aditi because she is without distinction. || 3-13

1.1.s:
sarvapuṇyakarībhāvānmahīyasyapi sā mahī |
tathānāhataśīrṣṇī cānāhato'bhyudayo yataḥ || 3-14 ||
1.1.d:
सर्वपुण्यकरीभावान्महीयस्यपि सा मही |
तथानाहतशीर्ष्णी चानाहतोऽभ्युदयो यतः || 3-14 ||
1.1.m: Because she brings about all virtue, and because she is most exalted, she is Mahī; / and she is also Anāhataśīrṣṇī, since her manifestation is unstruck. || 3-14

1.1.s:
prāṇayantī svasaṃvittyā jagatprāṇā itīryate |
parāhatāsurūpatvānmantramātā prakīrtitā || 3-15 ||
1.1.d:
प्राणयन्ती स्वसंवित्त्या जगत्प्राणा इतीर्यते |
पराहतासुरूपत्वान्मन्त्रमाता प्रकीर्तिता || 3-15 ||
1.1.m: Enlivening through her own consciousness, she is called Jagatprāṇā; / because her form strikes down demons from above, she is proclaimed as Mantramātā. || 3-15

1.1.s:
trāyantī gāyataḥ sarvān gāyattrītyabhidhīyate |
prakurvatī jagat svena prakṛtiḥ parigīyate || 3-16 ||
1.1.d:
त्रायन्ती गायतः सर्वान् गायत्त्रीत्यभिधीयते |
प्रकुर्वती जगत् स्वेन प्रकृतिः परिगीयते || 3-16 ||
1.1.m: Protecting all who sing [her praise], she is called Gāyatrī; / producing the universe by her own power, she is celebrated as Prakṛti. || 3-16

1.1.s:
mimīte ca tatā ceti sā mātā parikīrtitā |
sarveṣāmaviparyāsācchivaṃkaratayā śivā || 3-17 ||
1.1.d:
मिमीते च तता चेति सा माता परिकीर्तिता |
सर्वेषामविपर्यासाच्छिवंकरतया शिवा || 3-17 ||
1.1.m: Because she measures out and is extended, she is proclaimed as Mātā; / because of the absence of error in all things and by bringing about auspiciousness, she is Śivā. || 3-17

1.1.s:
taruṇī kāmyamānatvāt tārā saṃsāratāraṇāt |
aviparyāsarūpatvāt satyā satyadvayānvayāt || 3-18 ||
1.1.d:
तरुणी काम्यमानत्वात् तारा संसारतारणात् |
अविपर्यासरूपत्वात् सत्या सत्यद्वयान्वयात् || 3-18 ||
1.1.m: She is Taruṇī because she is desired; Tārā because she carries across worldly existence; / Satyā because her nature is without delusion, through connection with the two truths. || 3-18

1.1.s:
śāntāśeṣavikāratvācchāntā sā cintyate budhaiḥ |
mohānapanayantī sā mohinī mohanādapi || 3-19 ||
1.1.d:
शान्ताशेषविकारत्वाच्छान्ता सा चिन्त्यते बुधैः |
मोहानपनयन्ती सा मोहिनी मोहनादपि || 3-19 ||
1.1.m: Because all modifications are stilled, she is contemplated by the wise as Śāntā; / not removing delusion, and also through deluding, she is Mohinī. || 3-19

1.1.s:
iḍā haviradhiṣṭhānādiṣyamāṇatayāpi ca |
ramayantīti sā rantī ratiśca parikīrtitā || 3-20 ||
1.1.d:
इडा हविरधिष्ठानादिष्यमाणतयापि च |
रमयन्तीति सा रन्ती रतिश्च परिकीर्तिता || 3-20 ||
1.1.m: She is Iḍā as the substratum of the oblation, and also because she is longed for; / delighting, she is proclaimed as Rantī and Rati. || 3-20
Known to the virtuous as Viśruti; reminding, [she is] Sarasvatī; / because her light is uncurtailed, she is called Mahābhāsā. || 3-21
By these various significant names, based upon various treatises,
her entire glory is displayed: the supreme power of Viṣṇu. || 3-22

1.1.s:
udadheriva ca sthairyaṃ mahatteva vihāyasaḥ |
prabheva divaseśasya jyotsneva himadīdhiteḥ || 3-23 ||
1.1.d:
उदधेरिव च स्थैर्यं महत्तेव विहायसः |
प्रभेव दिवसेशस्य ज्योत्स्नेव हिमदीधितेः || 3-23 ||
1.1.m: As stillness belongs to the ocean, as vastness belongs to the sky, / as radiance belongs to the sun, as moonlight belongs to the moon, || 3-23

1.1.s:
viṣṇoḥ sarvāṅgasaṃpūrṇā bhāvābhāvānugāminī |
śaktirnārāyaṇī divyā sarvasiddhāntasaṃmatā || 3-24 ||
1.1.d:
विष्णोः सर्वाङ्गसंपूर्णा भावाभावानुगामिनी |
शक्तिर्नारायणी दिव्या सर्वसिद्धान्तसंमता || 3-24 ||
1.1.m: so the divine Śakti of Viṣṇu, complete in all her limbs, accompanying [both] presence and absence, / is called Nārāyaṇī, agreed upon by all established doctrines. || 3-24
The distinction of Śakti from the possessor of Śakti

1.1.s:
devācchaktimato bhinnā brahmaṇaḥ parameṣṭhinaḥ |
eṣa caiṣā ca śāstreṣu dharmadharmisvabhāvataḥ || 3-25 ||
1.1.d:
देवाच्छक्तिमतो भिन्ना ब्रह्मणः परमेष्ठिनः |
एष चैषा च शास्त्रेषु धर्मधर्मिस्वभावतः || 3-25 ||
1.1.m: Distinct from the god who possesses Śakti, from Brahman, the Supreme Lord, / this male and this female are spoken of in the scriptures through the nature of property and property-bearer, || 3-25
as if a single principle in the form of becoming and being. / In her independent nature, this consort of Viṣṇu is wondrous, || 3-26
from whom, about to become the universe, an awakening flashes forth somewhere.
The twofold nature of Śakti and threefold nature of Bhūtiśakti
A portion of an arbuda of crores upon crores of streams of thousands and tens of thousands of crores, || 3-27

1.1.s:
lakṣmīmayaḥ samunmeṣaḥ sa dvidhā vyavatiṣṭhate |
kriyābhūtivibhedena bhūtiḥ sā ca tridhā matā || 3-28 ||
1.1.d:
लक्ष्मीमयः समुन्मेषः स द्विधा व्यवतिष्ठते |
क्रियाभूतिविभेदेन भूतिः सा च त्रिधा मता || 3-28 ||
1.1.m: that awakening consisting of Lakṣmī abides in two ways: / through the division into kriyā and bhūti; and that bhūti is considered threefold, || 3-28
through the states of the unmanifest, time, and the male soul. Their forms will be declared.
The power of action as the propeller of the power of becoming
This awakening called action is that which impels becoming. || 3-29

1.1.s:
lakṣmīmayaḥ prāṇarūpo viṣṇoḥ saṃkalpa ucyate |
svātantryamūla icchātmā prekṣārūpaḥ kriyāphalaḥ || 3-30 ||
1.1.d:
लक्ष्मीमयः प्राणरूपो विष्णोः संकल्प उच्यते |
स्वातन्त्र्यमूल इच्छात्मा प्रेक्षारूपः क्रियाफलः || 3-30 ||
1.1.m: Consisting of Lakṣmī, having the nature of life-breath, it is called the creative resolve of Viṣṇu; / rooted in independence, essentially desire, having the nature of foresight, having action as its fruit. || 3-30

1.1.s:
unmeṣo yaḥ susaṃkalpaḥ sarvatrāvyāhataḥ kṛtau |
avyaktakālapuṃrūpāṃ cetanācetanātmikām || 3-31 ||
1.1.d:
उन्मेषो यः सुसंकल्पः सर्वत्राव्याहतः कृतौ |
अव्यक्तकालपुंरूपां चेतनाचेतनात्मिकाम् || 3-31 ||
1.1.m: The awakening which is the auspicious creative resolve, unhindered everywhere in execution, / brings into manifestation the becoming consisting of Lakṣmī, the Śakti of Viṣṇu, || 3-31

1.1.s:
bhūtiṃ lakṣmīmayīṃ viṣṇoḥ śaktiṃ saṃbhāvayatyasau |
avyaktaṃ pariṇāmena kālaṃ kalanakarmaṇā || 3-32 ||
1.1.d:
भूतिं लक्ष्मीमयीं विष्णोः शक्तिं संभावयत्यसौ |
अव्यक्तं परिणामेन कालं कलनकर्मणा || 3-32 ||
1.1.m: which consists of the conscious and the unconscious, taking the form of the unmanifest, time, and the male soul: / the unmanifest through transformation, time through the activity of enumeration, || 3-32

1.1.s:
puruṣaṃ bhojanodyogaiḥ sarge saṃyojayatyayam |
sāmarthyatritayādānād viyojayati saṃcare || 3-33 ||
1.1.d:
पुरुषं भोजनोद्योगैः सर्गे संयोजयत्ययम् |
सामर्थ्यत्रितयादानाद् वियोजयति संचरे || 3-33 ||
1.1.m: and it unites the soul with the exertions of experience at creation; / and through the withdrawal of the triad of capacities, it disunites them at cosmic dissolution. || 3-33

1.1.s:
viṣame pariṇāme yat sāmarthyaṃ triguṇātmanaḥ |
sṛṣṭau dadhāti tat tasmin viparyāsaṃ ca saṃhṛtau || 3-34 ||
1.1.d:
विषमे परिणामे यत् सामर्थ्यं त्रिगुणात्मनः |
सृष्टौ दधाति तत् तस्मिन् विपर्यासं च संहृतौ || 3-34 ||
1.1.m: Whatever capacity belongs to that which consists of the three guṇas in unequal transformation, / it establishes that in it during creation, and the reverse at dissolution. || 3-34

1.1.s:
avyaktapuruṣodyogasaṃyojanavidhikramam |
kāle dadhāti sargādau viparyāsaṃ ca saṃhṛtau || 3-35 ||
1.1.d:
अव्यक्तपुरुषोद्योगसंयोजनविधिक्रमम् |
काले दधाति सर्गादौ विपर्यासं च संहृतौ || 3-35 ||
1.1.m: The order of rule for joining the efforts of the unmanifest and the soul / it establishes in time at the beginning of creation, and the reverse at dissolution. || 3-35

1.1.s:
puṃsaśca vuddhisāmarthyamasāmarthyaṃ ca bhojane |
saṃkalpaḥ kurute viṣṇoḥ sargaprativisargayoḥ || 3-36 ||
1.1.d:
पुंसश्च वुद्धिसामर्थ्यमसामर्थ्यं च भोजने |
संकल्पः कुरुते विष्णोः सर्गप्रतिविसर्गयोः || 3-36 ||
1.1.m: And the capacity of intellect for the soul, and its incapacity in experience, / the creative resolve of Viṣṇu produces at creation and dissolution. || 3-36

1.1.s:
trīnetān saṃhatān sṛṣṭau vihatān pratisaṃcare |
dadhāti svena rūpeṇa guṇo maṇigaṇāniva || 3-37 ||
1.1.d:
त्रीनेतान् संहतान् सृष्टौ विहतान् प्रतिसंचरे |
दधाति स्वेन रूपेण गुणो मणिगणानिव || 3-37 ||
1.1.m: These three, conjoined at creation and dispersed at dissolution, / it holds by its own nature, as a thread [holds] a multitude of gems. || 3-37

1.1.s: sthitau ca kurute rakṣāṃ teṣāṃ kāryasamīkṣaṇāt |
1.1.d: स्थितौ च कुरुते रक्षां तेषां कार्यसमीक्षणात् |
1.1.m: And during maintenance it provides protection by overseeing their functions.
That which is unhindered everywhere is the distinguishing characteristic of Sudarśana. || 3-38
The conformability of the power of action to all entities through manifold forms

1.1.s:
so'yaṃ sudarśanaṃ nāma saṃkalpaḥ spandanātmakaḥ |
vibhajya bahudhā rūpaṃ bhāve bhāve'vatiṣṭhate || 3-39 ||
1.1.d:
सोऽयं सुदर्शनं नाम संकल्पः स्पन्दनात्मकः |
विभज्य बहुधा रूपं भावे भावेऽवतिष्ठते || 3-39 ||
1.1.m: This very creative resolve named Sudarśana, whose nature is pulsation, / dividing its form manifoldly, abides in each and every entity. || 3-39
Elaboration of the manifold forms

1.1.s:
vyāptiṃ sudarśanasyemāṃ procyamānāṃ mayā śṛṇu |
yajjñātvā puruṣo loke kṛtakṛtyatvamaśnute || 3-40 ||
1.1.d:
व्याप्तिं सुदर्शनस्येमां प्रोच्यमानां मया शृणु |
यज्ज्ञात्वा पुरुषो लोके कृतकृत्यत्वमश्नुते || 3-40 ||
1.1.m: Hear from me as it is declared, this all-pervasiveness of Sudarśana, / knowing which a man attains the state of having accomplished his purpose in the world. || 3-40

1.1.s:
ṣāḍguṇyaṃ yat paraṃ brahma yā gatiryogināṃ parā |
nārāyaṇaḥ sa viśvātmā bhāvābhāvamidaṃ jagat || 3-41 ||
1.1.d:
षाड्गुण्यं यत् परं ब्रह्म या गतिर्योगिनां परा |
नारायणः स विश्वात्मा भावाभावमिदं जगत् || 3-41 ||
1.1.m: That supreme Brahman possessing the six attributes, which is the highest goal of yogins, / is Nārāyaṇa, the self of the universe. This universe, consisting of being and non-being, || 3-41

1.1.s:
niṣkalena svarūpeṇa yadā prāpya niyacchati |
sadā sattā hi yā tasya jagannirmāṇaśaktikā || 3-42 ||
1.1.d:
निष्कलेन स्वरूपेण यदा प्राप्य नियच्छति |
सदा सत्ता हि या तस्य जगन्निर्माणशक्तिका || 3-42 ||
1.1.m: when he pervades and regulates through his partless essential form, / his eternal being is indeed the power that creates the universe. || 3-42

1.1.s:
sarvabhāvātmikā lakṣmīrahaṃtā paramātmanaḥ |
taddharmadharmiṇī devī bhūtvā sarvamidaṃ jagat || 3-43 ||
1.1.d:
सर्वभावात्मिका लक्ष्मीरहंता परमात्मनः |
तद्धर्मधर्मिणी देवी भूत्वा सर्वमिदं जगत् || 3-43 ||
1.1.m: Lakṣmī, the I-ness of the Paramātman, identical with all entities, / becoming this whole universe as the goddess who is property and property-bearer, || 3-43

1.1.s:
niṣkalena svarūpeṇa sāpi tadvanniyacchati |
tadīyaikā kalā bhūtirjagadbhavanasaṃjñitā || 3-44 ||
1.1.d:
निष्कलेन स्वरूपेण सापि तद्वन्नियच्छति |
तदीयैका कला भूतिर्जगद्भवनसंज्ञिता || 3-44 ||
1.1.m: she too likewise regulates through her partless essential form. / A single portion of hers is the becoming named 'world-becoming'. || 3-44

1.1.s:
vyāpāro vāstavastatra jaganniyamanātmakaḥ |
niṣkalā yā kriyāśaktirlakṣmyāḥ saudarśanī kalā || 3-45 ||
1.1.d:
व्यापारो वास्तवस्तत्र जगन्नियमनात्मकः |
निष्कला या क्रियाशक्तिर्लक्ष्म्याः सौदर्शनी कला || 3-45 ||
1.1.m: The actual function there consists of the regulation of the universe: / the partless power of action of Lakṣmī is the portion pertaining to Sudarśana. || 3-45

1.1.s:
p. 27) bhajete tau yadā rūpaṃ manonayananandanam |
rakṣāyai jagatāmīśau cakrapadme tadā kriyā || 3-46 ||
1.1.d:
प्. 27) भजेते तौ यदा रूपं मनोनयननन्दनम् |
रक्षायै जगतामीशौ चक्रपद्मे तदा क्रिया || 3-46 ||
1.1.m: When the two rulers assume a form that delights the mind and eyes / for the protection of the worlds, then action is the discus and the lotus. || 3-46

1.1.s:
rakṣopakaraṇaṃ devau tau yāvadyāvadicchataḥ |
śaṅkhaśārṅgādirūpeṇa tāvat tāvat sudarśanam || 3-47 ||
1.1.d:
रक्षोपकरणं देवौ तौ यावद्यावदिच्छतः |
शङ्खशार्ङ्गादिरूपेण तावत् तावत् सुदर्शनम् || 3-47 ||
1.1.m: To whatever extent the two deities desire instruments of protection, / to that extent Sudarśana takes the form of the conch, the bow Śārṅga, and the rest. || 3-47
When they wish to benefit the universe through light, delight, and falling [heat], / then the Sudarśana discus takes the form of sun, moon, and fire. || 3-48

1.1.s:
devadaityādikān bhāvān yadā tau bhajataḥ svayam |
tattadastramayī devī tadā saudarśanī kriyā || 3-49 ||
1.1.d:
देवदैत्यादिकान् भावान् यदा तौ भजतः स्वयम् |
तत्तदस्त्रमयी देवी तदा सौदर्शनी क्रिया || 3-49 ||
1.1.m: When they themselves assume states such as gods and daityas, / then the action pertaining to Sudarśana is the goddess consisting of those respective missile weapons. || 3-49

1.1.s:
yadā viśvopakārāya śāstraṃ nānāphalāśrayam |
kurutaḥ sā kriyā tatra śāsanaṃ hṛdayasthitam || 3-50 ||
1.1.d:
यदा विश्वोपकाराय शास्त्रं नानाफलाश्रयम् |
कुरुतः सा क्रिया तत्र शासनं हृदयस्थितम् || 3-50 ||
1.1.m: When for the benefit of the universe they compose scripture, which rests on various fruits, / there that action is the instruction abiding in the heart. || 3-50

1.1.s:
yadā tau bhavataḥ śāstraṃ viśvopakṛtaye vibhū |
tadā sā śāstratātparyaṃ kriyā saudarśanī kalā || 3-51 ||
1.1.d:
यदा तौ भवतः शास्त्रं विश्वोपकृतये विभू |
तदा सा शास्त्रतात्पर्यं क्रिया सौदर्शनी कला || 3-51 ||
1.1.m: When the two all-pervading lords become scripture for the benefit of the universe, / then that action, the portion pertaining to Sudarśana, is the purport of scripture. || 3-51

1.1.s:
śāstrādhikāriṇo nāma yadā tau pitarau dhruvau |
adhikārastadā teṣāṃ kriyāśaktiḥ sudarśanam || 3-52 ||
1.1.d:
शास्त्राधिकारिणो नाम यदा तौ पितरौ ध्रुवौ |
अधिकारस्तदा तेषां क्रियाशक्तिः सुदर्शनम् || 3-52 ||
1.1.m: When the two constant parents are [the source of] qualified recipients of scripture, / then their qualification is the power of action, Sudarśana. || 3-52

1.1.s:
yadā śāstrārthabhūtau tau phalasādhanasaṃśrayāt |
phalaprasavasāmarthyaṃ kriyā tatra sudarśanam || 3-53 ||
1.1.d:
यदा शास्त्रार्थभूतौ तौ फलसाधनसंश्रयात् |
फलप्रसवसामर्थ्यं क्रिया तत्र सुदर्शनम् || 3-53 ||
1.1.m: When the two become the subject-matter of scripture through recourse to means and results, / there action is Sudarśana as the capacity to generate the result. || 3-53

1.1.s:
puruṣārthāstu catvāro yadā tau bhavataḥ svayam |
ātmatarpaṇasāmarthyaṃ tadā cakraṃ sudarśanam || 3-54 ||
1.1.d:
पुरुषार्थास्तु चत्वारो यदा तौ भवतः स्वयम् |
आत्मतर्पणसामर्थ्यं तदा चक्रं सुदर्शनम् || 3-54 ||
1.1.m: When they themselves become the four aims of human life, / then the Sudarśana discus is the capacity to satisfy the self. || 3-54

1.1.s:
p. 28) yadā mantramayīṃ rakṣāṃ bhajato jagatāṃ hite |
mantrayantramayī devī kriyāśaktistadā tviyam || 3-55 ||
1.1.d:
प्. 28) यदा मन्त्रमयीं रक्षां भजतो जगतां हिते |
मन्त्रयन्त्रमयी देवी क्रियाशक्तिस्तदा त्वियम् || 3-55 ||
1.1.m: When for the welfare of the worlds they resort to protection consisting of mantras, / then this power of action is the goddess consisting of mantras and yantras. || 3-55

1.1.s:
vaiśvarūpyasya saṃkṣepaḥ kriyāśakteḥ pradarśitaḥ |
sudarśanātmikāyāste kiṃ bhūyaḥ śrotumicchasi || 3-56 ||
1.1.d:
वैश्वरूप्यस्य संक्षेपः क्रियाशक्तेः प्रदर्शितः |
सुदर्शनात्मिकायास्ते किं भूयः श्रोतुमिच्छसि || 3-56 ||
1.1.m:
A summary of the universal form of the power of action has been shown to you,
which consists of Sudarśana. What more do you wish to hear? || 3-56

1.1.s:
iti śrīpāñcarātre tantrarahasye ahirbudhnyasaṃhitāyāṃ
kriyāśaktervaiśvarūpyapradarśanaṃ nāma tṛtīyo'dhyāyaḥ || 3 ||
1.1.d:
इति श्रीपाञ्चरात्रे तन्त्ररहस्ये अहिर्बुध्न्यसंहितायां
क्रियाशक्तेर्वैश्वरूप्यप्रदर्शनं नाम तृतीयोऽध्यायः || 3 ||
1.1.m:
Thus ends the third chapter, named 'Demonstration of the Universal Form of the Power of Action',
in the Ahirbudhnyasaṃhitā in the secret teachings of the tantra of the venerable Pāñcarātra. || 3
Chapter Four, named 'Description of Cosmic Dissolution'

1.1.s:
bhagavan devadeveśa sarvajña vṛṣaketana |
kiṃ tat kāraṇamityuktaṃ sṛṣṭaye yat pravartate || 4-1 ||
1.1.d:
भगवन् देवदेवेश सर्वज्ञ वृषकेतन |
किं तत् कारणमित्युक्तं सृष्टये यत् प्रवर्तते || 4-1 ||
1.1.m:
O Bhagavān, lord of the gods of gods, all-knowing one, whose banner is the bull!
What is that cause, so called, which proceeds toward creation? || 4-1

1.1.s:
sudarśanena yad vyāptaṃ rūpataḥ kāryato'rthataḥ |
vistareṇa mamācakṣva jagataḥ kāraṇaṃ param || 4-2 ||
1.1.d:
सुदर्शनेन यद् व्याप्तं रूपतः कार्यतोऽर्थतः |
विस्तरेण ममाचक्ष्व जगतः कारणं परम् || 4-2 ||
1.1.m:
Which is pervaded by Sudarśana through its form, effect, and reality—
explain to me in detail the supreme cause of the world. || 4-2
Description of the Dissolution into Prakṛti

1.1.s:
procyamānaṃ mayā tattvaṃ kāraṇasyāvadhāraya |
tatra tāvannibodhemaṃ prākṛtaṃ pratisaṃcaram || 4-3 ||
1.1.d:
प्रोच्यमानं मया तत्त्वं कारणस्यावधारय |
तत्र तावन्निबोधेमं प्राकृतं प्रतिसंचरम् || 4-3 ||
1.1.m:
Understand the true nature of the cause as it is being spoken by me;
first, comprehend this cosmic dissolution into Prakṛti: || 4-3

1.1.s:
yena kālena sā vidyā prakṛtirmūlasaṃjñitā |
sasyādisṛṣṭaye dhenurabhavanmegharūpiṇī || 4-4 ||
1.1.d:
येन कालेन सा विद्या प्रकृतिर्मूलसंज्ञिता |
सस्यादिसृष्टये धेनुरभवन्मेघरूपिणी || 4-4 ||
1.1.m:
During that time when that knowledge-principle, the Prakṛti termed the primal source,
became a cow in the form of clouds for the creation of crops and other things, || 4-4

1.1.s:
kālena tāvatā sā tu cikīrṣye pratisaṃcare |
adhenurnīrasā śuṣkā bhavatyavyaktasaṃjñitā || 4-5 ||
1.1.d:
कालेन तावता सा तु चिकीर्ष्ये प्रतिसंचरे |
अधेनुर्नीरसा शुष्का भवत्यव्यक्तसंज्ञिता || 4-5 ||
1.1.m:
by that same duration, when the cosmic dissolution is willed,
she becomes a barren cow, sapless, dry, termed the Unmanifest. || 4-5

1.1.s: kālena kiyatā sargaḥ sā dhenuḥ kāmarūpinī |
1.1.d: कालेन कियता सर्गः सा धेनुः कामरूपिनी |
1.1.m: For how long is the creation, she being a cow that takes form at will,

1.1.s: p. 30) adhenuḥ sā bhaved devī yāvatā pratisaṃcare || 4-6 ||
1.1.d: प्. 30) अधेनुः सा भवेद् देवी यावता प्रतिसंचरे || 4-6 ||
1.1.m: and for how long does she become a barren cow, the goddess in cosmic dissolution? || 4-6
Duration of Time for Cosmic Dissolution

1.1.s:
aṣṭādaśa nimeṣāstu kāṣṭhā triṃśattu tāḥ kalā |
tāstu triṃśat kṣaṇaste tu muhūrto dvādaśa smṛtaḥ || 4-7 ||
1.1.d:
अष्टादश निमेषास्तु काष्ठा त्रिंशत्तु ताः कला |
तास्तु त्रिंशत् क्षणस्ते तु मुहूर्तो द्वादश स्मृतः || 4-7 ||
1.1.m:
Eighteen twinklings of an eye are a kāṣṭhā, thirty of those are a kalā;
thirty of those are a kṣaṇa, and twelve of those are considered a muhūrta. || 4-7

1.1.s:
te tu pañcadaśāhaḥ syāt tāvatī rātririṣyate |
te pañcadaśa pakṣaḥ syāt pakṣau dvau māsa iṣyate || 4-8 ||
1.1.d:
ते तु पञ्चदशाहः स्यात् तावती रात्रिरिष्यते |
ते पञ्चदश पक्षः स्यात् पक्षौ द्वौ मास इष्यते || 4-8 ||
1.1.m:
Fifteen of those would be a day, and the night is held to be of equal length;
fifteen of them would be a fortnight, and two fortnights are considered a month. || 4-8

1.1.s:
saṃvatsaro mānuṣastu tairdvādaśabhiriṣyate |
kāmyaḥ ṣoḍaśabhistaistu kāmyābdānāṃ tathā mune || 4-9 ||
1.1.d:
संवत्सरो मानुषस्तु तैर्द्वादशभिरिष्यते |
काम्यः षोडशभिस्तैस्तु काम्याब्दानां तथा मुने || 4-9 ||
1.1.m:
A human year is considered to consist of twelve of them;
a desire-born year consists of sixteen of them, and likewise of desire-born years, O sage: || 4-9

1.1.s:
vidyā dhenuradhenuśca bhavet kālena tāvatā |
adhenvāṃ tu tatastasyāṃ cikīrṣye pratisaṃcare || 4-10 ||
1.1.d:
विद्या धेनुरधेनुश्च भवेत् कालेन तावता |
अधेन्वां तु ततस्तस्यां चिकीर्ष्ये प्रतिसंचरे || 4-10 ||
1.1.m:
the knowledge-principle becomes a milch cow and a barren cow during that duration of time.
Then, when she has become a barren cow, when the cosmic dissolution is willed, || 4-10
Dissolution of Everything into Earth

1.1.s:
nīrasaṃ śuṣkamevāsījjagadetaccarācaram |
mahāvātena saṃśuṣkaṃ saṃdagdhaṃ ca mahāgninā || 4-11 ||
1.1.d:
नीरसं शुष्कमेवासीज्जगदेतच्चराचरम् |
महावातेन संशुष्कं संदग्धं च महाग्निना || 4-11 ||
1.1.m:
this world, moving and unmoving, became sapless and utterly dried up,
parched by a great wind and scorched by a great fire. || 4-11

1.1.s:
ā śailādā tṛṇāccaiva yadā bhūmau samunnatam |
mānaveṣu layaṃ yānti tadā mānavamānavāḥ || 4-12 ||
1.1.d:
आ शैलादा तृणाच्चैव यदा भूमौ समुन्नतम् |
मानवेषु लयं यान्ति तदा मानवमानवाः || 4-12 ||
1.1.m:
From the mountain down to the blade of grass, whatever has risen up on earth—
then the humans of Manu dissolve into the Manus. || 4-12

1.1.s:
p. 31) manuṣveva layaṃ yānti mānavāste catuḥśatam |
evaṃ cetanavarge tu manuṣveva layaṃ gate || 4-13 ||
1.1.d:
प्. 31) मनुष्वेव लयं यान्ति मानवास्ते चतुःशतम् |
एवं चेतनवर्गे तु मनुष्वेव लयं गते || 4-13 ||
1.1.m:
Those four hundred humans dissolve into the Manus alone;
when the conscious category has thus dissolved into the Manus alone, || 4-13

1.1.s:
mithunānyeva catvāri manūnāṃ kevalāni tu |
kūrmapṛṣṭhasamānāyāṃ bhuvi tiṣṭhanti vai mune || 4-14 ||
1.1.d:
मिथुनान्येव चत्वारि मनूनां केवलानि तु |
कूर्मपृष्ठसमानायां भुवि तिष्ठन्ति वै मुने || 4-14 ||
1.1.m:
only four pairs of Manus
remain upon the earth, which resembles the back of a tortoise, O sage. || 4-14

1.1.s:
nārāyaṇasya saṃkalpādavyāhatasudarśanāt |
bhūmergandhātmakaṃ sāraṃ grasantyāpastadā mune || 4-15 ||
1.1.d:
नारायणस्य संकल्पादव्याहतसुदर्शनात् |
भूमेर्गन्धात्मकं सारं ग्रसन्त्यापस्तदा मुने || 4-15 ||
1.1.m:
By the creative resolve of Nārāyaṇa, which is unimpeded Sudarśana,
the waters then devour the essence of earth, which consists of smell, O sage. || 4-15

1.1.s:
āttagandhā yadā bhūmirambhasā kāraṇātmanā |
atibhūya tadā pṛthvīṃ manavo'psu vyavasthitāḥ || 4-16 ||
1.1.d:
आत्तगन्धा यदा भूमिरम्भसा कारणात्मना |
अतिभूय तदा पृथ्वीं मनवोऽप्सु व्यवस्थिताः || 4-16 ||
1.1.m:
When the earth has its smell taken away by water as the causal principle,
then, transcending the earth, the Manus abide in the waters. || 4-16

1.1.s:
bhūmistvāttarasā śaśvajjahāti vyaktināmanī |
prabhavantyāpa etarhi jagadetaccarācaram || 4-17 ||
1.1.d:
भूमिस्त्वात्तरसा शश्वज्जहाति व्यक्तिनामनी |
प्रभवन्त्याप एतर्हि जगदेतच्चराचरम् || 4-17 ||
1.1.m:
The earth, its taste constantly taken away, abandons manifested form and name;
now the waters prevail, this world moving and unmoving. || 4-17

1.1.s:
saṃkalpādeva pūrvasmāt sudarśanamayāddhareḥ |
apāmapi rasaṃ sāraṃ jyotirgrasati kāraṇam || 4-18 ||
1.1.d:
संकल्पादेव पूर्वस्मात् सुदर्शनमयाद्धरेः |
अपामपि रसं सारं ज्योतिर्ग्रसति कारणम् || 4-18 ||
1.1.m:
By that very former creative resolve of Hari consisting of Sudarśana,
causal light devours the essence of the waters, taste. || 4-18

1.1.s:
atibhūya tadāpastu manavo jyotiṣi sthitāḥ |
āpaścāttarasāḥ śaśvajjahati vyaktināmanī || 4-19 ||
1.1.d:
अतिभूय तदापस्तु मनवो ज्योतिषि स्थिताः |
आपश्चात्तरसाः शश्वज्जहति व्यक्तिनामनी || 4-19 ||
1.1.m:
Transcending the waters then, the Manus abide in light;
and the waters, their taste constantly taken away, abandon manifested form and name. || 4-19
Now the world is blazing light alone, O sage.
Impelled by the creative resolve of Viṣṇu, the wind, termed causal, || 4-20

1.1.s:
jyotiṣo'pyāntaraṃ rūpaṃ sāraṃ grasati tad dhruvam |
saṃkalpacoditā viṣṇormanavo'pi tadā mune || 4-21 ||
1.1.d:
ज्योतिषोऽप्यान्तरं रूपं सारं ग्रसति तद् ध्रुवम् |
संकल्पचोदिता विष्णोर्मनवोऽपि तदा मुने || 4-21 ||
1.1.m:
devours that firm, internal form, the essence of light.
Impelled by the creative resolve of Viṣṇu, the Manus also then, O sage, || 4-21

1.1.s:
atibhūyākhilaṃ jyotirvāyumeva śrayanti te |
āttarūpaṃ tadā jyotirjahāti vyaktināmanī || 4-22 ||
1.1.d:
अतिभूयाखिलं ज्योतिर्वायुमेव श्रयन्ति ते |
आत्तरूपं तदा ज्योतिर्जहाति व्यक्तिनामनी || 4-22 ||
1.1.m:
transcending all light, take refuge in the wind alone;
then light, its form taken away, abandons manifested form and name. || 4-22
The furiously shaking wind is this entire world, moving and unmoving.
Then, impelled by the creative resolve of Viṣṇu, causal space || 4-23

1.1.s:
sāraṃ grasati saṃsparśaṃ kāraṇaṃ vai nabhasvataḥ |
sudarśaneritā viṣṇormanavo'pi mahāmune || 4-24 ||
1.1.d:
सारं ग्रसति संस्पर्शं कारणं वै नभस्वतः |
सुदर्शनेरिता विष्णोर्मनवोऽपि महामुने || 4-24 ||
1.1.m:
devours the touch-essence, the cause indeed of wind;
impelled by Viṣṇu's Sudarśana, the Manus also, O great sage, || 4-24

1.1.s:
na bhasyevāvatiṣṭhante vyatibhūya samīraṇam |
āttasparśastadā vāyurjahāti vyaktināmanī || 4-25 ||
1.1.d:
न भस्येवावतिष्ठन्ते व्यतिभूय समीरणम् |
आत्तस्पर्शस्तदा वायुर्जहाति व्यक्तिनामनी || 4-25 ||
1.1.m:
abide in space alone, having transcended wind;
then wind, its touch taken away, abandons manifested form and name. || 4-25
The universe, moving and unmoving, is space resounding vehemently.
Dissolution of Space into Egoity
Impelled by the power of action of Viṣṇu, egoity, possessing self-conceit, || 4-26

1.1.s:
sāraṃ grasati śabdākhyaṃ kāraṇaṃ nabhaso mune |
tayaiva preritā viṣṇoratibhūya viyatpadam || 4-27 ||
1.1.d:
सारं ग्रसति शब्दाख्यं कारणं नभसो मुने |
तयैव प्रेरिता विष्णोरतिभूय वियत्पदम् || 4-27 ||
1.1.m:
devours the essence called sound, the cause of space, O sage;
impelled by that same [power] of Viṣṇu, transcending the realm of space, || 4-27

1.1.s:
p. 33) ahaṃkāre'vatiṣṭhante manavo bhagavanmayāḥ |
āttaśabdaṃ viyat tacca jahāti vyaktināmanī || 4-28 ||
1.1.d:
प्. 33) अहंकारेऽवतिष्ठन्ते मनवो भगवन्मयाः |
आत्तशब्दं वियत् तच्च जहाति व्यक्तिनामनी || 4-28 ||
1.1.m:
the Manus, full of the Lord, abide in egoity;
and that space, its sound taken away, abandons manifested form and name. || 4-28
That universe is consisting of egoity, as 'I' alone, O sage.
Dissolution of Egoity into Intellect
Impelled by Viṣṇu's Sudarśana, intellect devours the cause of egoity, || 4-29

1.1.s:
sudarśaneritā viṣṇorbuddhirgrasati vai mune |
sudarśaneritā viṣṇoratibhūya tvahaṃkṛtim || 4-30 ||
1.1.d:
सुदर्शनेरिता विष्णोर्बुद्धिर्ग्रसति वै मुने |
सुदर्शनेरिता विष्णोरतिभूय त्वहंकृतिम् || 4-30 ||
1.1.m:
its essence consisting of self-conceit, O sage;
impelled by Viṣṇu's Sudarśana, transcending egoity, || 4-30

1.1.s:
buddhāvevāvatiṣṭhante manavo'ṣṭau mahāmune |
āttābhimāno'haṃkāro jahāti vyaktināmanī || 4-31 ||
1.1.d:
बुद्धावेवावतिष्ठन्ते मनवोऽष्टौ महामुने |
आत्ताभिमानोऽहंकारो जहाति व्यक्तिनामनी || 4-31 ||
1.1.m:
the eight Manus abide in intellect alone, O great sage;
egoity, its self-conceit taken away, abandons manifested form and name. || 4-31
All this is intellect alone, endowed with determinative resolve, O sage.
The imperishable cause of intellect, the essence called determination, || 4-32

1.1.s:
sudarśaneritaṃ viṣṇostamo grasati kāraṇam |
sudarśaneritā viṣṇormanavo'pi mahāmune || 4-33 ||
1.1.d:
सुदर्शनेरितं विष्णोस्तमो ग्रसति कारणम् |
सुदर्शनेरिता विष्णोर्मनवोऽपि महामुने || 4-33 ||
1.1.m:
causal darkness devours, impelled by Viṣṇu's Sudarśana;
impelled by Viṣṇu's Sudarśana, the Manus also, O great sage, || 4-33

1.1.s:
atibhūya tadā buddhiṃ tamasyeva śritāḥ sthitim |
āsīdidaṃ tamobhūtamaprajñātamalakṣaṇam || 4-34 ||
1.1.d:
अतिभूय तदा बुद्धिं तमस्येव श्रिताः स्थितिम् |
आसीदिदं तमोभूतमप्रज्ञातमलक्षणम् || 4-34 ||
1.1.m:
having then transcended intellect, take up their stand in darkness alone.
This became darkness, undiscovered, devoid of distinctive marks, || 4-34
beyond reasoning, unknowable, motionless, heavy, stupefying.
Dissolution of the Sense Faculties along with the Elements into their Respective Causes

1.1.s: ghrāṇaṃ jihvā ca cakṣuśca tvak ca śrotraṃ ca pañcamam || 4-35 ||
1.1.d: घ्राणं जिह्वा च चक्षुश्च त्वक् च श्रोत्रं च पञ्चमम् || 4-35 ||
1.1.m: the nose, the tongue, the eye, the skin, and the ear as the fifth, || 4-35

1.1.s:
p. 34) pāyūpasthaṃ tathā pādau hastau vāk caiva pañcamī |
dvayoḥ pañcakayordvandvaṃ ghrāṇapāyvādikaṃ kramāt || 4-36 ||
1.1.d:
प्. 34) पायूपस्थं तथा पादौ हस्तौ वाक् चैव पञ्चमी |
द्वयोः पञ्चकयोर्द्वन्द्वं घ्राणपाय्वादिकं क्रमात् || 4-36 ||
1.1.m:
the anus and the genitals, likewise the two feet, the two hands, and speech as the fifth—
these two sets of five, taken in pairs, beginning with the nose and the anus, in sequence, || 4-36

1.1.s:
mahījalādibhirhetau līyamānaiḥ svake svake |
samaṃ vilayamāyāti saha ghrāṇādivṛttibhiḥ || 4-37 ||
1.1.d:
महीजलादिभिर्हेतौ लीयमानैः स्वके स्वके |
समं विलयमायाति सह घ्राणादिवृत्तिभिः || 4-37 ||
1.1.m:
simultaneously dissolve along with the functions of the nose and the rest,
while earth, water, and the other [elements] are dissolving into their respective causes. || 4-37

1.1.s:
mano'haṃkāra ityetat savṛtti karaṇadvayam |
ahaṃkāre layaṃ yāti buddhau bodhanamindriyam || 4-38 ||
1.1.d:
मनोऽहंकार इत्येतत् सवृत्ति करणद्वयम् |
अहंकारे लयं याति बुद्धौ बोधनमिन्द्रियम् || 4-38 ||
1.1.m:
This pair of instruments along with their functions—namely mind and egoity—
dissolves into egoity; the sense faculty that cognises [dissolves] into intellect. || 4-38
Now this entire [universe] remains as darkness alone.
The power of fixation of this darkness, consisting in heaviness, || 4-39

1.1.s:
rajo grasati tāṃ śaśvadīśvarecchāpracoditam |
icchayā preritā viṣṇormanavo'pi mahāmune || 4-40 ||
1.1.d:
रजो ग्रसति तां शश्वदीश्वरेच्छाप्रचोदितम् |
इच्छया प्रेरिता विष्णोर्मनवोऽपि महामुने || 4-40 ||
1.1.m:
