is continually swallowed by passion, impelled by the will of the Lord.
Impelled by the will of Viṣṇu, O great sage, even the Manus || 4-40

1.1.s:
rajasyevāvatiṣṭhante vyatibhūya tamogatim |
āttasāraṃ tamastattu jahāti vyaktināmanī || 4-41 ||
1.1.d:
रजस्येवावतिष्ठन्ते व्यतिभूय तमोगतिम् |
आत्तसारं तमस्तत्तु जहाति व्यक्तिनामनी || 4-41 ||
1.1.m:
abide in passion alone, having transcended the state of darkness.
Then that darkness, its essence taken away, abandons manifested form and name. || 4-41

1.1.s: calakiryātmakaṃ duḥkhaṃ raja eva jagat tadā |
1.1.d: चलकिर्यात्मकं दुःखं रज एव जगत् तदा |
1.1.m: At that time the world is passion alone, characterized by unsteady action and suffering.
That power consisting of pulsation, whose nature is motion, full of passion, || 4-42

1.1.s:
tāṃ vai sudarśanādiṣṭaṃ sattvaṃ grasati kāraṇam |
rajaḥsthā manavaścaiva viṣṇusaṃkalpacoditāḥ || 4-43 ||
1.1.d:
तां वै सुदर्शनादिष्टं सत्त्वं ग्रसति कारणम् |
रजःस्था मनवश्चैव विष्णुसंकल्पचोदिताः || 4-43 ||
1.1.m:
is indeed swallowed by goodness, the cause, directed by Sudarśana.
And the Manus abiding in passion, impelled by the creative resolve of Viṣṇu, || 4-43

1.1.s:
p. 35) atibhūya rajaḥ sattvaṃ viśanti vimalaṃ mune |
āttasāraṃ rajastattu jahāti vyaktināmanī || 4-44 ||
1.1.d:
प्. 35) अतिभूय रजः सत्त्वं विशन्ति विमलं मुने |
आत्तसारं रजस्तत्तु जहाति व्यक्तिनामनी || 4-44 ||
1.1.m:
having transcended passion, enter pure goodness, O sage.
Then that passion, its essence taken away, abandons manifested form and name. || 4-44
This [universe], both moving and unmoving, became goodness: light and illuminating.
An attribute of Viṣṇu named Time, set in motion by Sudarśana, || 4-45

1.1.s:
sāraṃ prajñāmayaṃ sattvādādatte jñānakāraṇam |
atibhūya tadā sattvaṃ manavaḥ kālasaṃśritāḥ || 4-46 ||
1.1.d:
सारं प्रज्ञामयं सत्त्वादादत्ते ज्ञानकारणम् |
अतिभूय तदा सत्त्वं मनवः कालसंश्रिताः || 4-46 ||
1.1.m:
takes away from goodness the essence consisting of intelligence, the cause of knowledge.
Having then transcended goodness, the Manus resort to Time. || 4-46

1.1.s:
kāla eva jagat kṛtsnamidamāsīt tadā mune |
āttasāraṃ ca tat sattvaṃ jahāti vyaktināmanī || 4-47 ||
1.1.d:
काल एव जगत् कृत्स्नमिदमासीत् तदा मुने |
आत्तसारं च तत् सत्त्वं जहाति व्यक्तिनामनी || 4-47 ||
1.1.m:
At that time this entire world was Time alone, O sage;
and that goodness, its essence taken away, abandons manifested form and name. || 4-47

1.1.s:
kālī kālagatā śaktiryā sāśeṣaprakālinī |
niyatirnāma tāṃ tattvaṃ grasatīśvaracoditā || 4-48 ||
1.1.d:
काली कालगता शक्तिर्या साशेषप्रकालिनी |
नियतिर्नाम तां तत्त्वं ग्रसतीश्वरचोदिता || 4-48 ||
1.1.m:
The Black Power inhering in Time, which brings about all dissolution,
is swallowed, when impelled by the Lord, by the principle named Destiny. || 4-48

1.1.s:
sudarśaneritāste ca manavo'ṣṭau mahāmune |
atītya kālatattvaṃ tāṃ niyatiṃ pratipedire || 4-49 ||
1.1.d:
सुदर्शनेरितास्ते च मनवोऽष्टौ महामुने |
अतीत्य कालतत्त्वं तां नियतिं प्रतिपेदिरे || 4-49 ||
1.1.m:
Impelled by Sudarśana, those eight Manus, O great sage,
having passed beyond the principle of Time, reached that Destiny. || 4-49

1.1.s:
āttasārastadā kālo jahāti vyaktināmanī |
niyatirnāma sā viśvamidamāsīccarācaram || 4-50 ||
1.1.d:
आत्तसारस्तदा कालो जहाति व्यक्तिनामनी |
नियतिर्नाम सा विश्वमिदमासीच्चराचरम् || 4-50 ||
1.1.m:
Then Time, its essence taken away, abandons manifested form and name;
this entire universe, moving and unmoving, became Destiny by name. || 4-50

1.1.s:
mahāvidyāmayī śaktirniyateryā mahāmune |
śaktirnāma tadā tāṃ tu grasatīśvaracoditā || 4-51 ||
1.1.d:
महाविद्यामयी शक्तिर्नियतेर्या महामुने |
शक्तिर्नाम तदा तां तु ग्रसतीश्वरचोदिता || 4-51 ||
1.1.m:
The power of Destiny consisting of Great Knowledge, O great sage,
is then swallowed, when impelled by the Lord, by [the principle] named Power. || 4-51

1.1.s:
p. 36) manavo'pīśvarādiṣṭā niyatiṃ tāmatītya vai |
śaktiṃ māyāmayīṃ viṣṇorviśanti vipulātmikām || 4-52 ||
1.1.d:
प्. 36) मनवोऽपीश्वरादिष्टा नियतिं तामतीत्य वै |
शक्तिं मायामयीं विष्णोर्विशन्ति विपुलात्मिकाम् || 4-52 ||
1.1.m:
The Manus too, commanded by the Lord, having indeed passed beyond Destiny,
enter the vast Power consisting of Viṣṇu's Māyā. || 4-52

1.1.s:
niyatiścāttasārā sā jahāti vyaktināmanī |
atha śaktiridaṃ viśvaṃ jagadāsīccarācaram || 4-53 ||
1.1.d:
नियतिश्चात्तसारा सा जहाति व्यक्तिनामनी |
अथ शक्तिरिदं विश्वं जगदासीच्चराचरम् || 4-53 ||
1.1.m:
And Destiny, its essence taken away, abandons manifested form and name;
then Power became this universe, the moving and unmoving world. || 4-53
Dissolution of Power into the Immoveable Puruṣa

1.1.s:
ā caitanyonmiṣattāyāḥ śakteḥ śaktiḥ sanātanī |
sudarśaneritastāṃ tu puruṣo grasati svayam || 4-54 ||
1.1.d:
आ चैतन्योन्मिषत्तायाः शक्तेः शक्तिः सनातनी |
सुदर्शनेरितस्तां तु पुरुषो ग्रसति स्वयम् || 4-54 ||
1.1.m:
The eternal Power, extending up to the unfolding of consciousness,
is swallowed by the Puruṣa himself, impelled by Sudarśana. || 4-54

1.1.s:
atītya manavaḥ śaktiṃ taṃ viśantīśvareritāḥ |
āttasārā tadā śaktirjahāti vyaktināmanī || 4-55 ||
1.1.d:
अतीत्य मनवः शक्तिं तं विशन्तीश्वरेरिताः |
आत्तसारा तदा शक्तिर्जहाति व्यक्तिनामनी || 4-55 ||
1.1.m:
Passing beyond Power, the Manus, impelled by the Lord, enter him.
Then Power, its essence taken away, abandons manifested form and name. || 4-55

1.1.s:
sarvātmā sarvataḥśaktiḥ puruṣaḥ sarvatomukhaḥ |
sarvajñaḥ sarvagaḥ sarvaḥ sarvamāvṛtya tiṣṭhati || 4-56 ||
1.1.d:
सर्वात्मा सर्वतःशक्तिः पुरुषः सर्वतोमुखः |
सर्वज्ञः सर्वगः सर्वः सर्वमावृत्य तिष्ठति || 4-56 ||
1.1.m:
The Puruṣa, the Self of all, with power on every side, facing every direction,
omniscient, all-pervading, all, stands encompassing all. || 4-56

1.1.s:
manūnāmeṣa kūṭasthaḥ puruṣo dvicaturmayaḥ |
kṛtsnakarmādhikāro vai devadevasya vai hareḥ || 4-57 ||
1.1.d:
मनूनामेष कूटस्थः पुरुषो द्विचतुर्मयः |
कृत्स्नकर्माधिकारो वै देवदेवस्य वै हरेः || 4-57 ||
1.1.m:
This immoveable Puruṣa, consisting of the eight Manus,
is the sphere of all action of Hari, the God of gods. || 4-57

For the thirteen [principles], from earth up to Power, O great sage,
whose respective effects have dissolved, the duration is a hundred desired years. || 4-58
Dissolution of the Immoveable Puruṣa into Aniruddha

1.1.s:
puṃsastrīṇi śatāni syustato manumayaḥ pumān |
caturdhā svaṃ vibhajyātha brahmakṣatrādibhāvataḥ || 4-59 ||
1.1.d:
पुंसस्त्रीणि शतानि स्युस्ततो मनुमयः पुमान् |
चतुर्धा स्वं विभज्याथ ब्रह्मक्षत्रादिभावतः || 4-59 ||
1.1.m:
There are three hundred [years] for the Puruṣa; then the Puruṣa composed of the Manus,
dividing himself fourfold through the nature of Brahmins, Kṣatriyas, and the rest, || 4-59

1.1.s:
p. 37) sve sve sthāne'niruddhasya mukhabāhvādike mune |
pralīyate kṣaṇenaiva taptāyaḥ piṇḍavārivat || 4-60 ||
1.1.d:
प्. 37) स्वे स्वे स्थानेऽनिरुद्धस्य मुखबाह्वादिके मुने |
प्रलीयते क्षणेनैव तप्तायः पिण्डवारिवत् || 4-60 ||
1.1.m:
in Aniruddha's respective places—the mouth, the arms, and so forth—O sage,
dissolves in a single moment, like water on a red-hot lump of iron. || 4-60

1.1.s:
tato'sau bhagavānekaḥ pralīnacidacinmayaḥ |
śatāni daśa ṣaṭ cātha varṣāṇāmavatiṣṭhate || 4-61 ||
1.1.d:
ततोऽसौ भगवानेकः प्रलीनचिदचिन्मयः |
शतानि दश षट् चाथ वर्षाणामवतिष्ठते || 4-61 ||
1.1.m:
Then that one Bhagavān, in whom consciousness and non-consciousness have dissolved,
remains for sixteen hundred years. || 4-61
Dissolution of Aniruddha into Pradyumna

1.1.s:
avasthāya tato'pyeti pradyumnamajaraṃ vibhum |
nirudhya sarvaceṣṭāḥ svāstāvatkālaṃ sa tiṣṭhati || 4-62 ||
1.1.d:
अवस्थाय ततोऽप्येति प्रद्युम्नमजरं विभुम् |
निरुध्य सर्वचेष्टाः स्वास्तावत्कालं स तिष्ठति || 4-62 ||
1.1.m:
Having remained thus, he dissolves into the ageless, all-pervading Pradyumna;
checking all his activities, he remains for the same length of time. || 4-62
Dissolution of Pradyumna into Saṃkarṣaṇa

1.1.s:
tataḥ pradyumnasaṃjño'sau bhagavān puṣkarekṣaṇaḥ |
apyeti bhagavantaṃ taṃ saṃkarṣaṇamanāmayam || 4-63 ||
1.1.d:
ततः प्रद्युम्नसंज्ञोऽसौ भगवान् पुष्करेक्षणः |
अप्येति भगवन्तं तं संकर्षणमनामयम् || 4-63 ||
1.1.m:
Then that lotus-eyed Bhagavān named Pradyumna
dissolves into that Bhagavān Saṃkarṣaṇa, free from affliction. || 4-63

1.1.s:
kālaṃ tiṣṭhati tāvantaṃ sarvadevamayo'cyutaḥ |
cidacitkhacitaṃ viśvaṃ śuddhāśuddhamaśeṣataḥ || 4-64 ||
1.1.d:
कालं तिष्ठति तावन्तं सर्वदेवमयोऽच्युतः |
चिदचित्खचितं विश्वं शुद्धाशुद्धमशेषतः || 4-64 ||
1.1.m:
Acyuta, embodying all the gods, remains for the same length of time,
holding within his body consisting of knowledge the entire universe, pure and impure, || 4-64

1.1.s:
tilakālakavat svasya dehe jñānamaye dadhat |
udayāstācalāveṣa devaḥ saṃkarṣaṇo balaḥ || 4-65 ||
1.1.d:
तिलकालकवत् स्वस्य देहे ज्ञानमये दधत् |
उदयास्ताचलावेष देवः संकर्षणो बलः || 4-65 ||
1.1.m:
inlaid with consciousness and non-consciousness, like a dark mole [on the skin].
This Lord Saṃkarṣaṇa, the strong, is the mountain of rising and setting || 4-65

1.1.s:
cidindoracidaṅkasya kalāstā anudhāvataḥ |
ahīnamaharetaddhi saṃkarṣaṇamayaṃ param || 4-66 ||
1.1.d:
चिदिन्दोरचिदङ्कस्य कलास्ता अनुधावतः |
अहीनमहरेतद्धि संकर्षणमयं परम् || 4-66 ||
1.1.m:
for those digits that follow the moon of consciousness, whose mark is non-consciousness;
for this supreme, unbroken day consists of Saṃkarṣaṇa, || 4-66
wherein entities of various kinds are manifested under their respective names.
Dissolution of Saṃkarṣaṇa into Vāsudeva
Having remained for sixteen hundred years, this Acyuta || 4-67

1.1.s:
p. 38) apyeti bhagavantaṃ taṃ vāsudevaṃ sanātanam |
nāsadāsīt tadānīṃ hi no sadāsīt tadā mune || 4-68 ||
1.1.d:
प्. 38) अप्येति भगवन्तं तं वासुदेवं सनातनम् |
नासदासीत् तदानीं हि नो सदासीत् तदा मुने || 4-68 ||
1.1.m:
dissolves into that eternal Bhagavān Vāsudeva.
Neither non-being existed then, nor being, O sage. || 4-68

1.1.s:
bhāvābhāvau vilopyāntarvicitravibhavodayau |
anirdeśyaṃ paraṃ brahma vāsudevo'vatiṣṭhate || 4-69 ||
1.1.d:
भावाभावौ विलोप्यान्तर्विचित्रविभवोदयौ |
अनिर्देश्यं परं ब्रह्म वासुदेवोऽवतिष्ठते || 4-69 ||
1.1.m:
Submerging within both being and non-being, the rise of whose wondrous glories had occurred,
Vāsudeva remains as the indescribable supreme Brahman. || 4-69

1.1.s:
sā rātristat paraṃ brahma tadavyaktamudāhṛtam |
ṣaṇṇāṃ yugāni vijñānabalādīnāmaśeṣataḥ || 4-70 ||
1.1.d:
सा रात्रिस्तत् परं ब्रह्म तदव्यक्तमुदाहृतम् |
षण्णां युगानि विज्ञानबलादीनामशेषतः || 4-70 ||
1.1.m:
That is declared to be the Night, that the supreme Brahman, that the Unmanifest.
Where all three pairs of the six [attributes]—knowledge, strength, and the rest— || 4-70

1.1.s:
trīṇi yasmin pralīyante yat tat sā rātrirucyate |
saṃkarṣaṇādibhūmyantamañjanaṃ vigataṃ yataḥ || 4-71 ||
1.1.d:
त्रीणि यस्मिन् प्रलीयन्ते यत् तत् सा रात्रिरुच्यते |
संकर्षणादिभूम्यन्तमञ्जनं विगतं यतः || 4-71 ||
1.1.m:
dissolve, that is called the Night;
and because the tint stretching from Saṃkarṣaṇa to earth has departed, || 4-71

1.1.s:
tadavyaktamiti jñeyaṃ samatvāt sama ucyate |
yā sā bhagavataḥ śaktirahaṃtā sarvabhāvagā || 4-72 ||
1.1.d:
तदव्यक्तमिति ज्ञेयं समत्वात् सम उच्यते |
या सा भगवतः शक्तिरहंता सर्वभावगा || 4-72 ||
1.1.m:
it is to be known as the Unmanifest; because of impartiality, it is called equal.
That Power of Bhagavān, the I-ness present in all entities, || 4-72

1.1.s:
apṛthakcāriṇī sattā mahānandamayī parā |
saṃkarṣaṇādibhūmyantastasyāḥ koṭyaṃśa īritaḥ || 4-73 ||
1.1.d:
अपृथक्चारिणी सत्ता महानन्दमयी परा |
संकर्षणादिभूम्यन्तस्तस्याः कोट्यंश ईरितः || 4-73 ||
1.1.m:
the supreme existence, inseparably moving [with him], consisting of great bliss—
[the span] from Saṃkarṣaṇa to earth is said to be a ten-millionth fraction of it. || 4-73

Where the universe shines in the forms of being and non-being, consciousness and non-consciousness,
when that continuous emergence of the world's tumult has ceased, || 4-74

1.1.s:
alakṣyā kāryataḥ śaktirdevādvijahatī bhidām |
pratisaṃcarikāṃ śaktiṃ kriyāṃ saudarśanīṃ svakām || 4-75 ||
1.1.d:
अलक्ष्या कार्यतः शक्तिर्देवाद्विजहती भिदाम् |
प्रतिसंचरिकां शक्तिं क्रियां सौदर्शनीं स्वकाम् || 4-75 ||
1.1.m:
the Power, imperceptible through effects, shedding distinction from the God,
withdrawing her dissolution-effecting Power, her own action belonging to Sudarśana, || 4-75

1.1.s:
saṃhṛtya bibhratī tāṃ tu sthitiṃ saṃkalparūpiṇīm |
indhanābhāvato jvālā vahnibhāvaṃ yathā gatā || 4-76 ||
1.1.d:
संहृत्य बिभ्रती तां तु स्थितिं संकल्परूपिणीम् |
इन्धनाभावतो ज्वाला वह्निभावं यथा गता || 4-76 ||
1.1.m:
and assuming that state having the form of divine resolve—
just as a flame, for lack of fuel, attains the state of fire— || 4-76

1.1.s:
p. 39) brahmabhāvaṃ vrajatyevaṃ sā śaktirvaiṣṇavī parā |
nārāyaṇaḥ paraṃ brahma śaktirnārāyaṇī ca sā || 4-77 ||
1.1.d:
प्. 39) ब्रह्मभावं व्रजत्येवं सा शक्तिर्वैष्णवी परा |
नारायणः परं ब्रह्म शक्तिर्नारायणी च सा || 4-77 ||
1.1.m:
so that supreme Vaiṣṇava Power attains the state of Brahman:
Nārāyaṇa is the supreme Brahman, and she is the Nārāyaṇī Power. || 4-77

1.1.s:
vyāpakāvatisaṃśleṣādekaṃ tattvamiva sthitau |
saṃkarṣaṇodayo yāvadahaḥ pauruṣamiṣyate |
tāvatī pauruṣī rātriḥ saṃhṛtākhilavastukā || 4-78 ||
1.1.d:
व्यापकावतिसंश्लेषादेकं तत्त्वमिव स्थितौ |
संकर्षणोदयो यावदहः पौरुषमिष्यते |
तावती पौरुषी रात्रिः संहृताखिलवस्तुका || 4-78 ||

1.1.s:
iti śrīpāñcarātre tantrarahasye ahirbudhnyasaṃhitāyāṃ
pratisaṃcaravarṇanaṃ nāma caturtho'dhyāyaḥ || 4 ||
1.1.d:
इति श्रीपाञ्चरात्रे तन्त्ररहस्ये अहिर्बुध्न्यसंहितायां
प्रतिसंचरवर्णनं नाम चतुर्थोऽध्यायः || 4 ||
1.1.m: Thus ends the fourth chapter, named 'Description of Cosmic Dissolution', in the Ahirbudhnyasaṃhitā of the Śrī Pāñcarātra esoteric teaching. || 4
Chapter 5, named 'Description of the Pure Creation'

1.1.s:
kāryakāraṇavargasya pralayo'yaṃ pradarśitaḥ |
sudarśanamayīṃ sṛṣṭiṃ tasya vakṣyāmi te mune || 5-1 ||
1.1.d:
कार्यकारणवर्गस्य प्रलयोऽयं प्रदर्शितः |
सुदर्शनमयीं सृष्टिं तस्य वक्ष्यामि ते मुने || 5-1 ||
1.1.m:
This dissolution of the realm of causes and effects has been revealed.
Now I will tell you, O sage, of His creation consisting of Sudarśana. || 5-1
The nature of Brahman in the state of dissolution

1.1.s:
prasuptākhilakāryaṃ sarvataḥ samatāṃ gatam |
nārāyaṇaḥ paraṃ brahma sarvāvāsamanāhatam || 5-2 ||
1.1.d:
प्रसुप्ताखिलकार्यं सर्वतः समतां गतम् |
नारायणः परं ब्रह्म सर्वावासमनाहतम् || 5-2 ||
1.1.m:
All effects having fallen asleep, having attained equality everywhere,
Nārāyaṇa is the supreme Brahman, the abode of all, unstruck, || 5-2
possessing the six attributes full and motionless, like the windless sky.
The awakening of Lakṣmī as Power in some respect
His Power, which has the form of motionlessness, having the form of voidness, || 5-3

1.1.s:
svātantryādeva kasmāccit kvacit sonmeṣamṛcchati |
ātmabhūtā hi yā śaktiḥ parasya brahmaṇo hareḥ || 5-4 ||
1.1.d:
स्वातन्त्र्यादेव कस्माच्चित् क्वचित् सोन्मेषमृच्छति |
आत्मभूता हि या शक्तिः परस्य ब्रह्मणो हरेः || 5-4 ||
1.1.m:
spontaneously from freedom alone attains awakening somewhere;
for the Power that is essential to Hari, the supreme Brahman, || 5-4

1.1.s:
devī vidyudiva vyomni kvaciduddyotate tu sā |
śaktirvidyotamānā sā śaktirityucyate'mbare || 5-5 ||
1.1.d:
देवी विद्युदिव व्योम्नि क्वचिदुद्द्योतते तु सा |
शक्तिर्विद्योतमाना सा शक्तिरित्युच्यतेऽम्बरे || 5-5 ||
1.1.m:
that Goddess flashes forth somewhere like lightning in the sky.
That Power, flashing forth, is called 'Power' in the sky. || 5-5
The Power as manifesting manifold states of existence
She manifests diverse states of being, pure and impure, endowed with form.

1.1.s: p. 41) tasyā unmeṣamṛcchantyāḥ svātantryaṃ yat svanirmitam || 5-6 ||
1.1.d: प्. 41) तस्या उन्मेषमृच्छन्त्याः स्वातन्त्र्यं यत् स्वनिर्मितम् || 5-6 ||
1.1.m: Of her, as she attains awakening, that freedom which is produced by herself, || 5-6

1.1.s:
prekṣaṇātmā sa saṃkalpastat sudarśanamucyate |
sā kriyā taddharervīryaṃ tat tejaśca balaṃ ca tat || 5-7 ||
1.1.d:
प्रेक्षणात्मा स संकल्पस्तत् सुदर्शनमुच्यते |
सा क्रिया तद्धरेर्वीर्यं तत् तेजश्च बलं च तत् || 5-7 ||
1.1.m:
that creative resolve consisting of vision—that is called Sudarśana.
That is action; that is Hari's virility, that is His splendour, and that is His strength. || 5-7

1.1.s:
vyajyante ye ca te bhāvāḥ svabhittiparivartitāḥ |
sā bhūtirviṣṇuśaktiḥ sā śakteḥ koṭyaṃśakalpitā || 5-8 ||
1.1.d:
व्यज्यन्ते ये च ते भावाः स्वभित्तिपरिवर्तिताः |
सा भूतिर्विष्णुशक्तिः सा शक्तेः कोट्यंशकल्पिता || 5-8 ||
1.1.m:
And those states of being that are manifested, displayed upon their own screen,
that is becoming; that is Viṣṇu's Power, fashioned as a ten-millionth portion of the Power. || 5-8

1.1.s:
bahubhirdvandvabhāvaiḥ sā śaktirbhūtamayī sthitā |
śuddhāśuddhavibhāgena cetyacetanarūpataḥ || 5-9 ||
1.1.d:
बहुभिर्द्वन्द्वभावैः सा शक्तिर्भूतमयी स्थिता |
शुद्धाशुद्धविभागेन चेत्यचेतनरूपतः || 5-9 ||
1.1.m:
Endowed with many dualities, that Power stands consisting of the elements:
by the division of pure and impure, through the forms of the sentient and the insentient, || 5-9

by the division of time and that which is measured by time, by the distinction of manifest and unmanifest,
in the form of the indicated and the indicator, by the distinction of the expressed and the expressive, || 5-10

by the distinction of the enjoyed and the enjoyer, by the distinction of body and embodied soul;
and by other such varieties of dual pairs she is differentiated. || 5-11

1.1.s:
evaṃ prakārabhedena yā śaktirhetutāṃ gatā |
tāṃ vijānīhi devarṣe divyāṃ saudarśanīṃ kalām || 5-12 ||
1.1.d:
एवं प्रकारभेदेन या शक्तिर्हेतुतां गता |
तां विजानीहि देवर्षे दिव्यां सौदर्शनीं कलाम् || 5-12 ||
1.1.m:
The Power that has thus become the cause through diverse modes—
know her, O divine sage, to be the divine part belonging to Sudarśana. || 5-12

1.1.s:
samīryate yathā vahnirmegho vāpi samīraṇāt |
tathā sudarśanenaiva vibhūtiḥ preryate kalā || 5-13 ||
1.1.d:
समीर्यते यथा वह्निर्मेघो वापि समीरणात् |
तथा सुदर्शनेनैव विभूतिः प्रेर्यते कला || 5-13 ||
1.1.m:
Just as fire or a cloud is set in motion by the wind,
even so is the divine manifestation, the part, impelled by Sudarśana alone. || 5-13

1.1.s:
ānulomyena sarge tu prātilomyena saṃhṛtau |
yathā saṃpreryamāṇā sā sudarśananabhavasvatā || 5-14 ||
1.1.d:
आनुलोम्येन सर्गे तु प्रातिलोम्येन संहृतौ |
यथा संप्रेर्यमाणा सा सुदर्शननभवस्वता || 5-14 ||
1.1.m:
In the direct order during creation, but in reverse order during cosmic dissolution,
impelled by Sudarśana, the sun of the sky, || 5-14

1.1.s: p. 42) dadhāti vividhān bhāvāṃstathā me gadataḥ śṛṇu |
1.1.d: प्. 42) दधाति विविधान् भावांस्तथा मे गदतः शृणु |
1.1.m: she assumes diverse states of being; hear that from me as I speak.
Elaboration of the pure creation

1.1.s: tatra śuddhamayaṃ sargaṃ vibhūteḥ prathamaṃ śṛṇu || 5-15 ||
1.1.d: तत्र शुद्धमयं सर्गं विभूतेः प्रथमं शृणु || 5-15 ||
1.1.m: Therein, hear first of the creation consisting of the pure [realm] of divine manifestation. || 5-15

1.1.s:
yat tat ṣāḍguṇyamityuktaṃ jñānaiśvaryabalādikam |
yugaistasya tribhiḥ śuddhā sṛṣṭirbhūteḥ pravartate || 5-16 ||
1.1.d:
यत् तत् षाड्गुण्यमित्युक्तं ज्ञानैश्वर्यबलादिकम् |
युगैस्तस्य त्रिभिः शुद्धा सृष्टिर्भूतेः प्रवर्तते || 5-16 ||
1.1.m:
What was spoken of as the possessing of the six attributes—knowledge, sovereignty, strength, and the rest—
through three pairs of those, the pure creation of becoming proceeds. || 5-16
The manifestation of the triad of emanations from the three pairs of attributes

1.1.s:
tatra jñānabaladvandvādrūpaṃ sāṃkarṣaṇaṃ hareḥ |
aiśvaryavīryasaṃbhedādrūpaṃ prādyumnamucyate || 5-17 ||
1.1.d:
तत्र ज्ञानबलद्वन्द्वाद्रूपं सांकर्षणं हरेः |
ऐश्वर्यवीर्यसंभेदाद्रूपं प्राद्युम्नमुच्यते || 5-17 ||
1.1.m:
There, from the pair of knowledge and strength comes the form of Hari known as Saṃkarṣaṇa;
from the combination of sovereignty and virility, the form known as Pradyumna is spoken of. || 5-17

1.1.s:
śaktitejaḥsamutkarṣādāniruddhī tanurhareḥ |
ete śaktimayā vyūhā guṇonmeṣasvalakṣaṇāḥ || 5-18 ||
1.1.d:
शक्तितेजःसमुत्कर्षादानिरुद्धी तनुर्हरेः |
एते शक्तिमया व्यूहा गुणोन्मेषस्वलक्षणाः || 5-18 ||
1.1.m:
From the pre-eminence of power and splendour comes Hari's form as Aniruddha.
These emanations consist of power, characterised by the awakening of attributes. || 5-18
Continuity of the six attributes in all three emanations

1.1.s:
ṣāḍguṇyavigrahā devāḥ puruṣāḥ puṣkarekṣaṇāḥ |
tatra tatrāvaśiṣṭaṃ yad guṇānāṃ dviyugaṃ mune || 5-19 ||
1.1.d:
षाड्गुण्यविग्रहा देवाः पुरुषाः पुष्करेक्षणाः |
तत्र तत्रावशिष्टं यद् गुणानां द्वियुगं मुने || 5-19 ||
1.1.m:
These gods, the lotus-eyed Puruṣas, have the six attributes as their forms.
In each case, O sage, the remaining two pairs of attributes || 5-19
indeed follow along, each in its proper place.
The three modes of the fourfold state
Mere pervasion, the awakening of attributes, and the assumption of form—in these three ways || 5-20
Viṣṇu's fourfold state arises from the mingling of attributes.

1.1.s: p. 43) tatra jñānamayatvena devaḥ saṃkarṣaṇo balī || 5-21 ||
1.1.d: प्. 43) तत्र ज्ञानमयत्वेन देवः संकर्षणो बली || 5-21 ||
1.1.m: There, through consisting of knowledge, the powerful god Saṃkarṣaṇa || 5-21
manifests the exclusive path, the means to the attainment of the Bhagavān.
The god Pradyumna, the highest Puruṣa, consisting of virility and sovereignty, || 5-22
stands as the meaning of the scriptures, by way of the path to the attainment of the Bhagavān.
The fruit of the meaning of the scriptures, which is characterised by the attainment of the Bhagavān— || 5-23

1.1.s:
prāpayatyaniruddhaḥ san sādhakān puruṣottamaḥ |
śāstraśāstrārthatatsādhyaphalanirvāhakā ime || 5-24 ||
1.1.d:
प्रापयत्यनिरुद्धः सन् साधकान् पुरुषोत्तमः |
शास्त्रशास्त्रार्थतत्साध्यफलनिर्वाहका इमे || 5-24 ||
1.1.m:
being Aniruddha, the highest Puruṣa brings practitioners to achieve that.
These are the effectors of scripture, the meaning of scripture, and the fruit to be accomplished through it: || 5-24
these lotus-eyed Puruṣas, the emanations of Hari, consisting of power.
The fourfold nature of the emanation together with supreme Vāsudeva
Bhagavān Vāsudeva and these three emanations, O sage— || 5-25
know this to be the fourfold state, characterised by the manifest and the unmanifest.
Demonstration of the nature of the awakening of attributes
Those attributes consisting of power, namely knowledge, sovereignty, strength, and the rest— || 5-26

1.1.s:
teṣāṃ yugapadunmeṣaḥ staimityavirahātmakaḥ |
saṃkalpakalpito viṣṇoryaḥ sa tadvyaktilakṣaṇaḥ || 5-27 ||
1.1.d:
तेषां युगपदुन्मेषः स्तैमित्यविरहात्मकः |
संकल्पकल्पितो विष्णोर्यः स तद्व्यक्तिलक्षणः || 5-27 ||
1.1.m:
their simultaneous awakening, consisting of the cessation of motionlessness,
projected by Viṣṇu's creative resolve, is that which is characterised by His manifestation. || 5-27

1.1.s:
p. 44) bhagavān vāsudevaḥ sa paramā prakṛtiśca sā |
śaktiryā vyāpino viṣṇoḥ sā jagatprakṛtiḥ parā || 5-28 ||
1.1.d:
प्. 44) भगवान् वासुदेवः स परमा प्रकृतिश्च सा |
शक्तिर्या व्यापिनो विष्णोः सा जगत्प्रकृतिः परा || 5-28 ||
1.1.m:
He is Bhagavān Vāsudeva, and she is supreme Prakṛti;
that Power belonging to all-pervading Viṣṇu is the supreme Prakṛti of the world. || 5-28
Through distinction between the power and the possessor of power, He is called Vāsudeva.
The manifestation of Saṃkarṣaṇa from Vāsudeva desiring to create
The god Vāsudeva, consisting of all powers, through the desire to create, || 5-29
divides Himself by Himself—that [manifestation] is remembered as Saṃkarṣaṇa.
Just as light bursts forth when the sun rests on the eastern mountain, || 5-30
so, when the God rises, there is the light whose essence is Saṃkarṣaṇa.
His waiting for sixteen hundred years
Inactive, this power remains for sixteen hundred [years], || 5-31

1.1.s:
saṃkarṣaṇātmikā sākṣād vijñānabalavāribhiḥ |
ananto bhagavān viṣṇuḥ śaktimān puruṣottamaḥ || 5-32 ||
1.1.d:
संकर्षणात्मिका साक्षाद् विज्ञानबलवारिभिः |
अनन्तो भगवान् विष्णुः शक्तिमान् पुरुषोत्तमः || 5-32 ||
1.1.m: consisting directly of Saṃkarṣaṇa through the waters of knowledge and strength. / Bhagavān Viṣṇu is infinite, endowed with power, the Supreme Puruṣa, || 5-32

1.1.s:
pūrṇastimitaṣāḍguṇyo nistaraṅgārṇavopamaḥ |
ṣaṇṇāṃ yugapadunmeṣād guṇānāṃ svapracoditāt || 5-33 ||
1.1.d:
पूर्णस्तिमितषाड्गुण्यो निस्तरङ्गार्णवोपमः |
षण्णां युगपदुन्मेषाद् गुणानां स्वप्रचोदितात् || 5-33 ||
1.1.m: possessing full and motionless six attributes, like a waveless ocean. / From the simultaneous awakening of the six attributes, impelled by his own will, || 5-33

1.1.s:
ananta eva bhagavān vāsudevaḥ sanātanaḥ |
tatra jñānabalonmeṣāt svasaṃkalpapracoditāt || 5-34 ||
1.1.d:
अनन्त एव भगवान् वासुदेवः सनातनः |
तत्र ज्ञानबलोन्मेषात् स्वसंकल्पप्रचोदितात् || 5-34 ||
1.1.m: Bhagavān Vāsudeva is indeed eternal and infinite. / There, from the awakening of knowledge and strength impelled by his own resolve, || 5-34
Bhagavān Deva Saṃkarṣaṇa is indeed infinite and imperishable.
Having remained for sixteen [hundred] years, the imperishable God, full of power, || 5-35

1.1.s:
ananta eva bhagavān pradyumnaḥ puruṣottamaḥ |
aṃśāṃśenoditā śaktiḥ prādyumnī bhagavatprabhā || 5-36 ||
1.1.d:
अनन्त एव भगवान् प्रद्युम्नः पुरुषोत्तमः |
अंशांशेनोदिता शक्तिः प्राद्युम्नी भगवत्प्रभा || 5-36 ||
1.1.m: Bhagavān Pradyumna, the Supreme Puruṣa, is indeed infinite. / Arisen from a part of a part is the power belonging to Pradyumna, the radiance of Bhagavān. || 5-36
Inactive, this [power] remains silent for sixteen hundred [years].
Then the God full of power, Pradyumna, the Supreme Puruṣa, || 5-37

1.1.s:
śatāni ṣoḍaśa sthitvā svasaṃkalpapracoditaḥ |
ananta eva bhagavānaniruddho bhavatyuta || 5-38 ||
1.1.d:
शतानि षोडश स्थित्वा स्वसंकल्पप्रचोदितः |
अनन्त एव भगवाननिरुद्धो भवत्युत || 5-38 ||
1.1.m: having remained for sixteen hundred [years], impelled by his own resolve, / indeed becomes the infinite Bhagavān Aniruddha. || 5-38

1.1.s:
aṃśāṃśenoditā śaktirāniruddhī hareḥ prabhā |
avyāpṛtā śatānyeṣā tūṣṇīṃ tiṣṭhati ṣoḍaśa || 5-39 ||
1.1.d:
अंशांशेनोदिता शक्तिरानिरुद्धी हरेः प्रभा |
अव्यापृता शतान्येषा तूष्णीं तिष्ठति षोडश || 5-39 ||
1.1.m: Arisen from a part of a part is the power belonging to Aniruddha, the radiance of Hari. / Inactive, this [power] remains silent for sixteen hundred [years]. || 5-39
The engagement in creation of the emanation after sixteen hundred years

1.1.s:
śatāni ṣoḍaśa sthitvāniruddhaḥ śaktimānasau |
tadā vyāpriyate sṛṣṭau pūrvābhyāṃ saha nārada || 5-40 ||
1.1.d:
शतानि षोडश स्थित्वानिरुद्धः शक्तिमानसौ |
तदा व्याप्रियते सृष्टौ पूर्वाभ्यां सह नारद || 5-40 ||
1.1.m: Having remained for sixteen hundred [years], this powerful Aniruddha, / O Nārada, then engages in creation together with the preceding two. || 5-40
These emanations, large-eyed, are the four Supreme Puruṣas.
The emanations' opposition to defilement and their beginninglessness
Faultless, free from misery, blameless, and eternal, || 5-41
and this fourfold state is infinite and imperishable, O great sage!
In the waveless state, they are without differentiated existence, consisting of pure consciousness; || 5-42

1.1.s:
śaktyātmakā guṇonmeṣadaśāyāṃ te vyavasthitāḥ |
tatra sthūladaśāyāṃ te vyaktibhāvamupāgatāḥ || 5-43 ||
1.1.d:
शक्त्यात्मका गुणोन्मेषदशायां ते व्यवस्थिताः |
तत्र स्थूलदशायां ते व्यक्तिभावमुपागताः || 5-43 ||
1.1.m: in the state of the awakening of attributes, they abide as powers. / There, in the gross state, they reach manifest being || 5-43
for the benefit of the worlds, characterized by being, consciousness, and bliss.
The fourfold state serving as a support for the mind
This establishment of the fourfold state is for serving as a support for the mind. || 5-44
The manifestation of sub-emanations from the emanations
And the knowers of the secret sacred tradition have taught / divisions such as the sub-emanations and divine descents, devised by his resolve, belonging to this [fourfold state]. || 5-45

1.1.s: vyūhāntaraṃ daśa dve ca keśavādyāḥ prakīrtitāḥ |
1.1.d: व्यूहान्तरं दश द्वे च केशवाद्याः प्रकीर्तिताः |
1.1.m: The sub-emanations are declared to be twelve, beginning with Keśava.
The triad beginning with Keśava from Vāsudeva
There, the triad beginning with Keśava is manifested from Vāsudeva. || 5-46
The manifestation of the triad beginning with Govinda from Saṃkarṣaṇa
And from Saṃkarṣaṇa [arises] the wondrous triad preceded by Govinda.
The manifestation of the triad beginning with Trivikrama from Pradyumna
The triad beginning with Trivikrama has arisen from Pradyumna, O sage! || 5-47
The manifestation of the triad beginning with Hṛṣīkeśa from Aniruddha
The reality beginning with Hṛṣīkeśa [arises] from Aniruddha, O great sage!
The threefold nature of the sub-emanations
The highest are situated within their own causes; the subtle are remembered as two-armed; || 5-48
the gross are to be known as four-armed, the lords of the three worlds. / The arrangement of their weapons, such as the discus, will be explained in the treatise on diagrams. || 5-49
The thirty-nine divine descents

1.1.s:
vibhavāḥ padmanābhādyāstriṃśacca nava caiva hi |
padmanābho dhruvo'nantaḥ śaktyātmā madhusūdanaḥ || 5-50 ||
1.1.d:
विभवाः पद्मनाभाद्यास्त्रिंशच्च नव चैव हि |
पद्मनाभो ध्रुवोऽनन्तः शक्त्यात्मा मधुसूदनः || 5-50 ||
1.1.m: The divine descents beginning with Padmanābha are indeed thirty-nine: / Padmanābha, Dhruva, Ananta, Śaktyātman, Madhusūdana, || 5-50

1.1.s:
vidyādhidevaḥ kapilo viśvarūpo vihaṃgamaḥ |
kroḍātmā baḍabāvaktro dharmo vāgīśvarastathā || 5-51 ||
1.1.d:
विद्याधिदेवः कपिलो विश्वरूपो विहंगमः |
क्रोडात्मा बडबावक्त्रो धर्मो वागीश्वरस्तथा || 5-51 ||
1.1.m: Vidyādhideva, Kapila, Viśvarūpa, Vihaṅgama, / Kroḍātman, Baḍabāvaktra, Dharma, and likewise Vāgīśvara, || 5-51

1.1.s:
ekāmbhonidhiśāyī ca bhagavān kamaṭheśvaraḥ |
varāho nārasiṃhaśca pīyūṣaharaṇastathā || 5-52 ||
1.1.d:
एकाम्भोनिधिशायी च भगवान् कमठेश्वरः |
वराहो नारसिंहश्च पीयूषहरणस्तथा || 5-52 ||
1.1.m: and the one who reclines upon the single ocean, Bhagavān Kamaṭheśvara, / Varāha, Nārasiṃha, and likewise Pīyūṣaharaṇa, || 5-52

1.1.s:
śrīpatirbhagavān devaḥ kāntātmāmṛtadhārakaḥ |
rāhujit kālanemighnaḥ pārijātaharastathā || 5-53 ||
1.1.d:
श्रीपतिर्भगवान् देवः कान्तात्मामृतधारकः |
राहुजित् कालनेमिघ्नः पारिजातहरस्तथा || 5-53 ||
1.1.m: Śrīpati, the divine Bhagavān, Kāntātman, the nectar-bearer, / the conqueror of Rāhu, the slayer of Kālanemi, and the stealer of the Pārijāta, || 5-53

1.1.s:
lokanāthastu śāntātmā dattātreyo mahāprabhuḥ |
nyagrodhaśāyī bhagavānekaśṛṅgatanustathā || 5-54 ||
1.1.d:
लोकनाथस्तु शान्तात्मा दत्तात्रेयो महाप्रभुः |
न्यग्रोधशायी भगवानेकशृङ्गतनुस्तथा || 5-54 ||
1.1.m: and Lokanātha of tranquil nature, the great lord Dattātreya, / Bhagavān who reclines on the banyan tree, and the one whose body has a single horn, || 5-54

1.1.s:
devo vāmanadehastu sarvavyāpī trivikramaḥ |
naro nārāyaṇaścaiva hariḥ kṛṣṇastathaiva ca || 5-55 ||
1.1.d:
देवो वामनदेहस्तु सर्वव्यापी त्रिविक्रमः |
नरो नारायणश्चैव हरिः कृष्णस्तथैव च || 5-55 ||
1.1.m: the God with the body of a dwarf, the all-pervading Trivikrama, / Nara, Nārāyaṇa, Hari, and likewise Kṛṣṇa, || 5-55

1.1.s:
jvalatparaśudhṛgrāmo rāmaścānyo dhanurdharaḥ |
vedavidbhagavān kalkī pātālaśayanaḥ smṛtaḥ || 5-56 ||
1.1.d:
ज्वलत्परशुधृग्रामो रामश्चान्यो धनुर्धरः |
वेदविद्भगवान् कल्की पातालशयनः स्मृतः || 5-56 ||
1.1.m: Rāma holding a blazing axe, and the other Rāma who bears the bow, / the knower of the Vedas Bhagavān Kalkī, and the one remembered as reclining in the netherworld. || 5-56

1.1.s: p. 48) triṃśacca nava caivete padmanābhādayo matāḥ |
1.1.d: प्. 48) त्रिंशच्च नव चैवेते पद्मनाभादयो मताः |
1.1.m: These, beginning with Padmanābha, are considered to be thirty-nine.
Their origin and so forth are to be known from the Sāttvata and other texts
From where their origin is, what their activity is, what their weapon is, || 5-57

1.1.s:
yā mūrtiryādṛśī caiva yatra caite vyavasthitāḥ |
bhūṣaṇāni vicitrāṇi vāsāṃsi vividhāni ca || 5-58 ||
1.1.d:
या मूर्तिर्यादृशी चैव यत्र चैते व्यवस्थिताः |
भूषणानि विचित्राणि वासांसि विविधानि च || 5-58 ||
1.1.m: what form and of what kind, and where they abide, / their various ornaments and different garments, || 5-58

1.1.s:
bāhyāntaḥkaraṇānāṃ ca trayo vargāḥ savṛttayaḥ |
saṃkalpanirmitā śaktiryā tattatkāryagocarā |
sāttvate śāsane sarvaṃ tattaduktaṃ mahāmune || 5-59 ||
1.1.d:
बाह्यान्तःकरणानां च त्रयो वर्गाः सवृत्तयः |
संकल्पनिर्मिता शक्तिर्या तत्तत्कार्यगोचरा |
सात्त्वते शासने सर्वं तत्तदुक्तं महामुने || 5-59 ||
1.1.m: and the three classes of external and internal organs together with their functions, / the power produced by resolve, which has those respective duties as its scope— / all that has been spoken of in the Sāttvata teaching, O great sage! || 5-59
Summary of the chapter's content

1.1.s:
itīyaṃ śuddhasṛṣṭiste viṣṇoḥ saṃkalpakalpitā |
bhūtyaṃśo leśataḥ proktaḥ śṛṇu sṛṣṭimathetarām || 5-60 ||
1.1.d:
इतीयं शुद्धसृष्टिस्ते विष्णोः संकल्पकल्पिता |
भूत्यंशो लेशतः प्रोक्तः शृणु सृष्टिमथेतराम् || 5-60 ||
1.1.m: Thus this pure creation of Viṣṇu, devised by his resolve, / has been spoken of concisely as a portion of his becoming. Now hear the other creation. || 5-60

1.1.s:
iti śrīpāñcarātre tantrarahasye ahirbudhnyasaṃhitāyāṃ
śuddhasṛṣṭivarṇanaṃ nāma pañcamo'dhyāyaḥ || 5 ||
1.1.d:
इति श्रीपाञ्चरात्रे तन्त्ररहस्ये अहिर्बुध्न्यसंहितायां
शुद्धसृष्टिवर्णनं नाम पञ्चमोऽध्यायः || 5 ||
1.1.m: Thus ends the fifth chapter, named the Description of Pure Creation, in the Ahirbudhnya Saṃhitā of the secret doctrine of the Pāñcarātra. || 5
Chapter Six, named Description of Creation Other Than Pure
Demonstration of identity as well as difference between power and the possessor of power

1.1.s:
yo'sau nārāyaṇo devaḥ paramātmā sanātanaḥ |
ahaṃbhāvātmikā śaktistasya taddharmiṇī || 6-1 ||
1.1.d:
योऽसौ नारायणो देवः परमात्मा सनातनः |
अहंभावात्मिका शक्तिस्तस्य तद्धर्मिणी || 6-1 ||
1.1.m: That god who is Nārāyaṇa, the eternal Paramātman— / His power consists of I-ness and possesses His attributes. // 6-1

1.1.s:
tāvimāvekadhaivoktau bhedyabhedakabhāvataḥ |
pṛthaktvena ca śāstreṣu jagaddhetutayoditau || 6-2 ||
1.1.d:
ताविमावेकधैवोक्तौ भेद्यभेदकभावतः |
पृथक्त्वेन च शास्त्रेषु जगद्धेतुतयोदितौ || 6-2 ||
1.1.m: These two are spoken of as one, yet by reason of their condition as distinguished and distinguisher, / they are also stated in the scriptures to be distinct as the cause of the world. // 6-2
Inseparable subsistence of power and the possessor of power

1.1.s:
naiva śaktyā vinā kaścicchaktimānasti kāraṇam |
na ca śaktimatā śaktirvinaikā vyavatiṣṭhate || 6-3 ||
1.1.d:
नैव शक्त्या विना कश्चिच्छक्तिमानस्ति कारणम् |
न च शक्तिमता शक्तिर्विनैका व्यवतिष्ठते || 6-3 ||
1.1.m: Indeed, without power no possessor of power exists as a cause, / nor does power subsist alone without the possessor of power. // 6-3
Explanation of the conventional designation of Bhagavān and Lakṣmī each as the cause of the world
Relying upon the respective pre-eminence of each, masters of the Tantras and Vedānta / have shown both gods, as it were, individually as the cause of the world. // 6-4
Declaration of the explanation of creation other than pure
This having been established, hear this creation that remains to be described.
The set-in-motion of the power of becoming by the power of action in the form of His own will
This manifestation consisting of becoming belonging to the power of Viṣṇu, described earlier— // 6-5

1.1.s: p. 50) tasyāḥ saṃkalpamayyaiva sphūrtyā sā bahu nartyate |
1.1.d: प्. 50) तस्याः संकल्पमय्यैव स्फूर्त्या सा बहु नर्त्यते |
1.1.m: by her very manifestation consisting of will, she is made to dance in manifold ways.
The emanations, divine descents, and other forms as the pure manifestation serving as supports for yoga
The pure manifestation of becoming is that which consists of the emanations and divine descents, // 6-6
relying upon which yogins cross this ocean of worldly existence.
Creation other than pure having its foundation in the emanations and divine descents
Now, creation other than pure proceeds having that as its very foundation. // 6-7

1.1.s:
puruṣaścaiva kālaśca guṇaśceti tridhocyate |
bhūtiḥ śuddhetarā viṣṇoḥ puruṣo dvicaturmayaḥ || 6-8 ||
1.1.d:
पुरुषश्चैव कालश्च गुणश्चेति त्रिधोच्यते |
भूतिः शुद्धेतरा विष्णोः पुरुषो द्विचतुर्मयः || 6-8 ||
1.1.m: It is stated to be threefold, namely Puruṣa, Time, and the Gunas; / [such is] the becoming of Viṣṇu other than pure. Puruṣa consists of two-times-four. // 6-8
He is the aggregate of the Manus divided into Brahmins, Kṣatriyas, and so forth.
The emergence of the four pairs from Pradyumna
A Brahmin male and a Brahmin female: this pair is those two Manus. // 6-9

1.1.s:
pradyumnasya musvājjātaṃ svasaṃkalpena coditam |
urasaḥ kṣatriyadvandvamūrutaśca viśo dvayam || 6-10 ||
1.1.d:
प्रद्युम्नस्य मुस्वाज्जातं स्वसंकल्पेन चोदितम् |
उरसः क्षत्रियद्वन्द्वमूरुतश्च विशो द्वयम् || 6-10 ||
1.1.m: Born from the mouth of Pradyumna, impelled by His own will; / from His chest arose the pair of Kṣatriyas, and from His thighs the pair of Vaiśyas; // 6-10

1.1.s:
padbhyāṃ śūdradvayaṃ caiva pradyumnasya samudgatam |
samaṣṭiryā manūnāṃ sā puruṣo dvicaturmayaḥ || 6-11 ||
1.1.d:
पद्भ्यां शूद्रद्वयं चैव प्रद्युम्नस्य समुद्गतम् |
समष्टिर्या मनूनां सा पुरुषो द्विचतुर्मयः || 6-11 ||
1.1.m: and from His feet the pair of Śūdras came forth, belonging to Pradyumna. / The totality of these Manus is the Puruṣa consisting of two-times-four. // 6-11

1.1.s:
sūkṣmakālaguṇāvasthā sudarśanasamīritā |
pradyumnasya lalāṭācca bhruvoḥ karṇādudīritā || 6-12 ||
1.1.d:
सूक्ष्मकालगुणावस्था सुदर्शनसमीरिता |
प्रद्युम्नस्य ललाटाच्च भ्रुवोः कर्णादुदीरिता || 6-12 ||
1.1.m: The subtle state of Time and the Gunas, impelled by Sudarśana, / was sent forth from the forehead of Pradyumna, and from His eyebrows and ear. // 6-12
Bestowal of the command of preservation upon Aniruddha
Puruṣa and Power—this pair consisting of the conscious and the unconscious: / 'Nourish it!' thus it is handed over to Aniruddha by Pradyumna. // 6-13

1.1.s:
antaḥsthapuruṣāṃ śaktiṃ tāmādāya svamūrtigām |
saṃvardhayati yogena hyaniruddhaḥ svatejasā || 6-14 ||
1.1.d:
अन्तःस्थपुरुषां शक्तिं तामादाय स्वमूर्तिगाम् |
संवर्धयति योगेन ह्यनिरुद्धः स्वतेजसा || 6-14 ||
1.1.m: Taking that power, containing Puruṣa within it, which entered His own form, / Aniruddha fosters it through yoga by His own splendour. // 6-14

1.1.s:
niyatiḥ kāla ityevaṃ śaktiḥ saṃkalpacoditā |
dvidhodetyaniruddhāt sā yat tat kālamayaṃ vapuḥ || 6-15 ||
1.1.d:
नियतिः काल इत्येवं शक्तिः संकल्पचोदिता |
द्विधोदेत्यनिरुद्धात् सा यत् तत् कालमयं वपुः || 6-15 ||
1.1.m: Destiny and Time: thus the power, impelled by His will, / arises twofold from Aniruddha—that form which is composed of Time. // 6-15
The threefold nature of Prakṛti consisting of the Gunas

1.1.s:
yattadguṇamayaṃ rūpaṃ śaktestasyāḥ prakīrtitam |
sattvaṃ rajastama iti tridhodeti krameṇa tat || 6-16 ||
1.1.d:
यत्तद्गुणमयं रूपं शक्तेस्तस्याः प्रकीर्तितम् |
सत्त्वं रजस्तम इति त्रिधोदेति क्रमेण तत् || 6-16 ||
1.1.m: That form of that power which is known as composed of the Gunas / arises in succession threefold as goodness, passion, and darkness. // 6-16
Emergence of passion and the rest from goodness and the rest
From goodness arose passion, [from passion] darkness; and from that darkness intellect arose;
from intellect egoity, and from it the five subtle elements of the gross elements; // 6-17

1.1.s:
ekādaśakamakṣāṇāṃ mātrebhyo bhūtapañcakam |
bhūtebhyo bhautikaṃ sarvamityayaṃ sṛṣṭisaṃgrahaḥ || 6-18 ||
1.1.d:
एकादशकमक्षाणां मात्रेभ्यो भूतपञ्चकम् |
भूतेभ्यो भौतिकं सर्वमित्ययं सृष्टिसंग्रहः || 6-18 ||
1.1.m: the eleven faculties [arose], and from the subtle elements the five gross elements; / from the gross elements all elemental things [arose]—this is the summary of creation. // 6-18
Question asking for an elaboration of creation at length once again

1.1.s:
bhagavan bhaganetraghna tattvavijñānavāridhe |
ākhyāhi vistareṇādya bhūterunmeṣamadbhutam || 6-19 ||
1.1.d:
भगवन् भगनेत्रघ्न तत्त्वविज्ञानवारिधे |
आख्याहि विस्तरेणाद्य भूतेरुन्मेषमद्भुतम् || 6-19 ||
1.1.m: O Bhagavat, slayer of the eyes of Bhaga, ocean of knowledge of the principles! / Tell now at length of the wondrous awakening of becoming. // 6-19

1.1.s:
śṛṇu nārada tattvena viṣṇoḥ saṃkalpakāritām |
bhūteḥ pariṇatiṃ citrāṃ cidacidvargasaṃkulām || 6-20 ||
1.1.d:
शृणु नारद तत्त्वेन विष्णोः संकल्पकारिताम् |
भूतेः परिणतिं चित्रां चिदचिद्वर्गसंकुलाम् || 6-20 ||
1.1.m: Hear in truth, O Nārada, the manifold transformation of becoming, / brought about by the will of Viṣṇu, crowded with the classes of the conscious and the unconscious. // 6-20
Demonstration that Para-Vāsudeva possesses eternal divine manifestation

1.1.s:
śuddhā pūrvoditā sṛṣṭiryā sā vyūhādibhedinī |
sudarśanākhyāt saṃkalpāt tasyā eva prabhojjvalā || 6-21 ||
1.1.d:
शुद्धा पूर्वोदिता सृष्टिर्या सा व्यूहादिभेदिनी |
सुदर्शनाख्यात् संकल्पात् तस्या एव प्रभोज्ज्वला || 6-21 ||
1.1.m: The pure creation spoken of before, divided into emanations and the like— / radiant with light, from the very will named Sudarśana, // 6-21

1.1.s:
jñānānandamayī styānā deśabhāvaṃ vrajatyuta |
sa deśaḥ paramaṃ vyoma nirmalaṃ puruṣāt param || 6-22 ||
1.1.d:
ज्ञानानन्दमयी स्त्याना देशभावं व्रजत्युत |
स देशः परमं व्योम निर्मलं पुरुषात् परम् || 6-22 ||
1.1.m: composed of knowledge and bliss, becoming solidified, it indeed attains the nature of a realm. / That realm is the supreme space, spotless, beyond Puruṣa, // 6-22
a boundless continuum of happiness, faultless, untroubled; / there the experiences consist of bliss, and the worlds are characterized by bliss. // 6-23
The bodies of the liberated whose minds are cultivated are composed of knowledge and bliss.
The nature of the Lord of Śrī, Bhagavān, as an object of experience for the eternally liberated

1.1.s: sadā paśyanti te devāḥ puruṣaṃ puṣkarekṣaṇam || 6-24 ||
1.1.d: सदा पश्यन्ति ते देवाः पुरुषं पुष्करेक्षणम् || 6-24 ||
1.1.m: Those divine beings constantly behold the lotus-eyed Puruṣa, // 6-24

1.1.s:
ṣāḍguṇyavigrahaṃ devaṃ tādṛśyā ca śriyā yutam |
saṃkalpasādhitāśeṣadehadaihikavistaram || 6-25 ||
1.1.d:
षाड्गुण्यविग्रहं देवं तादृश्या च श्रिया युतम् |
संकल्पसाधिताशेषदेहदैहिकविस्तरम् || 6-25 ||
1.1.m: the God whose body possesses the six attributes, united with Śrī who is like Himself, / who has brought into being the entire extent of bodies and bodily appurtenances by His will, // 6-25
the Ruler of all this, the Lord of the moving and the unmoving world, / the dwelling of all, Himself without a dwelling, Nārāyaṇa, free from affliction. // 6-26

1.1.s:
tat padaṃ prāpya tattvajñā mucyante vītakalmaṣāḥ |
trasareṇupramāṇāste raśmikoṭivibhūṣitāḥ || 6-27 ||
1.1.d:
तत् पदं प्राप्य तत्त्वज्ञा मुच्यन्ते वीतकल्मषाः |
त्रसरेणुप्रमाणास्ते रश्मिकोटिविभूषिताः || 6-27 ||
1.1.m: Having reached that abode, the knowers of reality are liberated, free from stain; / they are of the measure of a mote of dust, adorned with millions of rays, // 6-27
free from the distinguishing attributes of manifestation and disappearance.
Having taken refuge in the supreme end of the path, the abode of Viṣṇu, // 6-28
they do not enter this path crowded with the billows of Time.
Attainment of fruit by them according to their meditation
Those devotees, in whatever form they took refuge while in the state of worldly existence— // 6-29

1.1.s:
tādṛśaṃ te samīkṣante paramavyomavāsinaḥ |
vihṛtya suciraṃ kālaṃ koṭyoghapratisaṃcaram || 6-30 ||
1.1.d:
तादृशं ते समीक्षन्ते परमव्योमवासिनः |
विहृत्य सुचिरं कालं कोट्योघप्रतिसंचरम् || 6-30 ||
1.1.m:
dwelling in the supreme space, they see that very [form],
having sported for a very long time, through crores of cosmic dissolutions; // 6-30

1.1.s: p. 54) tato viśanti te divyaṃ ṣāḍguṇyaṃ vaiṣṇavaṃ yaśaḥ |
1.1.d: प्. 54) ततो विशन्ति ते दिव्यं षाड्गुण्यं वैष्णवं यशः |
1.1.m: then they enter the divine glory of Viṣṇu, possessing the six attributes.
The impossibility of describing the supreme space
This supreme space has been shown to you in brief; // 6-31
its full extent cannot be spoken even in ten thousand years.
The collective Puruṣa of individual souls residing in a lower realm
The Puruṣa who is the sphere of action has been declared to you as four-yoked; // 6-32

1.1.s:
asmāt sa paramavyomnastiṣṭhatyarvāci vai pade |
sarvātmanāṃ samaṣṭiryā kośomadhukṛtāmiva || 6-33 ||
1.1.d:
अस्मात् स परमव्योम्नस्तिष्ठत्यर्वाचि वै पदे |
सर्वात्मनां समष्टिर्या कोशोमधुकृतामिव || 6-33 ||
1.1.m:
it stands in a lower realm indeed from this supreme space,
which is the aggregate of all souls, like a honeycomb of bees. // 6-33

1.1.s:
śuddhyaśuddhimayo bhāvo bhūteḥ sa puruṣaḥ smṛtaḥ |
anādivāsanāreṇukuṇṭhitairātmabhiścitaḥ || 6-34 ||
1.1.d:
शुद्ध्यशुद्धिमयो भावो भूतेः स पुरुषः स्मृतः |
अनादिवासनारेणुकुण्ठितैरात्मभिश्चितः || 6-34 ||
1.1.m:
That Puruṣa is remembered as a state of being consisting of purity and impurity of becoming,
filled with souls dulled by the dust of beginningless latent impressions. // 6-34
The concealment of the intrinsic nature of souls, though intrinsically pure, by Bhagavān's power

1.1.s:
ātmano bhūtibhedāste sarvajñāḥ sarvatomukhāḥ |
bhagavacchaktimayyaivaṃ mandatīvrādibhāvayā || 6-35 ||
1.1.d:
आत्मनो भूतिभेदास्ते सर्वज्ञाः सर्वतोमुखाः |
भगवच्छक्तिमय्यैवं मन्दतीव्रादिभावया || 6-35 ||
1.1.m:
Those souls, variations of becoming, are omniscient and facing everywhere;
thus, by [Śakti] consisting of Bhagavān's power, possessing states such as mild and intense, // 6-35

whose nature imitates the respective awakening and closing of Sudarśana,
they are pierced on all sides by ignorance consisting of affliction, and brought under control. // 6-36
The fourfold nature of those whose intrinsic nature is concealed

1.1.s:
brahmakṣatrādibhāvena cātūrūpyaṃ vrajanti te |
brāhmaṇāḥ kṣatriyā vaiśyāḥ śūdrā iti vibhedataḥ || 6-37 ||
1.1.d:
ब्रह्मक्षत्रादिभावेन चातूरूप्यं व्रजन्ति ते |
ब्राह्मणाः क्षत्रिया वैश्याः शूद्रा इति विभेदतः || 6-37 ||
1.1.m:
They attain a fourfold state in the manner of brāhmaṇa, kṣatriya, and so forth,
through the division into brāhmaṇas, kṣatriyas, vaiśyas, and śūdras. // 6-37

1.1.s: p. 55) ātmāno jīvasaṃjñāste bandhamokṣau vrajanti te |
1.1.d: प्. 55) आत्मानो जीवसंज्ञास्ते बन्धमोक्षौ व्रजन्ति ते |
1.1.m: Those souls, designated as living beings, undergo bondage and liberation.
Their descent to earth due to subjection to karma
The aggregates of them are declared as immoveable beings called Manus; // 6-38

1.1.s:
kleśāśayāparāmṛṣṭāḥ sarvajñāḥ sarvatomukhāḥ |
nityasiddhā hi bhūtyaṃśāste proktā bhagavanmayāḥ || 6-39 ||
1.1.d:
क्लेशाशयापरामृष्टाः सर्वज्ञाः सर्वतोमुखाः |
नित्यसिद्धा हि भूत्यंशास्ते प्रोक्ता भगवन्मयाः || 6-39 ||
1.1.m:
untouched by afflictions and karmic deposits, omniscient, facing everywhere,
eternally perfected portions of becoming, they are declared to consist of Bhagavān. // 6-39

1.1.s:
āvirbhāvatirobhāvaiḥ svasminnātmani nārada |
ātmano vartayantaste vaiṣṇavā ādhikārikāḥ || 6-40 ||
1.1.d:
आविर्भावतिरोभावैः स्वस्मिन्नात्मनि नारद |
आत्मनो वर्तयन्तस्ते वैष्णवा आधिकारिकाः || 6-40 ||
1.1.m:
By manifestations and disappearances in their own self, O Nārada,
maintaining the souls, they are Vaiṣṇava cosmic officials. // 6-40

1.1.s:
viṣṇoḥ saṃkalparūpeṇa sthitvāsmin pauruṣe pade |
yogenāvatarantyaṃśaiḥ sthānāt sthānaṃ dharāvadhi || 6-41 ||
1.1.d:
विष्णोः संकल्परूपेण स्थित्वास्मिन् पौरुषे पदे |
योगेनावतरन्त्यंशैः स्थानात् स्थानं धरावधि || 6-41 ||
1.1.m:
Remaining in this realm of Puruṣa in the form of Viṣṇu's will,
by yoga they descend with parts from place to place down to the earth. // 6-41
The descending ones becoming creators of offspring

1.1.s:
sṛṣṭāyāṃ karmabhūmau te mithunībhūya mānavān |
catuḥśataṃ sṛjantyete bhūyo mānavamānavān || 6-42 ||
1.1.d:
सृष्टायां कर्मभूमौ ते मिथुनीभूय मानवान् |
चतुःशतं सृजन्त्येते भूयो मानवमानवान् || 6-42 ||
1.1.m:
When the field of action is created, pairing up, they create
four hundred human beings, and then further human beings from human beings; // 6-42
and all of them are boundless; their expansion will be described there.
The origination of Śakti from Aniruddha
In a lower realm from that Puruṣa who is indeed four-yoked, // 6-43
Śakti is emitted from Aniruddha, impelled by his Sudarśana.
The descent of the immoveable Manus into Śakti
Now, when Śakti is emitted, O great sage, the eight Manus, // 6-44

1.1.s:
p. 56) avatīrya svakāt sthānādviṣṇusaṃkalpacoditāḥ |
tiṣṭhanti kalalībhūtāstasmiñśaktimaye pade || 6-45 ||
1.1.d:
प्. 56) अवतीर्य स्वकात् स्थानाद्विष्णुसंकल्पचोदिताः |
तिष्ठन्ति कललीभूतास्तस्मिञ्शक्तिमये पदे || 6-45 ||
1.1.m:
having descended from their own place, impelled by Viṣṇu's will,
remain blended together in that realm consisting of Śakti. // 6-45

1.1.s: kālo nāma guṇo nāma tasyā garbhasthitaṃ dvayam |
1.1.d: कालो नाम गुणो नाम तस्या गर्भस्थितं द्वयम् |
1.1.m: A pair, namely Time and Quality, resides in her womb.
The origination of Destiny from Śakti
The subtle controller of all, called Destiny, of Time, // 6-46
arises first from Śakti, impelled by Viṣṇu's will.
The Manus descend here, impelled by Sudarśana. // 6-47

1.1.s:
yasya syādyādṛśaṃ rūpaṃ yatkaraṃ yatsvabhāvakam |
sudarśanaprabhāvasthaṃ tattanniyamabhāvitam || 6-48 ||
1.1.d:
यस्य स्याद्यादृशं रूपं यत्करं यत्स्वभावकम् |
सुदर्शनप्रभावस्थं तत्तन्नियमभावितम् || 6-48 ||
1.1.m:
Whatever form, whatever function, and whatever nature one may have,
staying in the power of Sudarśana, that is produced by that Destiny. // 6-48
The origination of Time from Destiny

1.1.s:
kālasya pāvanaṃ rūpaṃ yattu tatkalanātmakam |
udeti niyateḥ so'tha kālaḥ saṃkalpacoditaḥ || 6-49 ||
1.1.d:
कालस्य पावनं रूपं यत्तु तत्कलनात्मकम् |
उदेति नियतेः सोऽथ कालः संकल्पचोदितः || 6-49 ||
1.1.m:
That purifying form of Time which consists of reckoning,
that Time then arises from Destiny, impelled by [Viṣṇu's] will. // 6-49

1.1.s:
niyatermanavo'pyatra kāle hyavataranti te |
kālaḥ sa kalayatyeko viṣṇusaṃkalpacoditaḥ || 6-50 ||
1.1.d:
नियतेर्मनवोऽप्यत्र काले ह्यवतरन्ति ते |
कालः स कलयत्येको विष्णुसंकल्पचोदितः || 6-50 ||
1.1.m:
The Manus too descend from Destiny here into Time;
that singular Time reckons, impelled by Viṣṇu's will. // 6-50
It drives everything to be driven, just as a current [carries away] the river bank.
The successive origination of the nature consisting of qualities from Time
That form consisting of qualities belonging to Śakti which was spoken of earlier, // 6-51
that qualitative body is manifested by degrees from Time.
First the origination of goodness therein
Therein, goodness, light, clear, in the form of a quality, free from disease, // 6-52
is first manifested from Time; from this the Manus descend.
Its presiding by the form of Viṣṇu belonging to Aniruddha
Then the form belonging to Aniruddha, impelled by its own will, // 6-53
presides over that goodness, bearing the very name of Viṣṇu.

1.1.s: tata eva tasya sukharūpatvaṃ svacchatvaṃ ca | sattvādraja-utpattiḥ
1.1.d: तत एव तस्य सुखरूपत्वं स्वच्छत्वं च | सत्त्वाद्रज-उत्पत्तिः
1.1.m: Hence its nature as pleasure and clarity; the origination of passion from goodness
This whole [goodness] was clear, pleasurable, and unperturbed. // 6-54

The goodness containing the Manus within, containing the insentient quality within, O sage,
was presided over by Viṣṇu; from that, impelled by Viṣṇu's will, // 6-55
the quality called passion abundantly manifests from that goodness.
The Manus descend here from goodness, impelled by [Viṣṇu's] will. // 6-56
Its having the form of Brahmā presided over by Aniruddha
And the form of Brahmā, belonging to Aniruddha, presides over that quality.
Hence its nature as pain
This passion is unstable, painful, and constantly active. // 6-57
And then this entire universe, resting within, became agitated.
From that [passion] presided over by Brahmā, which contains the Manus within, O sage,
impelled by Viṣṇu's resolve, arose the quality named darkness.
The Manus descend into it, impelled by Sudarśana. // 6-59
Its having the form of Rudra presided over by Aniruddha
And the quality named Rudra, belonging to Aniruddha, presides over it.
Hence its nature as causing delusion and the like
Heavy, obstructing, constantly causing delusion, and inactive— // 6-60
that is called darkness by those who have crossed to the farther shore of the ocean of qualities.
Attainment of equilibrium of the triad of qualities in part
Here, by the resolve of Hari which consists of Sudarśana alone, // 6-61

1.1.s:
codyamāne'pi sṛṣṭyarthaṃ pūrṇaṃ guṇayugaṃ tadā |
aṃśataḥ sāmyamāyāti viṣṇusaṃkalpacoditam || 6-62 ||
1.1.d:
चोद्यमानेऽपि सृष्ट्यर्थं पूर्णं गुणयुगं तदा |
अंशतः साम्यमायाति विष्णुसंकल्पचोदितम् || 6-62 ||
1.1.m: even while being impelled for the sake of creation, the full pair of qualities then / attains equilibrium in part, impelled by the resolve of Viṣṇu. // 6-62
Its nature as Prakṛti itself
That darkness is celebrated by knowers of reality as the state of possessing the three qualities.
Synonyms of Prakṛti

"Equilibrium of the qualities," "ignorance," "inherent nature," "womb," "imperishable," / "wombless," and "womb of the qualities"—such terms designate the state of possessing the three qualities. // 6-63

1.1.s:
iti śrīpāñcarātre tantrarahasye ahirbudhnyasaṃhitāyāṃ
śuddhetarasṛṣṭivarṇanaṃ nāma ṣaṣṭho'dhyāyaḥ || 6 ||
1.1.d:
इति श्रीपाञ्चरात्रे तन्त्ररहस्ये अहिर्बुध्न्यसंहितायां
शुद्धेतरसृष्टिवर्णनं नाम षष्ठोऽध्यायः || 6 ||
1.1.m:
Thus ends the sixth chapter, named "Description of the Creation Other Than Pure," in the Ahirbudhnyasaṃhitā of the secret doctrine of the Pāñcarātra. // 6

The seventh chapter, named "Description of the Creation Other Than Pure"
The aggregate of Prakṛti, Puruṣa, and Time

1.1.s:
anyūnānatiriktaṃ yad guṇasāmyaṃ tamomayam |
tat sāṃkhyairjagato mūlaṃ prakṛtiśceti kathyate || 7-1 ||
1.1.d:
अन्यूनानतिरिक्तं यद् गुणसाम्यं तमोमयम् |
तत् सांख्यैर्जगतो मूलं प्रकृतिश्चेति कथ्यते || 7-1 ||
1.1.m: That equilibrium of the qualities, consisting of darkness, which is neither deficient nor redundant, / is called by the followers of Sāṃkhya the root of the universe and Prakṛti. // 7-1

1.1.s:
kramāvatīrṇo yastatra caturmanuyugaḥ pumān |
samaṣṭiḥ puruṣo yoniḥ sa kūṭastha itīryate || 7-2 ||
1.1.d:
क्रमावतीर्णो यस्तत्र चतुर्मनुयुगः पुमान् |
समष्टिः पुरुषो योनिः स कूटस्थ इतीर्यते || 7-2 ||
1.1.m: The Puruṣa who has descended into it in due order, possessing four yugas of Manus, / the aggregate, the Puruṣa, the source, is called the immoveable Puruṣa. // 7-2

1.1.s:
yat tat kālamayaṃ tattvaṃ jagataḥ saṃprakālanam |
sa tayoḥ kāryamāsthāya saṃyojakavibhājakaḥ || 7-3 ||
1.1.d:
यत् तत् कालमयं तत्त्वं जगतः संप्रकालनम् |
स तयोः कार्यमास्थाय संयोजकविभाजकः || 7-3 ||
1.1.m: That principle consisting of Time, which drives forth the universe, / adopting the function of those two, unites and divides [them]. // 7-3
The arising of the Intellect and the rest from this triad impelled by Bhagavān's resolve

1.1.s:
mṛtpiṇḍībhūtametattu kālāditritayaṃ mune |
viṣṇoḥ sudarśanenaiva svasvakāryapracoditam || 7-4 ||
1.1.d:
मृत्पिण्डीभूतमेतत्तु कालादित्रितयं मुने |
विष्णोः सुदर्शनेनैव स्वस्वकार्यप्रचोदितम् || 7-4 ||
1.1.m: This triad of Time and the rest, having become a lump of clay, O sage, / impelled to its respective function solely by the Sudarśana of Viṣṇu, // 7-4
produces the group of principles beginning with the Intellect and ending with earth.
Prakṛti is transformable by its essential nature and innate disposition
Among these, Prakṛti transforms like milk, clay, and the like. // 7-5
Puruṣa is untransformable by its essential nature
Puruṣa, being untransformable, is a cause by its mere proximity.
Time's role as the ripener of Prakṛti and Puruṣa

1.1.s: kālaḥ pacati tattve dve prakṛtiṃ puruṣaṃ ca ha || 7-6 ||
1.1.d: कालः पचति तत्त्वे द्वे प्रकृतिं पुरुषं च ह || 7-6 ||
1.1.m: Time indeed matures the two principles, Prakṛti and Puruṣa. // 7-6
The arising of the principle of the Intellect from Prakṛti
From that [state of] equilibrium of the qualities presided over by Puruṣa, impelled by Viṣṇu's resolve, / and reckoned by Time, O great sage, // 7-7
the Great one, namely the principle of the Intellect, arose from the Unmanifest, O sage.
"Knowledge," "Gaurī," "the earth," "Brāhmī," "bride," "growth," "mind," "honey," // 7-8
"non-apprehension," "sovereign," and "wise": these are words designating it, O sage.

1.1.s: kālo buddhistathā prāṇa iti tredhā sa gīyate || 7-9 ||
1.1.d: कालो बुद्धिस्तथा प्राण इति त्रेधा स गीयते || 7-9 ||
1.1.m: It is proclaimed to be threefold: Time, intellect, and vital breath. // 7-9
Through the division of darkness, goodness, and passion, designated by their respective awakenings, / Time consists of moments, lavas, and the like; intellect is endowed with determination; // 7-10
and the vital breath has the form of effort: such are the divisions of the Great [principle].
The fourfold nature of the luminous aspect there
By the designations "righteousness," "knowledge," "dispassion," and "sovereignty," // 7-11
the luminous form of the Great [principle] is divided into four.
The fourfold nature of the dark aspect as well
Unrighteousness, ignorance, lack of dispassion, and lack of sovereignty constitute the dark [aspect]. // 7-12
The presence of the Manus in the principle of the Intellect

1.1.s:
vidyāyā udare'ṣṭau te sudarśanasamīritāḥ |
manavo garbhatāṃ yānti sarvajñāḥ sarvadarśinaḥ || 7-13 ||
1.1.d:
विद्याया उदरेऽष्टौ ते सुदर्शनसमीरिताः |
मनवो गर्भतां यान्ति सर्वज्ञाः सर्वदर्शिनः || 7-13 ||
1.1.m: Impelled by Sudarśana, those eight omniscient and all-perceiving Manus / become embryos within the belly of Knowledge. // 7-13

1.1.s:
bodhanaṃ nāma vaidyaṃ tadindriyaṃ teṣu jāyate |
yenārthānadhyavasyeyuḥ sadasatpravibhāginaḥ || 7-14 ||
1.1.d:
बोधनं नाम वैद्यं तदिन्द्रियं तेषु जायते |
येनार्थानध्यवस्येयुः सदसत्प्रविभागिनः || 7-14 ||
1.1.m: That cognitive faculty named apprehension arises in them, / by which, discriminating the real and the unreal, they can determine objects. // 7-14
The arising of egoity from the Intellect

1.1.s:
vidyāyā udare tatrāhaṃkṛtirnāma jāyate |
saṃkalpāccoditā viṣṇoścoditāyāḥ sudarśanāt || 7-15 ||
1.1.d:
विद्याया उदरे तत्राहंकृतिर्नाम जायते |
संकल्पाच्चोदिता विष्णोश्चोदितायाः सुदर्शनात् || 7-15 ||
1.1.m: There, within the belly of Knowledge impelled by Sudarśana, / arises what is called the 'I'-maker, impelled by the resolve of Viṣṇu. // 7-15

1.1.s:
ahaṃkāro'bhimānaśca prajāpatirahaṃkṛtiḥ |
abhimantā ca boddhā cetyasyāḥ paryāyavācakāḥ || 7-16 ||
1.1.d:
अहंकारोऽभिमानश्च प्रजापतिरहंकृतिः |
अभिमन्ता च बोद्धा चेत्यस्याः पर्यायवाचकाः || 7-16 ||
1.1.m: "Egoity," "self-conceit," "lord of creatures," "'I'-maker," / "one who conceives oneself," and "one who knows": these are its synonyms. // 7-16
The threefold nature of egoity

1.1.s:
tasya vaikārikaṃ nāma rūpaṃ sāttvikamucyate |
taijasaṃ rājasaṃ rūpaṃ bhūtādirnāma tāmasam || 7-17 ||
1.1.d:
तस्य वैकारिकं नाम रूपं सात्त्विकमुच्यते |
तैजसं राजसं रूपं भूतादिर्नाम तामसम् || 7-17 ||
1.1.m: Its luminous form is called the transformational; / its passionate form is the fiery; and its dark form is named the origin of the elements. // 7-17
The different forms of egoity

1.1.s:
kāmaḥ krodhaśca lobhaśca mānaścāvamatistṛṣā |
ityahaṃkṛtirūpāṇi darśitāni mune tava || 7-18 ||
1.1.d:
कामः क्रोधश्च लोभश्च मानश्चावमतिस्तृषा |
इत्यहंकृतिरूपाणि दर्शितानि मुने तव || 7-18 ||
1.1.m:
Desire, anger, greed, / pride, disrespect, and craving:
these forms of egoity have thus been shown to you, O sage. // 7-18
The abiding of the Manus in egoity
When egoity arises, endowed with various powers, / that group of four Manus enters as an embryo within it. // 7-19
The arising of the mind from egoity

1.1.s:
sudarśaneritaṃ viṣṇorāhaṃkārikamindriyam |
mano nāma manūnāṃ tajjāyate cintanātmakam || 7-20 ||
1.1.d:
सुदर्शनेरितं विष्णोराहंकारिकमिन्द्रियम् |
मनो नाम मनूनां तज्जायते चिन्तनात्मकम् || 7-20 ||
1.1.m: Impelled by Viṣṇu's Sudarśana, the organ originating from egoity / called mind, whose nature is thought, arises for the Manus. // 7-20
Likewise, the embryo consisting of the Manus is endowed with mind and intellect.
The arising of the subtle element of sound from the origin of the elements
Then, from the dark origin of the elements, the subtle element of sound arises. // 7-21
And from the subtle element of sound arises ether, characterized by sound.
Ether has sound as its sole quality and provides space. // 7-22
Impelled by Viṣṇu's will, they enter as an embryo within it—

1.1.s: p. 64) manavo'ṣṭau mahābuddhe tadā vaikārikāt punaḥ || 7-23 ||
1.1.d: प्. 64) मनवोऽष्टौ महाबुद्धे तदा वैकारिकात् पुनः || 7-23 ||
1.1.m: the eight Manus, O one of great intellect. Then, from the transformational [egoity], // 7-23

1.1.s:
śrotraṃ vāgiti vijñānakarmendriyayugaṃ mune |
samīkṣayaiva devasya manuṣu pratijāyate || 7-24 ||
1.1.d:
श्रोत्रं वागिति विज्ञानकर्मेन्द्रिययुगं मुने |
समीक्षयैव देवस्य मनुषु प्रतिजायते || 7-24 ||
1.1.m: the pair consisting of the sensory faculty and the motor faculty, the ear and speech, O sage, / arises within the Manus through the mere glance of the God. // 7-24
The Manus' possession of these attributes
Then the embryo consisting of the Manus has hearing and speech.
The arising of the subtle element of touch
Impelled by Viṣṇu's Sudarśana, from the origin of the elements, the subtle element of touch [arises]. // 7-25
Wind, endowed with touch, arises, and from that also arises:

1.1.s: śoṣaṇaṃ preraṇaṃ ceṣṭā vyūhanaṃ ca samūhanam || 7-26 ||
1.1.d: शोषणं प्रेरणं चेष्टा व्यूहनं च समूहनम् || 7-26 ||
1.1.m: drying, propelling, motion, dispersion, and gathering together. // 7-26
These different activities arise from wind, O sage.
From the transformational egoity, O sage, the pair of skin and hands— // 7-27
the pair of sensory and motor faculties—arises by His will.
Then the person consisting of the Manus enters as an embryo within it. // 7-28
Their possession of skin and hands
Then moving, the embryo, impelled by Viṣṇu's will, / possessed the pair of skin and hands for the accomplishment of feeling, grasping, and so forth. // 7-29
The arising of the subtle element of form and fire

1.1.s:
tāmasādatha bhūtādeḥ sudarśanasamīritāt |
jāyate rūpamātraṃ tu jyotistasmācca rūpavat || 7-30 ||
1.1.d:
तामसादथ भूतादेः सुदर्शनसमीरितात् |
जायते रूपमात्रं तु ज्योतिस्तस्माच्च रूपवत् || 7-30 ||
1.1.m: Then, from the dark origin of the elements impelled by Sudarśana, / the subtle element of form arises, and from that, light possessing form. // 7-30

1.1.s:
rūpaṃ vyaktistathā pākaḥ kāntirdīptiritīdṛśāḥ |
jāyante taijasā bhedā bhedādvaikārikāt tathā || 7-31 ||
1.1.d:
रूपं व्यक्तिस्तथा पाकः कान्तिर्दीप्तिरितीदृशाः |
जायन्ते तैजसा भेदा भेदाद्वैकारिकात् तथा || 7-31 ||
1.1.m: Form, manifestation, cooking, lustre, radiance—such / fiery varieties arise; and likewise, from the differentiation of the transformational [egoity], // 7-31
The arising of eyes and feet
the pair of eyes and feet is born, impelled by Sudarśana, O sage.
The abiding of the Manus in fire
Impelled by Sudarśana, they enter as an embryo within it. // 7-32
Their possession of eyes and feet

1.1.s:
manavo rūpavantaste kāntidīptyādiśālinaḥ |
cakṣuṣmantaḥ pādavanto vīkṣaṇāṭanayoginaḥ || 7-33 ||
1.1.d:
मनवो रूपवन्तस्ते कान्तिदीप्त्यादिशालिनः |
चक्षुष्मन्तः पादवन्तो वीक्षणाटनयोगिनः || 7-33 ||
1.1.m: Those Manus possess form, endowed with lustre, radiance, and the like; / possessing eyes and feet, capable of seeing and moving about. // 7-33
The arising of the subtle element of taste and waters
Then, from the dark origin of the elements directed by Viṣṇu's gaze,

1.1.s: p. 66) jāyate rasamātraṃ tu jāyante'mbhāṃsi vai tataḥ || 7-34 ||
1.1.d: प्. 66) जायते रसमात्रं तु जायन्तेऽम्भांसि वै ततः || 7-34 ||
1.1.m: the subtle element of taste arises, and from that, indeed, the waters arise. // 7-34
Then their qualities arise: taste, unctuousness, liquidity, and so forth.
The arising of the faculties of tongue and genitals
Then, from that transformational [egoity], impelled by Viṣṇu's will, // 7-35
the tongue and the genitals arise, consisting of perception and action.
Impelled by Viṣṇu's will, they enter as an embryo within it— // 7-36
the Manus, O one of great intellect, who are authorized for Viṣṇu's work.
Their possession of tongue and genitals
Possessing sap, endowed with unctuousness, having fluids such as blood, // 7-37
possessing tongues, differentiated by male and female characteristics, they are born.
The arising of the subtle element of smell and earth
Then, from that origin of the elements impelled by Sudarśana, // 7-38
the subtle element of smell is born, [and] from that, the odorous earth.
Hardness, heaviness, stability, and so forth are qualities belonging to earth. // 7-39
Arising of the nose and the anus

1.1.s:
vaikārikādahaṃkārāt sudarśanasamīritāt |
ghrāṇaṃ pāyuriti dvandvaṃ jñānakarmātmakaṃ mune || 7-40 ||
1.1.d:
वैकारिकादहंकारात् सुदर्शनसमीरितात् |
घ्राणं पायुरिति द्वन्द्वं ज्ञानकर्मात्मकं मुने || 7-40 ||
1.1.m: From the transformational egoity impelled by Sudarśana, / the pair consisting of the nose and the anus, of the nature of sensation and action [respectively], O sage, // 7-40
State of the Manus in the earth
impelled by the will of Viṣṇu, they become embryos of the earth.
Their distinction of [possessing] nose and anus
Heavy, of solid composition, endowed with bones, teeth, and so forth, // 7-41
possessing noses, possessing anuses, with complete limbs, O sage.
Intention and zealous exertion, as well as the five kinds of vital breaths, // 7-42
are born indeed earlier from mind, egoity, and intellect.
Thus the fullness of all limbs of the Manus
Thus, with all limbs complete, endowed with the vital breaths prāṇa, apāna, and the rest, // 7-43
endowed with all faculties, the Manus [stand] there as embodied beings, O sage.
Equal duration of creation and dissolution
Whatever duration was described earlier at its cosmic dissolution, // 7-44

1.1.s:
p. 68) sarge sa eva vijñeyo vaiṣṇavaistattvacintakaiḥ |
vidyāvipariṇāmo'yaṃ saptadhā vīkṣayā hareḥ || 7-45 ||
1.1.d:
प्. 68) सर्गे स एव विज्ञेयो वैष्णवैस्तत्त्वचिन्तकैः |
विद्याविपरिणामोऽयं सप्तधा वीक्षया हरेः || 7-45 ||
1.1.m: that very same [duration] should be understood in creation by Vaiṣṇava thinkers on the principles. / This transformation of Vidyā occurs sevenfold through the glance of Hari. // 7-45
They declare those sevenfold divisions to be the gross elements, O sage.
The Manus also, impelled by Sudarśana, are divided // 7-46

1.1.s:
yugaśo yugaśaḥ pūrvaṃ paścāt puṃstrīvibhedataḥ |
svayamāgatavijñānāḥ sarvajñāḥ sarvadarśinaḥ || 7-47 ||
1.1.d:
युगशो युगशः पूर्वं पश्चात् पुंस्त्रीविभेदतः |
स्वयमागतविज्ञानाः सर्वज्ञाः सर्वदर्शिनः || 7-47 ||
1.1.m: into pairs, into pairs at first, and then according to the distinction of male and female. / Endowed with spontaneous discernment, omniscient, all-seeing, // 7-47
they then hold within themselves Aniruddha, the overseer and lord.
Production of embryos by the Manus
Possessing that overseer, therefore, impelled by his will, // 7-48
those Manus implant embryos by the hundreds in the women.
Their designations as brāhmaṇas and so forth
Brāhmaṇas, kṣatriyas, vaiśyas, and śūdras—of four kinds // 7-49
humans are born from the wives of the Manus, characterised by pairs.
Designation of those born from them as human-descendants of Manu and so forth

1.1.s: manubhiḥ saṃskṛtāste tu svāsu patnīṣu mānavāḥ || 7-50 ||
1.1.d: मनुभिः संस्कृतास्ते तु स्वासु पत्नीषु मानवाः || 7-50 ||
1.1.m: Consecrated by the Manus, those humans, in their own wives, // 7-50
beget many sons; these are the human-descendants of Manu.
Their performance of service to the Lord
Numerous are their lineages, by which all this [world] is pervaded; // 7-51
consisting of the four social classes, they perform service to the Lord.
Attainment of liberation for those who perform service to the Lord

1.1.s: teṣāṃ ye karma kurvanti sādhavaḥ śatavārṣikam || 7-52 ||
1.1.d: तेषां ये कर्म कुर्वन्ति साधवः शतवार्षिकम् || 7-52 ||
1.1.m: Among them, the virtuous who perform their duties for a hundred years, // 7-52
having attained discriminating knowledge, enter the supreme Hari.
Attainment of transmigratory existence for others
Those who, through the degeneration of the world-ages from the first age onwards, perform other deeds, // 7-53

1.1.s: phalābhidhyāyino yānti tatprasūtāṃ gatiṃ tu te |
1.1.d: फलाभिध्यायिनो यान्ति तत्प्रसूतां गतिं तु ते |
1.1.m: yearning for results, attain a destination brought about by those [deeds].
Creation of gods and others caused by karma

1.1.s: yā sā vidyā purā proktā manugarbhavatī mune || 7-54 ||
1.1.d: या सा विद्या पुरा प्रोक्ता मनुगर्भवती मुने || 7-54 ||
1.1.m: That Vidyā who was previously described as having the Manus as her embryos, O sage, // 7-54

1.1.s:
garbhavatyeva sā devān nānāguṇavibheditān |
daityadānavarakṣāṃsi gandharvoragakiṃnarān || 7-55 ||
1.1.d:
गर्भवत्येव सा देवान् नानागुणविभेदितान् |
दैत्यदानवरक्षांसि गन्धर्वोरगकिंनरान् || 7-55 ||
1.1.m: being pregnant, [gives birth to] the gods differentiated by various qualities, / Daityas, Dānavas, Rakṣases, Gandharvas, Uragas, and Kiṃnaras. // 7-55

1.1.s:
iti nānāvidhā yonīrviṣṇoḥ saṃkalpacoditā |
svasaṃkalpena sṛjati te cānyāṃste'pi cāparān || 7-56 ||
1.1.d:
इति नानाविधा योनीर्विष्णोः संकल्पचोदिता |
स्वसंकल्पेन सृजति ते चान्यांस्तेऽपि चापरान् || 7-56 ||
1.1.m: Thus, impelled by the will of Viṣṇu, she creates manifold wombs / by her own will; and they create others, and those create yet others. // 7-56
